4-0006-0000.sourceText: Une information pour les membres: notre collègue Branko Grims n’est plus membre du groupe PPE et siège dorénavant parmi les députés non inscrits, à compter d’aujourd’hui 9 juillet 2026.
4-0006-0000.englishText: Information for members: our colleague Branko Grims is no longer a member of the EPP group and is now sitting among the non-attached members, effective today, July 9, 2026.

4-0008-0000.sourceText:
L’ordre du jour appelle le débat sur la question avec demande de réponse orale adressée à la Commission sur la communication conjointe sur l’aide humanitaire, posée par Barry Andrews et Leire Pajín, au nom de la commission du développement (O-000026/2026 – B10-0013/26) (2026/2734(RSP)).

Je tiens à rappeler aux intervenants que, compte tenu des mesures de test actuellement en place et de leurs impératifs de fin du débat, il sera nécessaire de respecter strictement les temps de parole.

Pour ouvrir notre discussion, je donne la parole à notre collègue Pajín de la commission du développement.
4-0008-0000.englishText:
The next item is the debate on the question for oral answer to the Commission on the joint communication on humanitarian aid, tabled by Barry Andrews and Leire Pajín, on behalf of the Committee on Development (O-000026/2026 – B10-0013/26) (2026/2734(RSP)).

I would like to remind speakers that, given the testing measures currently in place and their end-of-debate requirements, it will be necessary to strictly adhere to speaking times.

To open our discussion, I give the floor to our colleague Pajín from the Committee on Development.

4-0009-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora comisaria, las razones para esta Comunicación y para hacer de la ayuda humanitaria una prioridad para la Unión Europea son muchas.

Esta Comunicación llega en un momento particularmente difícil —el más difícil, seguramente, que hemos vivido en los últimos tiempos— para la ayuda humanitaria. En el año 2026, 239 millones de personas necesitarán asistencia humanitaria, pero, al mismo tiempo, el sistema humanitario mundial prevé llegar solo a 135 millones; es decir, cuando más necesario es un sistema humanitario robusto y fuerte, menos recursos disponibles tenemos, menos voluntad política existe, hay más violación del sistema humanitario internacional.

En este tiempo hemos visto de todo: hemos visto asesinar deliberadamente a trabajadores humanitarios, hemos visto violar el Derecho humanitario internacional una y otra vez, e incluso hemos visto utilizar la ayuda humanitaria como un arma de guerra.

Hay otras cifras que deberían hacernos reflexionar a todos los que estamos aquí. El llamamiento humanitario hiperpriorizado de las Naciones Unidas para 2026 asciende a 33 000 millones de dólares. Poco más del 1 % del gasto militar mundial de un solo año bastaría para financiar todo ese llamamiento. Dicho de otra manera, poco más de cuatro días servirían de gasto mundial para cubrir ese llamamiento.

Hago esa analogía para entender, de una vez por todas, que trabajar por un mundo en paz, en equilibrio con los derechos humanos, es también trabajar por la mejor garantía de seguridad, la forma más inteligente de ejercer influencia y una mayor seguridad para todos y todas.

Señora comisaria, le quiero agradecer su trabajo. La dirección de la Comunicación es tremendamente positiva, pero la verdadera prueba será la aplicación, un plan de seguimiento, supervisión y un intercambio continuo con el Parlamento y con el sector.

Sobre el primer pilar —proteger—, ese es el corazón de la acción humanitaria y creo que eso es lo que debemos fortalecer. Vivimos tiempos muy oscuros para el Derecho internacional humanitario. En el año 1997, 39 trabajadores humanitarios fueron asesinados. En los últimos tres años, casi mil trabajadores humanitarios han muerto o han sido asesinados mientras cumplían su misión humanitaria de salvar vidas. Son testigos incómodos de genocidios y también son quienes acaban con la coartada de la impunidad de quienes la ejercen.

¿Cuándo y cómo hemos llegado a normalizar esto, como diría nuestro amigo y jefe de OCHA, Tom Fletcher? Por eso, damos todo el apoyo a los trabajadores humanitarios, como la iniciativa «Protect Aid Workers», que debería ser permanente y adecuadamente financiada.

La Unión Europea debe ser muy clara: la ayuda humanitaria no puede ser instrumentalizada, politizada ni utilizada para apoyar agendas militares u otros objetivos no humanitarios.

Como usted sabe bien, señora comisaria, la diplomacia humanitaria es una de las áreas de esta Comunicación con un potencial considerable, si se aplica bien. La diplomacia humanitaria debe ser una herramienta práctica, útil, eficaz. La Unión Europea necesita personal formado que sepa hacer diplomacia humanitaria con la información adecuada, el nivel adecuado y respetando siempre los principios humanitarios.

Señorías, sobre el segundo pilar —actuar—, apoyamos la ambición de hacer que la ayuda humanitaria sea más eficaz, más flexible y centrada en las personas. También apoyamos el objetivo de hacer más eficientes las cadenas de suministros humanitarios, donde se concentra una parte importante de los costes de la ayuda humanitaria. Pero las ganancias de la eficiencia deben volver a la respuesta sobre el terreno, no traducirse en una reducción del nivel global de asistencia.

La localización de la ayuda humanitaria también es esencial. El compromiso de canalizar el 25 % de la financiación humanitaria, de la forma más directa posible hacia los actores locales de aquí a 2027, es muy positivo, pero tenemos que ser conscientes de que, para ello, tenemos que fortalecer las capacidades de los actores locales, que no siempre están garantizadas. Esto no se puede limitar tampoco a un objetivo numérico.

Sobre el tercer pilar —asociarse—, acogemos positivamente el enfoque específico de la fragilidad, una demanda histórica del Parlamento y de los sectores humanitarios y de desarrollo. La Unión Europea debe trabajar mejor entre la acción humanitaria, el desarrollo y la paz. En contextos frágiles, no existe un modelo único aplicable a todos los casos, debemos adaptarlo en cada uno de los contextos. La Unión Europea debe utilizar análisis de conflicto, adaptar los programas a cada contexto y dar flexibilidad a las delegaciones de la Unión Europea cuando las situaciones se deterioren rápidamente.

Todos los actores tienen un papel que desempeñar en contextos frágiles y, dependiendo del contexto, hay que adaptarlos, pero todos los actores deben integrarse en un enfoque adaptado a cada situación. A nivel de la Comisión, esto significa que todos los servicios pertinentes deben tener un papel claro en la aplicación de esta estrategia para contextos frágiles.

Señora comisaria, la diplomacia humanitaria es absolutamente esencial: desplegar todas las capacidades para garantizar corredores humanitarios, para garantizar que el esfuerzo humanitario llega de verdad, es absolutamente importante. Por eso, nosotros hoy, que hemos construido un consenso en esta Comunicación que esperemos que se vea traducido en la votación, queremos trabajar para que esta Comunicación se implemente y, por eso, quiero preguntarle hoy cuál es el plan y los primeros pasos para que, cuanto antes, esto sea una realidad, porque la credibilidad humanitaria de Europa no se juzgará por sus compromisos, sino por sus resultados y también por la coherencia de otros departamentos de la Comisión.
4-0009-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, the reasons for this Communication and for making humanitarian aid a priority for the European Union are many.

This Communication comes at a particularly difficult time—surely the most difficult we have experienced in recent times—for humanitarian aid. In the year 2026, 239 million people will need humanitarian assistance, but, at the same time, the global humanitarian system expects to reach only 135 million; in other words, just when a robust and strong humanitarian system is most necessary, we have fewer resources available, there is less political will, and there is more violation of the international humanitarian system.

During this time we have seen everything: we have seen humanitarian workers deliberately murdered, we have seen international humanitarian law violated over and over again, and we have even seen humanitarian aid used as a weapon of war.

There are other figures that should make all of us here reflect. The United Nations hyper-prioritised humanitarian appeal for 2026 amounts to 33 billion dollars. A little over 1% of a single year's global military spending would be enough to finance that entire appeal. Put another way, just over four days of global spending would be enough to cover that appeal.

I make that analogy to understand, once and for all, that working for a world at peace, in equilibrium with human rights, is also working for the best guarantee of security, the most intelligent way to exercise influence, and greater security for everyone.

Madam Commissioner, I want to thank you for your work. The direction of the Communication is tremendously positive, but the real test will be implementation, a monitoring and supervision plan, and continuous exchange with Parliament and the sector.

On the first pillar—to protect—that is the heart of humanitarian action and I believe that is what we must strengthen. We are living through very dark times for international humanitarian law. In 1997, 39 humanitarian workers were killed. In the last three years, almost a thousand humanitarian workers have died or been killed while carrying out their humanitarian mission to save lives. They are uncomfortable witnesses to genocides and they are also the ones who put an end to the alibi of impunity of those who commit them.

When and how did we come to normalise this, as our friend and head of OCHA, Tom Fletcher, would say? Therefore, we give our full support to humanitarian workers, such as the "Protect Aid Workers" initiative, which should be permanent and adequately funded.

The European Union must be very clear: humanitarian aid cannot be instrumentalised, politicised, or used to support military agendas or other non-humanitarian objectives.

As you well know, Madam Commissioner, humanitarian diplomacy is one of the areas of this Communication with considerable potential, if applied well. Humanitarian diplomacy must be a practical, useful, effective tool. The European Union needs trained staff who know how to do humanitarian diplomacy with the right information, the right level, and always respecting humanitarian principles.

Members, on the second pillar—to act—we support the ambition to make humanitarian aid more effective, more flexible, and people-centred. We also support the objective of making humanitarian supply chains more efficient, where a significant part of the costs of humanitarian aid is concentrated. But efficiency gains must return to the response on the ground, not translate into a reduction in the overall level of assistance.

The localization of humanitarian aid is also essential. The commitment to channel 25% of humanitarian funding, as directly as possible, to local actors by 2027 is very positive, but we must be aware that, to achieve this, we must strengthen the capacities of local actors, which are not always guaranteed. Nor can this be limited to a numerical target.

On the third pillar—to partner—we warmly welcome the specific approach to fragility, a historical demand of Parliament and of the humanitarian and development sectors. The European Union must work better between humanitarian action, development, and peace. In fragile contexts, there is no single model applicable to all cases; we must adapt it to each context. The European Union must use conflict analysis, adapt programmes to each context, and give flexibility to European Union delegations when situations deteriorate rapidly.

All actors have a role to play in fragile contexts and, depending on the context, they must be adapted, but all actors must be integrated into an approach tailored to each situation. At the Commission level, this means that all relevant services must have a clear role in the implementation of this strategy for fragile contexts.

Madam Commissioner, humanitarian diplomacy is absolutely essential: deploying all capabilities to guarantee humanitarian corridors, to guarantee that the humanitarian effort truly arrives, is extremely important. Therefore, today, having built a consensus on this Communication that we hope will be reflected in the vote, we want to work so that this Communication is implemented, and therefore, I want to ask you today what the plan and the first steps are to make this a reality as soon as possible, because Europe's humanitarian credibility will not be judged by its commitments, but by its results and also by the coherence of other Commission departments.

4-0010-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, honourable Members, the joint communication on humanitarian action comes at a critical moment of unprecedented challenges – unprecedented in terms of the number and severity of global crises and the ever-expanding humanitarian funding gap; unprecedented in terms of systematic attacks on international humanitarian law, civilians and humanitarian workers, with deliberate attacks on civilians, destruction of schools and hospitals, widespread sexual violence and weaponisation of humanitarian access.

This is also why our new humanitarian communication is also unprecedented. It is, for the first time ever, a joint communication presented together with the HR/VP. It is a joint effort of our humanitarian, development, peace and foreign policy. It is not about mixing up what is humanitarian aid, what is development cooperation and what is foreign policy. Nor is it shifting away from our long-standing and firm commitment to humanitarian aid principles like humanity, impartiality, neutrality and independence. These will always remain our non-negotiable compass, where it is better using all of our tools and policies in complementarity for a better impact.

We have outlined three pillars: protect, perform and partner. Protect our humanitarian principles, defending international humanitarian law; protect aid workers and civilians, securing humanitarian access and developing a strategic approach to humanitarian diplomacy.

Today, 300 million people's lives depend on humanitarian aid while we are reaching the lowest level of funding in decades. To save more lives, we need to perform. This is our second pillar: improving the efficiency of humanitarian aid, avoiding duplication, reforming supply chains, delivering our aid closer to those in need through localisation.

And finally, we need to work in a more sustainable manner, addressing protracted crises and their root causes. That is why we need our third pillar: partner. Partner with the private sector, the international financial institutions, the philanthropic sector to find new blended finance, encourage and secure investments in fragile countries, strengthening the humanitarian development peace nexus and increasing global resilience.

This joint communication is our comprehensive answer to the challenges of today. And I hope I can count on your support for bringing this important work from policy strategy to achievements on the ground.

4-0011-0000.sourceText:
Madam President. Commissioner, you're the first commissioner in this House who has kept within the speaking time. You were even briefer and said a lot while doing that. I'm really impressed by that, and that's a big contribution to parliamentarism.

Dear colleagues, the European Union is the strongest soft power on earth, and we have to remain in that role because we contribute to a better life for many people, to rescuing people from difficult situations and to giving life to what we call European values. But it is also important that people know we do that, and we should speak about it, because the world is full of confrontation, of actors who seek to use their hard power – not always for the best (in very many cases, for the worst). Europe is developing its hard power, but we have to strengthen our soft power and keep our soft power also as a leverage – not only for pure European interests, which is also good and fine and for the sake of the Europeans, but for the universal approach with European values.

So communication on humanitarian aid is important. To include all stakeholders is important. To respect the very traditions and the culture of the countries and the societies we deal with is extremely important. Might there be a coordination with religious leaders or respecting the values of a given country when we go there to help?

So Europe, as a strong soft power, also has to set an example all over the world, for an evidence‑based approach, especially – and I time and again repeat that – when it comes to health. There are already, like in the pandemic, conspiracy theories about health crises on our planet, such as Ebola, such as the hantavirus. Again, extremists try to misuse these health issues for their purpose of division, of separation, of polarisation, far away from any evidence‑based approach.

This is where the European Union comes in again. We are not only the strongest soft power. We are not only values‑based. We are also more reliable than any other actor on earth when it comes to evidence. And when we talk about communication and humanitarian aid, of course you must never forget that we are dealing with taxpayers' money, meaning we have to explain, time and again, and also show our responsibility, time and again, towards the citizens of the European Union, Member States, the European Union citizens, what we are doing with their money and that it is worth it – that it is worth it for the people affected by the crisis, but it is also worth it for the European interest, European values and the proper future for everybody. Because Europeans will have a better future when everybody has a better future.

4-0012-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Hunderte von Millionen Menschen in akuter Not, so viele zur Flucht gezwungen wie noch nie. Frau Kommissarin, Sie haben die volle Unterstützung dieses Hauses für Ihre engagierte Arbeit.

Jeder Ebola-Ausbruch, den wir nicht im Keim ersticken, wird auf uns zurückkommen. Jeder Hunger, der nicht gestillt wird, wird sich irgendwann in Gewalt ausdrücken, und jeder Krieg, der nicht verhindert wird und der nicht, wenn er nicht verhindert werden kann, dann wenigstens schnell beendet wird, wird in unendlichem Elend geflüchteter Menschen münden.

Wir müssen handeln, die Mittel zur Verfügung stellen – ja, Sie machen das richtig, indem Sie die Effektivität erhöhen, Mittel vor Ort verausgaben, aber wir brauchen das ganze Arsenal: keine Handelsverträge mit denen, die Blut an den Händen haben; keine diplomatischen Verrenkungen gegenüber denjenigen, die Kriege befeuern. Das erwarten wir von der Kommission und von den Mitgliedstaaten.
4-0012-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear colleagues! Hundreds of millions of people in acute distress, more forced to flee than ever before. Madam Commissioner, you have the full support of this House for your dedicated work.

Every Ebola outbreak that we do not nip in the bud will come back to us. Every hunger that is not satisfied will at some point express itself in violence, and every war that is not prevented and, if it cannot be prevented, then at least quickly ended, will result in infinite misery for displaced people.

We must act, provide the funds – yes, you are doing the right thing by increasing effectiveness, spending funds locally, but we need the entire arsenal: no trade agreements with those who have blood on their hands; no diplomatic contortions towards those who fuel wars. We expect this from the Commission and from the Member States.

4-0013-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, I try to follow the wise words of my colleagues, but in my mother tongue, Hungarian.

Tisztelt Biztos Asszony! Tisztelt Elnök Úr! Ha az Európai Unió valamilyen sikert tud felmutatni a világban az elmúlt évtizedekben, az akkor tényleg a humanitárius segítségnyújtás, aminek célja – itt, ahogy már említették – az emberi szenvedés enyhítése. Különösen igaz ez most, amikor Gázában kétmillió ember nem jut egészségügyi ellátáshoz és oktatáshoz. Amikor Szudánban a világ legnagyobb menekültválsága közepette 14 millió ember kényszerült elhagyni otthonát, amikor Jemenben 20 millió ember függ a nemzetközi élelmiszersegélyektől. Világszerte 90 millió gyermek maradt ki az oktatásból a fegyveres konfliktus miatt. Egyszerű a kérdés: mi lesz velük? Az egységes fellépés most minden eddiginél fontosabb. Ennek alapja, ahogy itt elhangzott: az emberiesség, a pártatlanság, a semlegesség és természetesen a függetlenség.

Tisztelt Képviselőtársaim! Itt az Európai Parlamentben már megkezdődött a verseny a következő évi pénzügyi keret forrásaiért. Egyelőre eddig soha nem látott módon sajnos meghatározhatatlan, hogy valóban mekkora összeg fog rendelkezésre állni a humanitárius segítségnyújtásra, és miként kerül az főleg elosztásra. Valóban a bajba jutottak szenvedésének enyhítésére használja ezt a Bizottság, vagy más politikai szándékot akar finanszírozni? Furcsa kimondani – és vigyázok is vele –, a szenvedők kárára. Sajnos meg kell állapítanunk azt is, hogy az utóbbi időben a humanitárius politika összekeveredik az ideológiai törekvésekkel. Ez bizony rossz irány. A humanitárius segítségnyújtás portfólióját nem szabad más területekkel összekeverni.

Tisztelt Képviselőtársaim! A következő hónapok feladata biztosítani: az Unió humanitárius fellépése megfelelő költségvetéssel valóban hiteles és független, az eddigieknél – nagyon remélem – hatékonyabban tudja a szükséget szenvedőket segíteni.
4-0013-0000.englishText:
Mr President, I try to follow the wise words of my colleagues, but in my mother tongue, Hungarian.

Dear Madam Commissioner, dear Mr President! If the European Union has been able to show any success in the world in recent decades, it is truly humanitarian aid, the aim of which is—as mentioned here—to alleviate human suffering. This is especially true now, when two million people in Gaza have no access to healthcare and education. When in Sudan, amidst the world's largest refugee crisis, 14 million people have been forced to leave their homes, when in Yemen 20 million people depend on international food aid. Worldwide, 90 million children have dropped out of school because of armed conflict. The question is simple: what will happen to them? Unified action is now more important than ever. The basis of this, as has been said here, is: humanity, impartiality, neutrality and, of course, independence.

Dear fellow Members! Here in the European Parliament, the race for the resources of the financial framework for the next year has already begun. For now, in a way never seen before, it is unfortunately undetermined what amount will actually be available for humanitarian aid and how it will be distributed. Is the Commission really using this to alleviate the suffering of those in trouble, or does it want to finance another political intention? It is strange to say—and I am careful with it—at the expense of the sufferers. Unfortunately, we also have to state that recently humanitarian policy is being mixed with ideological endeavors. This is certainly a bad direction. The portfolio of humanitarian aid must not be mixed with other areas.

Dear fellow Members! The task of the coming months is to ensure: with an appropriate budget, the Union's humanitarian action is truly credible and independent, and can help those in need more effectively than before—I very much hope so.

4-0015-0000.sourceText:
Herr talman! Kommissionens yttrande pekar på att det globala biståndssystemet står inför en kollaps. Det är ju allvarligt, men samtidigt tycker jag vi måste titta på vad har vi från Europa gjort?

Sverige har under 25 år fyrdubblat sin biståndsbudget och Europeiska unionen har fördubblat i ännu många fler gånger under de här 25 åren. Ändå är världen i det läget som det är. Då måste man fråga sig om man har misslyckats? Om man pumpar in allt mer pengar och man får allt sämre resultat, då är det ju någonting som inte riktigt stämmer. Jag tror att det är ett feltänk som ligger i grunden här.

Europa kan inte rädda världen. Det är ett kolonialt, förlegat tänkande. Vi kan inte göra det, utan vi måste se till att vi blir starka i stället. Vi som folkvalda representerar människorna i unionen och vi har väldigt många stora problem att ta hand om här, socialt och ekonomiskt. Det finns ingen anledning att öka budgeten. Den borde i stället minska.
4-0015-0000.englishText:
Mr. President! The Commission's opinion points out that the global aid system is facing a collapse. That is serious, but at the same time I think we must look at what we from Europe have done?

Sweden has quadrupled its aid budget over 25 years and the European Union has doubled it many times over during these 25 years. Still, the world is in the state that it is in. Then one must ask oneself if one has failed? If you pump in more and more money and you get worse and worse results, then something is not quite right. I think there is a flawed way of thinking at the root of this.

Europe cannot save the world. It is a colonial, outdated way of thinking. We cannot do that, but we must ensure that we become strong instead. We as democratically elected officials represent the people in the union and we have a very large number of major problems to take care of here, socially and economically. There is no reason to increase the budget. It should instead decrease.

4-0016-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, le marqueur de l’aide humanitaire, c’est l’irréductibilité de la dignité humaine. Le consensus européen pour l’aide humanitaire nous le rappelle. Mais, entre-temps, la rage destructrice de MAGA est passée par là. Elle menace tout sur son passage.

La politique européenne humanitaire, quant à elle, elle résiste – disons qu’elle résiste encore. Elle résiste parce qu’elle est impartiale. L’impartialité, cela veut dire qu’on assiste celui qui est dans le besoin. On n’assiste pas celui qui nous plaît, on assiste celui qui a besoin de notre aide et sans laquelle il ne pourrait pas survivre. Elle résiste encore à l’aspect transactionnel, qui semble envahir tous les secteurs – des pans entiers de la politique européenne –, y compris la politique d’aide au développement. Et cette politique, elle a un visage: c’est le visage de notre commissaire. Elle mérite notre soutien parce qu’elle défend ce que l’Union européenne, dans sa politique extérieure, a de plus noble. Elle et les valeurs qu’elle défend représentent le marqueur de cette politique de l’aide humanitaire, dont nous devons préserver le caractère.

J’invite toute cette assemblée à résister à la tentation de voter l’amendement 15, qui entend mettre fin, de façon très sournoise, à ce caractère impartial et désintéressé de la politique d’aide humanitaire.
4-0016-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the marker of humanitarian aid is the irreducibility of human dignity. The European consensus on humanitarian aid reminds us of this. But in the meantime, MAGA's destructive rage has passed this way. It threatens everything in its path.

European humanitarian policy, for its part, resists – let's say it still resists. It resists because it is impartial. Impartiality means assisting those in need. We do not assist the one we like, we assist the one who needs our help and without whom they could not survive. It still resists the transactional aspect, which seems to invade all sectors – whole swathes of European policy – including development aid policy. And this policy has a face: it is the face of our Commissioner. She deserves our support because she defends what is most noble about the European Union in its foreign policy. She and the values she defends represent the marker of this humanitarian aid policy, the character of which we must preserve.

I invite this entire assembly to resist the temptation to vote for amendment 15, which aims to put an end, in a very insidious way, to this impartial and selfless character of humanitarian aid policy.

4-0017-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident! Im Gazastreifen leiden nach wie vor über 2 Millionen Menschen unter wenig Zugang zu Wasser, zu Strom und zur Grundversorgung; über 1 Million Menschen leben dort in Zelten. Und wir haben auch viele andere Krisen in dieser Welt, wie zum Beispiel im Sudan, wo wir knapp 20 Millionen Menschen haben, die unter Hungersnot leiden. Insgesamt sind über 230 Millionen Menschen – das muss man sich einmal ausmalen! – abhängig von humanitärer Hilfe, weil sie unter Bedingungen leben, die wir alle uns gar nicht vorstellen können.

Und wir diskutieren jetzt zurzeit hier im Europäischen Parlament, aber auch an anderen Orten darüber, wie die globalen Instrumente der Europäischen Union in der Zukunft aussehen sollen. Ich will ganz deutlich sagen, dass das, was der Rat, was die Mitgliedstaaten machen, nämlich Kürzungen in diesem Bereich vorzuschlagen, der absolut falsche Weg ist. Wir haben nicht nur eine Verpflichtung anderen Regionen gegenüber, sondern wir haben auch ein Interesse, dass wir auch weiterhin starke humanitäre Hilfe haben werden, und deshalb ist es wichtig, dass wir uns dafür einsetzen, dass ein Teil des Budgets auch weiter für humanitäre Hilfe reserviert sein wird.
4-0017-0000.englishText:
Mr President! In the Gaza Strip, more than 2 million people continue to suffer from poor access to water, electricity, and basic supplies; over 1 million people live there in tents. And we also have many other crises in this world, such as in Sudan, where we have almost 20 million people suffering from famine. Overall, over 230 million people – just imagine that! – depend on humanitarian aid because they live under conditions that none of us can even imagine.

And we are currently discussing here in the European Parliament, but also in other places, what the global instruments of the European Union should look like in the future. I want to say very clearly that what the Council, what the Member States are doing, namely proposing cuts in this area, is the completely wrong approach. We not only have an obligation towards other regions, but we also have an interest in continuing to have strong humanitarian aid, and therefore it is important that we campaign to ensure that part of the budget continues to be reserved for humanitarian aid.

4-0018-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora comisaria, 22 millones de personas van a perder la vida de aquí a 2030, 5 millones de ellos serán niños. Es la consecuencia de los recortes de la ayuda humanitaria.

Cuando la llegada de comida, de agua o de medicamentos pasa a depender de la voluntad de un Gobierno, la ayuda humanitaria se convierte en una herramienta de chantaje político, en un privilegio y no en un derecho; un instrumento para que unos pocos decidan quién vive con dignidad y quién sobrevive esperando un convoy, mirando si llega agua o si llega pan ese día. Lo vemos en Gaza, donde la ayuda humanitaria sigue sin entrar y el hambre se utiliza como un arma de guerra más para continuar con el genocidio. Lo vemos en Cuba, donde los Estados Unidos están asfixiando a todo un pueblo y ni tan siquiera hay posibilidad de hacer llegar la ayuda por un bloqueo criminal. Y también lo vemos allí donde han desmantelado las ayudas de USAID, como en los campos de refugiados saharauis en el Sáhara Occidental, que llevan 50 años resistiendo.

La Unión Europea, comisaria, debe reforzar la ayuda humanitaria y cubrir el vacío que Trump vilmente ha dejado de cubrir si no queremos ser cómplices de estos atentados contra la humanidad.
4-0018-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, 22 million people are going to lose their lives between now and 2030, 5 million of them will be children. This is the consequence of cuts to humanitarian aid.

When the arrival of food, water or medicine depends on the will of a government, humanitarian aid becomes a tool for political blackmail, a privilege and not a right; an instrument for a few to decide who lives with dignity and who survives waiting for a convoy, watching to see if water or bread arrives that day. We see it in Gaza, where humanitarian aid is still not getting in and hunger is used as yet another weapon of war to continue the genocide. We see it in Cuba, where the United States is suffocating an entire people and there is not even the possibility of getting aid through due to a criminal blockade. And we also see it wherever USAID aid has been dismantled, such as in the Sahrawi refugee camps in Western Sahara, which have been resisting for 50 years.

The European Union, Commissioner, must reinforce humanitarian aid and fill the void that Trump has vilely left unfilled if we do not want to be accomplices to these attacks against humanity.

4-0019-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin, meine Damen und Herren! Je weniger realen Einfluss die EU weltweit hat, desto mehr inszeniert sie sich als moralische Großmacht. Nichts gegen Hilfe in akuten Notlagen und den Schutz humanitären Personals, aber Ihre Entschließung will aus humanitärer Politik ein dauerhaftes, milliardenschweres Instrument mit eigener Umsetzungsarchitektur und ausufernden politischen Verpflichtungen machen.

Es ist immer dasselbe Muster: Die Grünen fordern im Bundestag 3 Milliarden Euro zusätzlich, aber solange in Deutschland Brücken marode sind, Krankenhäuser Personalnot leiden und Rentner Pfandflaschen sammeln müssen, ist ein solcher Einsatz einfach unangemessen.

Und was passiert denn mit dem Geld? Im Jemen hat die GIZ jahrelang deutsche Hilfsgelder veruntreut – fingierte Rechnungen, bandenmäßiger Betrug, zweistelliger Millionenschaden. Das ist das System, das hier weiter verfestigt werden soll: die Finanzierung von NGOs und oftmals korrupten Regimen, ohne dass wir in Europa etwas davon haben.

Und wo unsere Hilfe in der Welt gute Resultate zeigt, da sind es oft andere, die davon profitieren. China betreibt seine Entwicklungspolitik streng geostrategisch und ausschließlich zum eigenen Nutzen. Wenn Europa nicht der nützliche Idiot sein will, der für Chinas Investitionen das Feld bereitet, dann muss dieser Weltrettungsanspruch aufhören.

Humanitäre Hilfe – ja, aber bedarfsorientiert und streng kontrolliert. Sie darf nicht isoliert von der sonstigen Entwicklungspolitik betrachtet werden. Wir brauchen Konditionalität: Wer unsere Mittel will, muss bei der Bekämpfung zum Beispiel von illegaler Migration kooperieren. Der Blankoscheck für globale NGOs und endlose Transfers, den die linke Hälfte dieses Hauses bis hinein in die EVP hier fordert, das ist der Ausverkauf europäischer Interessen, und daher lehnen wir diesen Entschließungsantrag ab.
4-0019-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen! The less real influence the EU has worldwide, the more it presents itself as a moral superpower. Nothing against aid in acute emergencies and the protection of humanitarian personnel, but your resolution wants to turn humanitarian policy into a permanent, multi-billion instrument with its own implementation architecture and sprawling political commitments.

It is always the same pattern: the Greens demand an additional 3 billion euros in the Bundestag, but as long as bridges in Germany are dilapidated, hospitals suffer from a shortage of staff and pensioners have to collect returnable bottles, such a deployment is simply inappropriate.

And what happens to the money? In Yemen, GIZ embezzled German aid money for years - forged invoices, gang fraud, double-digit million damage. This is the system that is to be further cemented here: the financing of NGOs and often corrupt regimes without us in Europe getting anything out of it.

And where our aid shows good results in the world, it is often others who benefit from it. China pursues its development policy strictly geostrategically and exclusively for its own benefit. If Europe does not want to be the useful idiot who prepares the field for China's investments, then this world-salvation claim must stop.
Z
Humanitarian aid - yes, but needs-based and strictly controlled. It must not be viewed in isolation from other development policy. We need conditionality: whoever wants our funds must cooperate in combating illegal migration, for example. The blank cheque for global NGOs and endless transfers demanded here by the left half of this House up to the EPP, that is the sell-out of European interests, and therefore we reject this motion for a resolution.

4-0020-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, liebe Frau Kommissarin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Humanitäre Hilfe ist Ausdruck unserer europäischen Werte. Sie rettet Leben, sie lindert Leid, und sie muss diejenigen erreichen, die sie am dringendsten brauchen.

Aber gerade deshalb dürfen wir auch nicht naiv sein; humanitäre Hilfe ist niemals völlig unpolitisch. Nach einer Naturkatastrophe mag das noch am ehesten so sein, aber allein die Frage, wer überhaupt humanitäre Hilfe bekommt in Kriegen und insbesondere in Bürgerkriegen – hier gibt es immer auch eine politische Dimension. Wer Zugang bekommt, wer verteilt, wer kontrolliert, und wer profitiert – all das kann das Kräfteverhältnis vor Ort beeinflussen. Umso mehr, wenn humanitäre Hilfe nicht nur vorübergehend, sondern dauerhaft oder gar zur alleinigen Lebensquelle wird.

Das gilt auch mit Blick auf Gaza und die West Bank. Hilfe muss die Zivilbevölkerung erreichen, aber sie darf nicht dazu beitragen, terroristische Organisationen, gewaltsame Akteure oder korrupte Strukturen zu stabilisieren. Oder sie sollte, wie beispielsweise im Fall Afghanistan, mit ortsangepassten Auflagen verbunden werden, die zumindest zu einer graduellen Verbesserung der Situation der Unterdrückten führen.

Wenn Hilfsgüter umgeleitet werden, wenn Gelder in falsche Hände geraten oder wenn internationale Organisationen nicht ausreichend kontrollieren, entsteht ein massiver Vertrauensverlust bei den Bürgern Europas, aber auch in der internationalen Gemeinschaft. Neutralität darf nicht Blindheit bedeuten; Unparteilichkeit heißt nicht Kontrollverzicht, und Menschlichkeit verlangt gerade, dass Hilfe nicht missbraucht wird.

Deshalb brauchen wir von der Kommission klare Antworten darauf, ob humanitäre Hilfe ankommt, welche Prüfmechanismen es bei den Partnerorganisationen gibt, und wie bei Zweckentfremdung reagiert wird. Europa muss helfen, aber auch kontrollieren.
4-0020-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear Commissioner, dear colleagues! Humanitarian aid is an expression of our European values. It saves lives, it relieves suffering, and it must reach those who need it most.

But precisely for that reason, we must not be naive either; humanitarian aid is never completely apolitical. After a natural disaster, that may be the case most of all, but the mere question of who actually receives humanitarian aid in wars, and particularly in civil wars – here there is always a political dimension as well. Who gets access, who distributes, who controls, and who profits – all of this can influence the balance of power on the ground. All the more so when humanitarian aid is not just temporary, but becomes permanent or even the sole source of livelihood.

This also applies with a view to Gaza and the West Bank. Aid must reach the civilian population, but it must not contribute to stabilizing terrorist organizations, violent actors, or corrupt structures. Or it should, as for example in the case of Afghanistan, be linked to conditions adapted to the local context that at least lead to a gradual improvement in the situation of the oppressed.

If relief supplies are diverted, if funds end up in the wrong hands, or if international organizations do not exercise sufficient control, a massive loss of trust arises among the citizens of Europe, but also in the international community. Neutrality must not mean blindness; impartiality does not mean renunciation of control, and humanity precisely demands that aid is not abused.

Therefore, we need clear answers from the Commission on whether humanitarian aid is arriving, what auditing mechanisms exist with partner organizations, and how misuse is responded to. Europe must help, but also control.

4-0021-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, humanitaire hulp moet abrupte noodsituaties verlichten, maar veel van de situaties die nu om onze hulp vragen, zijn helemaal niet abrupt.

We weten dat het stopzetten van ontwikkelingsprogramma's voor gezondheidszorg leidt tot uitbraken van voorkoombare ziektes. We weten dat het indirect steunen van illegale mijnbouw gemeenschappen ontwricht en ontheemt. We weten dat het voortzetten van handelsdeals met een staat die genocide pleegt, ongekend menselijk lijden veroorzaakt.

Humanitaire hulp staat niet los van onze internationale partnerschappen en mag geen vervanging zijn voor een consistent buitenlandbeleid. Want als we met de ene hand omstandigheden blijven creëren die tot crises leiden en met de andere hand hulp bieden, lossen we niets op.

Het internationale systeem is stuk en dat kost miljoenen mensenlevens. Wanneer 300 miljoen mensen humanitaire hulp nodig hebben, vraagt dat om meer dan incidentele steun. Het vraagt om een manier van handelen die geen schade meer toebrengt aan mens en natuur.

Daarom wil ik aan de commissaris vragen hoe zij samen met haar collega's werkt aan een daadwerkelijk consistent buitenlandbeleid.
4-0021-0000.englishText:
Mr President, humanitarian aid should alleviate abrupt emergencies, but many of the situations now calling for our help are not abrupt at all.

We know that stopping development programs for healthcare leads to outbreaks of preventable diseases. We know that indirectly supporting illegal mining disrupts and displaces communities. We know that continuing trade deals with a state that commits genocide causes unprecedented human suffering.

Humanitarian aid is not separate from our international partnerships and must not be a substitute for a consistent foreign policy. Because if we continue with one hand to create circumstances that lead to crises and with the other hand offer aid, we solve nothing.

The international system is broken, and that costs millions of human lives. When 300 million people need humanitarian aid, it demands more than incidental support. It demands a way of acting that no longer causes harm to people and nature.

Therefore, I would like to ask the Commissioner how she is working with her colleagues on a genuinely consistent foreign policy.

4-0022-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, Senhora Comissária, na «Eneida», Virgílio lembra-nos que o sofrimento dos mortais interpela a consciência dos homens.

Perante a dor humana, a Europa não pode virar o rosto. A nossa ajuda deve continuar a proteger os mais vulneráveis e aqueles que arriscam a vida para os socorrer.

Mas Eneias ensina-nos também que a verdadeira compaixão exige responsabilidade.

Hoje, há mais trabalhadores humanitários mortos, mais fome, e o financiamento ao desenvolvimento regressou a níveis de há uma década.

Perante esta realidade, a resposta da Comissão chega demasiadas vezes tarde e, frequentemente, acompanhada da mesma chaga: a ineficiência.

A verdade, por mais incómoda, é esta: gastar mais não é ajudar melhor. Com centenas de milhões de pessoas a necessitar de assistência, cada euro perdido em burocracia, opacidade ou dispersão é um euro subtraído a quem dele mais precisa.

Porque a lição de Eneias permanece atual: a compaixão honra uma civilização, mas só a responsabilidade garante que ela perdure.
4-0022-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, in the Aeneid, Virgil reminds us that the suffering of mortals appeals to the conscience of men.

Faced with human pain, Europe cannot turn its face away. Our aid must continue to protect the most vulnerable and those who risk their lives to rescue them.

But Aeneas also teaches us that true compassion requires responsibility.

Today, there are more dead humanitarian workers, more hunger, and development funding has regressed to levels from a decade ago.

Faced with this reality, the Commission's response too often arrives late and, frequently, accompanied by the same scourge: inefficiency.

The truth, however uncomfortable, is this: spending more is not helping better. With hundreds of millions of people in need of assistance, every euro lost in bureaucracy, opacity or dispersion is a euro taken away from those who need it most.

Because Aeneas's lesson remains current: compassion honors a civilization, but only responsibility ensures that it endures.

4-0023-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, the fact that we are able to help each other in difficult times by providing humanitarian aid is the highest expression of humanity. It often becomes a factor uniting countries when political disagreements are put aside.

Unfortunately, the need for such aid is not decreasing, but is only growing as conflict zones expand. One of such countries is Ukraine, which is fighting Russian aggression. A significant part of its society is facing extreme difficulties, and humanitarian aid support must be continued.

However, humanitarian aid and funds must be allocated extremely responsibly so that they are not used to solve problems but to create them. They must not fall into the hands of terrorists and create opportunities for using those funds for aggression against neighbours. Some finance mechanisms may discredit humanitarian goals, like in the cases when the money went into the hands of Hamas terrorists. Therefore, the EU should act extremely cautiously and responsibly in the future.

4-0024-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, let me first start with thanking you, dear Commissioner Lahbib, for your principled leadership and commitment to international humanitarian law. The humanitarian communication is a testimony of this leadership.

Three hundred million people need humanitarian aid. Behind every number, there is a face, there are dreams, hopes, aspiration. There is a life that is uprooted and destroyed. It is the women in Sudan who walk through the desert in search for help. They are raped, they are beaten, they are witnessing massacres, only to find that there was no one to help. It is the children in Gaza who survived the war, but their parents and communities did not. Many of them are disabled and all of them traumatised. These are the voices that are never heard in this Chamber. They are never invited. Still, it is their need and experiences that must shape our acts.

My plea today is clear. Please, dear Commissioner, we need to urgently increase the funding to those – especially women-led organisations – who are the first responders when the catastrophe happens.

4-0025-0000.sourceText:
Herr talman! Tyvärr ökar antalet krig och konflikter i världen just nu, och samtidigt sker någonting som är ännu mer skrämmande. Respekten för den humanitära rätten urholkas, och helt oskyldiga barn och människor som är utsatta för de här konflikterna drabbas. Vi ser små barn i Gaza som försöker skapa en vardag bland rasmassor och försöker sova i läger som invaderas av råttor.

Samtidigt ser vi hur hjälpen har hindrats från att komma fram. Vi ser också attacker på sjukvårdspersonal, sjukhus och hjälparbetare. När humanitär hjälp används som ett verktyg för kontroll, när tillgången till bistånd villkoras av politiska eller militära mål, då hotas inte bara människorna i den aktuella konflikten. Då hotas hela det internationella system som skapades efter andra världskrigets fasor.

Accepterar vi det, då är vi på ett sluttande plan. Vi i denna kammare måste stå upp för internationell rätt, att den gäller alltid och för alla. Vi måste försvara FN:s roll, skydda humanitära organisationers möjlighet att verka och kräva att livräddande hjälp når fram till de oskyldiga människor som behöver den. Annars är vi alla i fara.
4-0025-0000.englishText:
Mr. President! Unfortunately, the number of wars and conflicts in the world is increasing right now, and at the same time, something even more frightening is happening. Respect for international humanitarian law is being eroded, and completely innocent children and people exposed to these conflicts are suffering. We see small children in Gaza trying to create a daily life among the rubble and trying to sleep in camps invaded by rats.

At the same time, we see how aid has been prevented from getting through. We also see attacks on medical personnel, hospitals, and aid workers. When humanitarian aid is used as a tool for control, when access to aid is made conditional on political or military goals, not only are the people in the current conflict threatened. Then the entire international system that was created after the horrors of the Second World War is threatened.

If we accept that, then we are on a slippery slope. We in this chamber must stand up for international law, that it applies always and to everyone. We must defend the UN's role, protect the ability of humanitarian organizations to operate, and demand that life-saving aid reaches the innocent people who need it. Otherwise, we are all in danger.

4-0026-0000.sourceText:
Gerbiamas Pirmininke, komisare, kolegos. Humanitarinė pagalba nėra labdara, tai strateginė investicija į Europos saugumą ir patikimumą. Šiandien pasaulyje vyksta apie 130 aktyvių konfliktų ir jie sugeneruoja maždaug 70 proc. pasaulinių humanitarinių poreikių. Poreikiai auga eksponentiškai, o finansiniai ištekliai ir veiklos galimybės mažėja. Tačiau juk akivaizdus ir poreikis reformuoti sistemą: mažinti dubliavimąsi tiekimo grandinėse ir reikalauti, kad finansavimas pasiektų žmones. Europos Sąjungos humanitarinės pagalbos kokybė, atskaitomybė ir strateginė orientacija lygiai tiek pat svarbi, kaip ir jos apimtis. Pastaraisiais metais smurtas prieš humanitarinius darbuotojus pasiekė precedento neturintį mastą. Žmonės, kurie rizikuoja savo gyvybe padėdami kitiems, patys tampa taikiniais. Tarptautinė humanitarinė teisė pažeidinėjama beveik nebaudžiamai. Turime reikalauti atsakomybės už išpuolius prieš pagalbos ir medicinos darbuotojus. Kartu turime suvokti, koks svarbus yra vietos veikėjų vaidmuo: jie visada yra pirmieji krizės atveju dar prieš atvykstant tarptautinėms organizacijoms. Veiklos rezultatai priklauso ir nuo veiksnių, kurių Europa negali kontroliuoti: mažėjančio donorų skaičiaus ar konflikto šalių nepagarbos humanitarinei teisei. Tačiau tai ne pretekstas pasyvumui, o paskata atkakliai išnaudoti kiekvieną mums prieinamą galimybę.

(Kalbėtojas sutiko atsakyti į mėlynosios kortelės klausimą)
4-0026-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues. Humanitarian aid is not charity, it is a strategic investment in European security and credibility. Today there are about 130 active conflicts in the world and they generate roughly 70 percent of global humanitarian needs. Needs are growing exponentially, while financial resources and operational capacities are decreasing. However, the need to reform the system is also obvious: to reduce duplication in supply chains and to demand that funding reaches the people. The quality, accountability and strategic orientation of the European Union's humanitarian aid are just as important as its scale. In recent years, violence against humanitarian workers has reached an unprecedented scale. People who risk their lives to help others are themselves becoming targets. International humanitarian law is being violated with near impunity. We must demand accountability for attacks on aid and medical workers. At the same time, we must realize how important the role of local actors is: they are always the first on the scene in a crisis even before international organizations arrive. Operational results also depend on factors that Europe cannot control: a decreasing number of donors or the disrespect of conflict parties for humanitarian law. However, this is not an excuse for passivity, but an incentive to persistently exploit every opportunity available to us.

(The speaker agreed to reply to a blue-card question)

4-0027-0000.sourceText:
Usted ha hablado de ayuda humanitaria. ¿Sabe que la Comisión se niega a publicar los informes de la destrucción de los proyectos humanitarios en Gaza, porque dice que perjudica sus relaciones internacionales? A mí me parece una expresión clara de la hipocresía europea, porque, con una mano, se financian proyectos allí y, con la otra, se financia a quien los destruye, se le da armas para destruir esos proyectos y para asesinar a las víctimas palestinas.

Yo quería saber su opinión, si está de acuerdo en negar el acceso a la información de la ciudadanía europea respecto a esos informes.
4-0027-0000.englishText:
You spoke about humanitarian aid. Do you know that the Commission refuses to publish the reports on the destruction of humanitarian projects in Gaza, because it says it harms its international relations? To me, it seems like a clear expression of European hypocrisy, because, with one hand, projects are financed there and, with the other hand, whoever destroys them is financed, they are given weapons to destroy those projects and to murder Palestinian victims.

I wanted to know your opinion, if you agree to deny European citizens access to information regarding those reports.

4-0028-0000.sourceText: Atsiprašau, man sudėtinga buvo suprasti klausimą. Bandysiu atsakyti kažkiek tai. Turbūt kalba čia eina apie informavimą ir informavimo srautus? Taigi tas atgalinis ryšys turi būti užprogramuotas ir kiekviena investicija, kokia ji bebūtų, į humanitarinę pagalbą privalo būti tinkamu būdu įvertinta ir diktuoti tam tikrus tolesnius veiksmus. Taip suprasčiau Jūsų klausimą.
4-0028-0000.englishText: I apologize, it was difficult for me to understand the question. I will try to answer somewhat. Is the talk here probably about information and information flows? So that feedback must be programmed and every investment, whatever it may be, in humanitarian aid must be properly evaluated and dictate certain further actions. That is how I would understand your question.

4-0029-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, l'aiuto umanitario non è merce di scambio, è dovere, dovere di intrecciare il filo che tiene in vita e riconosce dignità agli esseri umani quando tutto è in macerie.

Eppure, oggi, vicino e lontano dalla nostra Europa, quel filo viene spezzato sistematicamente. Organizzazioni osteggiate e definanziate, operatori uccisi, azioni interrotte, attori locali messi ai margini, comunità private di cibo, cure e riparo.

Il diritto internazionale umanitario è fatto a pezzi da chi sta in pace, formalmente, e da chi fa guerra. E se avviene in guerra non è una giustificazione, ma un'aggravante.

I più colpiti sono donne, minori e minoranze. Difendiamo con Lei, signora Commissaria, l'umanità e la generosa sostanza, sostenibilità e libertà del soccorso. Opponiamoci a chi vuole trasformare l'aiuto in brutale strumento di pressione politica e ribadiamo che il finanziamento pubblico è obbligo, non opzione.

Perciò, agli Stati membri e alle destre diciamo: nessun taglio.
4-0029-0000.englishText:
Mr President, honourable colleagues, humanitarian aid is not a bargaining chip, it is a duty, the duty to weave the thread that keeps human beings alive and recognises their dignity when everything is in ruins.

Yet today, near and far from our Europe, that thread is being systematically broken. Organisations opposed and defunded, aid workers killed, operations interrupted, local actors sidelined, communities deprived of food, medical care and shelter.

International humanitarian law is being torn to pieces by those who are formally at peace and by those who wage war. And if it happens in war, it is not a justification, but an aggravating factor.

The most affected are women, minors and minorities. With you, Madam Commissioner, let us defend humanity and the generous substance, sustainability and freedom of relief work. Let us oppose those who want to turn aid into a brutal instrument of political pressure and let us reiterate that public funding is an obligation, not an option.

Therefore, to the Member States and the right wing, we say: no cuts.

4-0030-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, mis primeras palabras son de apoyo y solidaridad por el terremoto en Venezuela. Este Parlamento no ha tenido la valentía de hablar de ese tema. Lo siento mucho, realmente, cuando se habla muchas veces de otras temáticas.

La ayuda humanitaria es un compromiso civilizatorio por el impacto de conflictos o desastres humanitarios. Es una obligación internacional, es compromiso, es empatía, es humanidad y solidaridad. Por eso también quiero agradecerle a la comisaria el trabajo en este sentido, porque creo que es la única comisaria valiente en haber denunciado el genocidio en Gaza y lo quiero reconocer públicamente.

Apoyamos esta Comunicación conjunta sobre la ayuda humanitaria delante del aumento de conflictos, delante de la falta del respeto del Derecho internacional, delante de la falta de apoyo a las organizaciones de derechos humanos y humanitarias. Gaza ha sido el ejemplo de dejar solos a los trabajadores humanitarios, de dejar solos a los palestinos. Gaza ha sido el ejemplo de la muerte de la ayuda humanitaria y, por eso, tenemos que seguir ayudando. Esa es una de las...

(el presidente retira la palabra a la oradora)
4-0030-0000.englishText:
Mr President, my first words are of support and solidarity for the earthquake in Venezuela. This Parliament has not had the courage to speak about that issue. I am very sorry, truly, when other topics are so often discussed.

Humanitarian aid is a civilisational commitment due to the impact of conflicts or humanitarian disasters. It is an international obligation, it is a commitment, it is empathy, it is humanity and solidarity. That is why I also want to thank the Commissioner for her work in this regard, because I believe she is the only brave Commissioner to have denounced the genocide in Gaza, and I want to acknowledge it publicly.

We support this Joint Communication on humanitarian aid in the face of the increase in conflicts, the lack of respect for international law, and the lack of support for human rights and humanitarian organisations. Gaza has been the example of leaving humanitarian workers alone, of leaving Palestinians alone. Gaza has been the example of the death of humanitarian aid, and therefore, we must continue helping. That is one of the...

(the President cuts off the speaker's microphone)

4-0031-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, parler de l’aide humanitaire, c’est avant tout parler de vies humaines. C’est parler de milliers de personnes qui, faute de moyens, n’ont tout simplement plus accès à une aide essentielle. En 2025, le financement international de l’aide humanitaire a atteint son niveau le plus bas depuis dix ans: une situation qui oblige les acteurs humanitaires à prendre des décisions impossibles – décider qui recevra une aide et qui en sera privé, qui sera soigné, qui mangera, qui sera protégé.

Ces choix ne devraient pas exister. C’est une question de volonté politique. Défendre des financements ambitieux, prévisibles et flexibles, refuser l’instrumentalisation de l’aide, assurer les principes de neutralité, d’impartialité et d’indépendance, protéger les travailleurs humanitaires, prendre en charge leur santé mentale et garantir leur accès à la justice: ces priorités doivent se traduire en actions concrètes, urgemment. Il s’agit de dignité humaine et de la vie de milliers de personnes.
4-0031-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, talking about humanitarian aid is above all talking about human lives. It is talking about thousands of people who, for lack of resources, simply no longer have access to essential aid. In 2025, international funding for humanitarian aid has reached its lowest level in ten years: a situation which forces humanitarian actors to make impossible decisions – deciding who will receive aid and who will be deprived of it, who will be treated, who will eat, who will be protected.

These choices should not exist. It is a matter of political will. Defending ambitious, predictable and flexible funding, refusing the instrumentalization of aid, ensuring the principles of neutrality, impartiality and independence, protecting humanitarian workers, taking care of their mental health and guaranteeing their access to justice: these priorities must be translated into concrete actions, urgently. This is a matter of human dignity and the lives of thousands of people.

4-0032-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora comisaria, ayer Israel asesinó a diez civiles, dos menores. Antes de ayer, asesinó al jefe de la agencia egipcia de ayuda humanitaria. Ya son casi 600 los trabajadores humanitarios asesinados en Gaza. Paremos de mandarle armas a Israel.

Hoy aquí estamos hablando de cómo hacer llegar ayuda humanitaria a muchos sitios y, entre otros lugares, a Gaza. Pero nuestra prioridad debería ser dejar de cooperar con Israel en el exterminio de ese pueblo, del pueblo palestino, en el que nosotros participamos.

Antes se lo preguntaba a un diputado del Partido Popular. La Comisión se niega a publicar los informes sobre la destrucción de sus propios proyectos, los proyectos que financia. Eso, para mí, es la expresión más clara de la hipocresía europea. Igual que se niega a cumplir con las resoluciones judiciales de los tribunales de justicia.

Creo que lo de la ayuda humanitaria parece una estrategia de marketing. Puede parecerlo para ocultar nuestra participación en ese genocidio.
4-0032-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, yesterday Israel murdered ten civilians, two of them minors. The day before yesterday, it murdered the head of the Egyptian humanitarian aid agency. Nearly 600 humanitarian workers have now been murdered in Gaza. Let's stop sending weapons to Israel.

Today here we are talking about how to get humanitarian aid to many places and, among other places, to Gaza. But our priority should be to stop cooperating with Israel in the extermination of that people, of the Palestinian people, in which we participate.

Earlier I was asking a member of the Partido Popular about this. The Commission refuses to publish reports on the destruction of its own projects, the projects it funds. That, to me, is the clearest expression of European hypocrisy. Just as it refuses to comply with judicial rulings from courts of justice.

I think that the humanitarian aid thing looks like a marketing strategy. It may look like it to hide our participation in that genocide.

4-0034-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, en el desorden global y en la multiplicación de las catástrofes naturales debidas en buena parte al calentamiento global, es más urgente que nunca la ayuda humanitaria.

Nunca ha habido más necesidades de ayuda humanitaria, ni tan urgentes, como en este momento en que estamos hablando. Y, sin embargo, la Unión Europea, que es campeona del mundo en ayuda al desarrollo y ayuda humanitaria, tiene la obligación de mejorar la eficacia diplomática de su ayuda humanitaria. Este es el objeto de esta pregunta oral: mejorar el nivel de protección, el compromiso con el Derecho internacional humanitario y el rendimiento de la ayuda humanitaria, de modo que toda esa inversión en ayuda se traduzca en transformación y en cambio real en los receptores de la ayuda.

Y, por supuesto, también hay que poner un acento especial en valores distintivos que deben vincular la política exterior y también la ayuda humanitaria de la Unión Europea: el empoderamiento de las mujeres, derechos sexuales y reproductivos y el apoyo a los trabajadores humanitarios acosados como nunca y sometidos a violencia en buena parte de los países necesitados de ayuda.
4-0034-0000.englishText:
Mr President, amidst global disorder and the multiplication of natural catastrophes largely due to global warming, humanitarian aid is more urgent than ever.

Never has there been a greater need for humanitarian aid, nor such urgent need, as at this moment while we are speaking. And yet, the European Union, which is the world champion in development aid and humanitarian aid, has the obligation to improve the diplomatic effectiveness of its humanitarian aid. This is the purpose of this oral question: to improve the level of protection, commitment to international humanitarian law, and the performance of humanitarian aid, so that all this investment in aid translates into transformation and real change in the recipients of the aid.

And, of course, special emphasis must also be placed on distinctive values that should link the foreign policy and also the humanitarian aid of the European Union: the empowerment of women, sexual and reproductive rights, and support for humanitarian workers who are harassed as never before and subjected to violence in a large part of the countries in need of aid.

4-0035-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, a government's first moral contract is to its own citizens. Making its own citizens' lives better, safer and more prosperous comes before everything else. It doesn't mean we can't do things like give humanitarian aid; of course we can, and we should. But pouring inefficient development aid around the world is another question.

European aid should serve European interests. We are not a charity and we don't have limitless piles of money to sink into agencies and NGOs that someone here finds worth supporting. So we must be strategic: focus on true life‑saving aid without ideological creep.

Funding leftist ideas and NGOs through development aid serves only leftist interests. Saving lives serves everyone's interests.

4-0037-0000.sourceText:
Merci, Monsieur le Président, et merci, chers parlementaires, pour ce débat plein d’humanité et de cœur. J’aimerais commencer par une des phrases qui a été dite. Un des premiers intervenants a dit que l’Union européenne et l’aide humanitaire étaient:

'The strongest soft power on earth.'

Cela m’a poussée à une réflexion, parce que j’ai essayé de le traduire en français. Est-ce qu’alléger les souffrances de femmes, d’enfants, déplacés par des tremblements de terre, par des guerres, par des épidémies, est-ce que c’est un pouvoir léger – soft power? Est-ce qu’arrêter des épidémies avant qu’elles ne contaminent d’autres pays, avant qu’elles ne se répandent, qu’elles ne nous atteignent, qu’elles ne nous propulsent dans de cauchemardesques blackouts, comme on en a eus par le passé, c’est un soft power? Est-ce que c’est léger? Je ne pense pas.

Alors, certes, l’aide humanitaire à elle seule ne peut pas tout résoudre, et c’est pour cela que nous avons publié cette communication humanitaire, qui est plus une stratégie, en réalité, face aux défis auxquels on fait face aujourd’hui. Pour qu’elle soit efficace, il faut qu’elle travaille main dans la main avec la diplomatie, avec l’aide au développement, pour avoir une vision à long terme. C’est pour cela aussi que nous avons proposé pour le prochain CFP d’avoir Global Europe avec un coussin de 25 milliards et des principes qui seront protégés, puisque les réglementations de 1996 propres à l’aide humanitaire resteront d’application.

Alors, est-ce que cet argent sera bien dépensé? C’est aussi une question qu’on peut, bien sûr, se poser. Il n’y a pas zéro risque, mais en tout cas nous avons zéro tolérance et un système de contrôle solide en place, avec un suivi de nos propres bureaux ECHO qui sont sur place, qui sont en contact avec nos partenaires qui distribuent l’aide humanitaire, avec des audits de la Cour des comptes européenne, avec des rapports circonstanciés. Donc oui, tout est en place pour que l’argent de nos citoyens soit bien dépensé.

L’aide humanitaire – je suis d’accord –, c’est la face la plus noble, la plus digne de l’Union européenne, et si on devait lui donner un visage, ce serait certainement celui d’une femme. Une femme au Soudan qui fuit la guerre, qui est déplacée parmi les 13 millions de déplacés, ou une femme qui cherche son enfant enseveli à Caracas. C’est ça, l’aide humanitaire. C’est ce que je vois, c’est ce à quoi je suis confrontée à chaque fois que je me déplace en mission. C’est l’espoir, c’est une vision d’avenir pour nous tous, et nous devons en être fiers, le maintenir en vie.

Je compte sur vous, je vous remercie et je vous souhaite un bon vote tout à l’heure pour votre résolution.
4-0037-0000.englishText:
Thank you, Mr President, and thank you, dear parliamentarians, for this debate full of humanity and heart. I would like to start with one of the sentences that was said. One of the first speakers said that the European Union and humanitarian aid were:

'The strongest soft power on earth.'

This led me to reflect, because I tried to translate it into French. Is easing the suffering of women, of children, displaced by earthquakes, by wars, by epidemics, is that a light power – soft power? Is stopping epidemics before they contaminate other countries, before they spread, before they reach us, before they propel us into nightmarish blackouts, as we have had in the past, is that soft power? Is it light? I do not think so.

So, admittedly, humanitarian aid alone cannot solve everything, and that is why we published this humanitarian communication, which is more of a strategy, in reality, in the face of the challenges we are facing today. For it to be effective, it must work hand in hand with diplomacy, with development aid, to have a long-term vision. That is also why we proposed for the next MFF to have Global Europe with a cushion of 25 billion and principles that will be protected, since the 1996 regulations specific to humanitarian aid will remain applicable.

So, will this money be well spent? That is also a question that we can, of course, ask ourselves. There is not zero risk, but in any case we have zero tolerance and a solid control system in place, with monitoring by our own ECHO offices which are on the spot, which are in contact with our partners who distribute humanitarian aid, with audits by the European Court of Auditors, with detailed reports. So yes, everything is in place to ensure that our citizens' money is well spent.

Humanitarian aid – I agree – is the noblest, most dignified face of the European Union, and if we were to give it a face, it would certainly be that of a woman. A woman in Sudan fleeing war, who is displaced among the 13 million displaced people, or a woman looking for her buried child in Caracas. That is humanitarian aid. That is what I see, that is what I am confronted with every time I go on a mission. It is hope, it is a vision of the future for us all, and we must be proud of it, keep it alive.

I count on you, I thank you and I wish you a good vote shortly for your resolution.

4-0040-0000.sourceText:
Merci beaucoup, Madame la Commissaire, pour votre engagement.

J’ai reçu une proposition de résolution pour clore ce débat.

Le débat est clos.

Le vote aura lieu aujourd’hui.

La séance est suspendue. Elle reprendra dans quelques instants avec la déclaration de la Commission sur l’évaluation de la politique commune de la pêche et suivi.
4-0040-0000.englishText:
Thank you very much, Madam Commissioner, for your commitment.

I have received a motion for a resolution to wind up this debate.

The debate is closed.

The vote will take place today.

The sitting is suspended. It will resume in a few moments with the Commission statement on the evaluation of the common fisheries policy and follow-up.

4-0046-0000.sourceText:
L’ordre du jour appelle le débat sur la déclaration de la Commission sur l’évaluation de la politique commune de la pêche et le suivi (2026/2778(RSP)).

Je tiens à rappeler aux intervenants que, compte tenu des mesures de test actuellement en place et de leurs impératifs de fin du débat, il sera nécessaire de respecter strictement les temps de parole.

Je souhaite la bienvenue au commissaire Costas Kadis, à qui j’ai le plaisir de donner la parole pour ouvrir cette discussion.
4-0046-0000.englishText: The next item is the debate on the Commission statement on the evaluation of the common fisheries policy and follow-up (2026/2778(RSP)). I would like to remind speakers that, given the testing measures currently in place and the constraints regarding the end of the debate, it will be necessary to strictly adhere to speaking times. I welcome Commissioner Costas Kadis, to whom I am pleased to give the floor to open this discussion.

4-0047-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, honourable Members, the Common Fisheries Policy Regulation is the European Union's foundation for sustainable fisheries and aquaculture. This April, one decade after its last revision, the Commission's evaluation confirmed that the approach adopted in 2013 to reconcile the three core objectives of the CFP – environmental, social and economic sustainability – remain valid. The evaluation further demonstrates that the regulation's effectiveness depends not only on its overarching framework, but also on the operationalisation of its tools, including technical and conservation measures, control mechanisms and multiannual plans.

Starting with the environmental pillar, the evaluation finds progress in reducing overfishing, but stock abundance has not increased as expected. The landing obligation has fallen short of expectations on selective behaviour or catch composition. This matters beyond the environment, because conservation underpins long‑term socio‑economic prosperity. And here the evaluation finds that the sector's socio‑economic performance also falls short of what the 2013 reform envisaged. This is linked to several persistent challenges facing the EU fisheries sector, including an ageing fleet, high energy dependency, rising operational costs and difficulties in attracting young generations. Access to marine biological resources is also an issue for the small‑scale fishers. Profitability has not improved as expected. This is not only due to the challenges I just mentioned, but can also be explained, to a large extent, by decreasing landings due to slow recovery of fish stocks and by an incomplete adjustment of the fleet capacity to available fish stocks.

Moreover, the evaluation found that while science and data collection have improved, there is a growing demand to better quantify the socio‑economic impact of this on the sector, and to integrate the data into the scientific advice that feeds into our policy decisions. Here, we have already taken steps forward with the first dedicated social report on the sector, published just two weeks ago.

In aquaculture, the evaluation shows the limits of the non-binding EU tools the sector relies on. Where measures depend mainly on guidance and voluntary uptake, progress can be uneven and too slow, particularly in areas such as administrative simplification and enabling conditions for growth.

External disruptions are also increasingly affecting fisheries and aquaculture: COVID‑19, the war in Ukraine, Brexit, and systemic changes such as demographic ageing, geopolitical shifts and accelerating climate change. While these factors go beyond the direct remit of the Common Fisheries Policy Regulation, stakeholders rightfully expect the policy framework to offer ways to respond and adapt.

On the international stage, the EU remains a global leader in sustainable fisheries. We must uphold this role, especially in combating illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, and ensure fair competition for our operators with third‑country fleets.

Honourable Members, the evaluation provided a diagnosis of the rules in place. Now we need to take political decisions on the way forward, including looking into the question of which shortcomings identified in the evaluation require legislative changes and to what extent. I look forward to the discussion that will follow.

4-0048-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señor comisario, señorías, en primer lugar, quiero agradecer al comisario Kadis su disposición. Creo que es una disposición, desde el principio, para trabajar en este tema tan importante. Siempre ha sido muy aperturista y ha escuchado a los pescadores y también a los científicos al respecto.

Tras diez años desde la reforma de 2013, la pregunta es si hemos avanzado rápidamente. Yo creo que hemos logrado resultados ambivalentes y, ahora, hay que cambiar el paradigma para poder solventar situaciones que se han producido a lo largo de estos años.

El paquete de simplificación no puede esperar —y eso lo sabemos— y al mismo tiempo lentamente hemos de trabajar con la PPC, que es un tema fundamental para el futuro de la pesquería. El 15 % de bajada, 2 000 buques al año de pérdida en Europa, hemos bajado 22,8 kilos de consumo por persona en diez años, con una fuerte subida de precio. Por tanto, no nos estamos alimentando de proteínas, importamos mucho pescado y va bajando la capacidad de nuestra flota.

Por tanto, tenemos que trabajar en esta casuística importante. ¿Qué quiere decir esto? Que hay mucho que reflexionar. Claro que hay que apostar por la sostenibilidad de los caladeros: eso es un tema irrenunciable, pero, además, es irrenunciable porque en estos momentos los pescadores así lo ven y así lo quieren hacer, pero con las herramientas necesarias, dotadas en la PPC para poder hacerlo: obligación de desembarque, tonelaje social, ir más allá en el Reglamento de control, el Reglamento sobre el Mediterráneo, el Reglamento sobre aguas profundas y las 87 zonas cerradas con el tema del palangre o el FEMPA y los recursos económicos que vamos a tener para el futuro, que esa es una de las primeras cuestiones que este Parlamento tiene que arreglar, siendo la pesquería un tema fundamental para el devenir de la alimentación, de las zonas costeras y, por supuesto, del trabajo de nuestros pescadores —hombres y mujeres— y la diversificación de la costa. Por tanto, ese es nuestro objetivo.
4-0048-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, firstly, I would like to thank Commissioner Kadis for his willingness. I believe he has shown a willingness from the outset to work on this very important issue. He has always been very open-minded and has listened to fishermen and also scientists in this regard.

Ten years after the 2013 reform, the question is whether we have progressed rapidly. I believe we have achieved ambivalent results and now we must change the paradigm in order to resolve situations that have arisen over these years.

The simplification package cannot wait—and we know that—and at the same time we must slowly work on the CFP, which is a fundamental issue for the future of the fishery. A 15% drop, a loss of 2 000 vessels per year in Europe, consumption has dropped by 22.8 kilos per person in ten years, with a sharp rise in price. Therefore, we are not feeding ourselves with protein, we import a lot of fish and our fleet capacity is declining.

Therefore, we have to work on this important set of circumstances. What does this mean? That there is much to reflect upon.
