Of course we must be committed to the sustainability of the fishing grounds: that is a non-negotiable issue, but it is also non-negotiable because at this moment fishermen see it that way and want to do so, but with the necessary tools provided in the CFP to be able to do it: landing obligation, social tonnage, going further in the Control Regulation, the Mediterranean Regulation, the deep-sea Regulation and the 87 closed areas regarding longlines or the EMFAF and the economic resources that we are going to have for the future, which is one of the first issues that this Parliament has to fix, fisheries being a fundamental issue for the future of food supply, coastal areas and, of course, the work of our fishermen—men and women—and the diversification of the coast. Therefore, that is our objective.

4-0049-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, Senhor Comissário, em maio, a Comissão das Pescas foi aos Açores. Ouvimos pescadores, armadores, investigadores, e a mensagem foi clara: os stocks melhoram, o rendimento da frota cai. O setor envelhece, as embarcações perdem eficiência. Os custos sobem e a concorrência internacional aperta. As áreas marinhas protegidas crescem, mas as compensações não chegam aos pescadores.

Senhor Comissário, sei do seu empenho na política comum das pescas, mas este é o momento de agir. Deixo por isso, quatro apelos.

Simplificar, sim; desproteger, não. Precisamos de controlos eficazes e de frotas modernizadas. Não é a papelada que salva os pescadores; são rendimentos, estabilidade, investimento e promoção da sustentabilidade.

Segundo, a renovação geracional. Sem presente para os pescadores, não há futuro para a política comum das pescas. É necessário, por isso, tornar este setor mais atrativo, para atrair mais gente.

O terceiro elemento diz respeito à dimensão internacional: combater a pesca ilegal, reforçar a cooperação pelos oceanos. A União Europeia tem de liderar a nível das respostas a estes desafios.

Por fim, o orçamento. Não é possível falar em futuro das pescas com um corte de 66 % do financiamento.

Este Parlamento e este grupo político vão continuar a lutar por mais fundos para as pescas e para as regiões ultraperiféricas, porque, como tenho dito várias vezes, só na matemática é que menos com menos dá mais.
4-0049-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, in May, the Committee on Fisheries went to the Azores. We heard from fishermen, vessel owners, researchers, and the message was clear: stocks are improving, fleet income is falling. The sector is aging, vessels are losing efficiency. Costs are rising and international competition is tightening. Marine protected areas are growing, but compensations are not reaching the fishermen.

Commissioner, I know of your commitment to the common fisheries policy, but now is the time to act. I therefore leave four appeals.

Simplify, yes; unprotect, no. We need effective controls and modernized fleets. It is not paperwork that saves fishermen; it is income, stability, investment, and the promotion of sustainability.

Second, generational renewal. Without a present for fishermen, there is no future for the common fisheries policy. It is therefore necessary to make this sector more attractive, to draw more people in.

The third element concerns the international dimension: combating illegal fishing, strengthening cooperation for the oceans. The European Union must lead in responding to these challenges.

Finally, the budget. It is not possible to talk about the future of fisheries with a 66% cut in funding.

This Parliament and this political group will continue to fight for more funds for fisheries and for the outermost regions, because, as I have said several times, only in mathematics does minus times minus equal plus.

4-0050-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, vandaag is er een debat over de evaluatie van het gemeenschappelijk visserijbeleid. Bij uw aantreden, eind 2024, kwam de aanlandplicht al ter sprake: een verplichting die in de praktijk voor veel vissers niet werkbaar is. U gaf toen aan dat dit opnieuw bekeken diende te worden, maar nu, bijna twee jaar later, moeten we vaststellen dat er nog geen zichtbare concrete actie is ondernomen.

In december 2025 werd mijn initiatiefverslag over de modernisering en verduurzaming van de Europese visserij aangenomen in dit Parlement. Daarin vroegen wij om regels te versoepelen en te vereenvoudigen, zodat innovatie sneller kan worden toegelaten. Wij vroegen om schepen te kunnen moderniseren en regels rond brutotonnage los te koppelen van echte viscapaciteit, zodat er ruimte komt voor veiligere schepen, betere werkomstandigheden en nieuwe motoren. Maar ook daar helaas geen concrete actie.

We hebben het gehad over innovatieve visietechnieken zoals pulsvissen, een techniek die minder brandstof verbruikt, minder bijvangst heeft en de zeebodem nagenoeg niet belast. En toch blijft deze techniek vastzitten in politieke blokkades, onwil en wantrouwen, in plaats van dat deze techniek beoordeeld wordt op basis van wetenschap. Ook daar op dit moment geen actie.

En dan de begroting. Terwijl vissers investeringen moeten doen om te moderniseren en te verduurzamen, gaat de visserijbegroting met ongeveer 68 % omlaag. En dan zegt de Commissie: er kunnen middelen komen via de nationale en regionale plannen. Maar laten we eerlijk zijn: als de visserij moet concurreren met alle grote prioriteiten, dan staan onze vissers achteraan in de rij. Ook hier werd geen concrete actie ondernomen om de visserijbegroting te verdedigen.

Vissers hebben geen nieuwe routekaarten of nieuwe strategieën nodig. Ook geen nieuw oceaanpact. Wat zij wel nodig hebben, zijn werkbare regels, investeringsruimte, rechtszekerheid en een toekomstperspectief. En daarom blijf ik herhalen: geen woorden, maar daden. Actie op de aanlandplicht, actie op innovatie, actie op modernisering en actie op de begroting.
4-0050-0000.englishText:
Mr President, today there is a debate on the evaluation of the Common Fisheries Policy. When you took office at the end of 2024, the landing obligation was already discussed: an obligation that in practice is unworkable for many fishermen. You indicated at the time that this needed to be looked at again, but now, almost two years later, we must conclude that no visible concrete action has been taken yet.

In December 2025, my own-initiative report on the modernisation and sustainability of European fisheries was adopted in this Parliament. In it, we asked to relax and simplify rules so that innovation can be authorised more quickly. We asked to be able to modernise vessels and to decouple rules on gross tonnage from actual fishing capacity, creating room for safer ships, better working conditions and new engines. But unfortunately no concrete action there either.

We have discussed innovative fishing techniques such as pulse fishing, a technique that consumes less fuel, has less bycatch and practically does not disturb the seabed. And yet this technique remains stuck in political blockades, unwillingness and distrust, instead of being assessed on the basis of science. No action there at the moment either.

And then the budget. While fishermen have to make investments to modernise and become more sustainable, the fisheries budget is going down by approximately 68%. And then the Commission says: funds can come through national and regional plans. But let's be honest: if fisheries have to compete with all the major priorities, then our fishermen are at the back of the queue. Here too, no concrete action was taken to defend the fisheries budget.

Fishermen do not need new roadmaps or new strategies. Nor a new ocean pact. What they do need is workable rules, room for investment, legal certainty and a future perspective. And that is why I keep repeating: actions speak louder than words. Action on the landing obligation, action on innovation, action on modernisation and action on the budget.

4-0051-0000.sourceText: Zahvaljujem. Povjereniče Kadis, kolegice i kolege, na plenarnoj sjednici konačno raspravljamo o ribarstvenoj politici. Nije pretjerano reći da je stanje alarmantno. Valja ponoviti podatak da Europa uvozi preko 70 posto ribe koju konzumiramo. Na neki način svojim regulativama pomažemo konkurenciji, stvaramo jaču konkurenciju nego što je potrebno, a naši ribari se i dalje nose s vrlo teškim teretom. Još nisam upoznao ribara koji mi kaže da mu je lakše otkad je Hrvatska ušla u Europsku uniju. Stanje se mora hitno promijeniti. Mediteranska uredba je na snazi 20 godina. Zastarjela je. Situacija se promijenila. Imamo nedostatak male plave ribe, to svi znamo, ali ništa se ne događa da se to stanje ispravi. Dakle, dame i gospodo, ribarima se godinama nameću nova ograničenja, dok konkretna rješenja izostaju. Zato je nužna hitna revizija Mediteranske uredbe i ovaj regulatorni okvir, koji će istodobno štititi ribarske interese, ali i osigurati stokove. Dakle, vrijeme je za djelovanje, a ne samo za prazne fraze.
4-0051-0000.englishText: Thank you. Commissioner Kadis, dear colleagues, at the plenary session we are finally discussing fisheries policy. It is no exaggeration to say that the situation is alarming. It is worth repeating the fact that Europe imports over 70 percent of the fish we consume. In a way, with our regulations we are helping the competition, we are creating stronger competition than necessary, and our fishermen are still dealing with a very heavy burden. I have not yet met a fisherman who tells me that it has been easier for him since Croatia joined the European Union. The situation must change urgently. The Mediterranean Regulation has been in force for 20 years. It is outdated. The situation has changed. We have a shortage of small pelagic fish, we all know that, but nothing is happening to correct this situation. Therefore, ladies and gentlemen, new restrictions have been imposed on fishermen for years, while concrete solutions are lacking. That is why an urgent revision of the Mediterranean Regulation is necessary, as well as this regulatory framework, which will simultaneously protect fishing interests and ensure stocks. Therefore, it is time for action, and not just empty phrases.

4-0052-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, the common fisheries policy stems back for more than 55 years and is, together with the common agricultural policy and the internal market, one of the core policies of our Union, and that is why this discussion is so important today.

For Renew Europe, our priority is on policies that deliver for fisheries, for the marine environment and for the coastal communities that depend on both of these. The Commission's evaluation of the CFP shows that there is room for improvement, and as we all know, evaluation is only worth something if it leads to action. We see a need for a landing obligation that meets the objectives – which this evaluation showed that it does not. We see a need for an energy transition within the sector, but the proposal for the new MFF risks burying funding under administrative red tape. And we see the need for the Commission to respond to the crisis, not least in the Baltic Sea, and not least since Parliament adopted our report on the management plan.

Commissioner, you have a lot to do and this evaluation shows that. But the main fight today should not be on the revision of the legal text or not. It should be about real action for real people. Our simple task for the Commission is simply to act. The time for reflection is over, and we need to make sure that we have a CFP that delivers thriving oceans, fisheries and coastal communities.

4-0053-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, colleagues, Commissioner, the 2013 CFP reform took more than four years to perform. There was a white paper, a green paper. We had impact assessments. We had discussions in Member States, evaluations, discussions in the sector. It took a very long time and it was a thorough work.

The evaluation now shows that what we did was the right thing to do. We haven't reached all the objectives – that's true. But the evaluation shows that it's not because the objectives were wrong, it is because there hasn't been enough commitment in Member States to really implement the policies needed. The landing obligation – there's funds to be used. There's ways and technical measures to avoid unwanted catches. But the evaluation shows that very few Member States have invested in that.

Rebuilding stocks at biomass levels above those that can produce maximum sustainable yields. Well, here we have to apply the precautionary approach with quota-setting. And we need accurate stock assessments. But that's impossible without sufficient control and data collection. Still, again, Member States have not invested in that enough. We still have overcapacity of fleets. The fact remains that with more boats, we will not have more fish in the ocean. The only thing we will have is less profitable fishermen, and this fact needs to really be understood. We need to focus on these things.

We also need to understand we have a climate crisis that is not only affecting people in Paris or us here sweating in Strasbourg, it's also affecting fish stocks and the ocean, and we need to take that into account. Now we have the chance to really harmonise and clarify our legislation with the Ocean Act, and that is what we should be focusing on.

4-0054-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, dear Commissioner, I was glad to see that the evaluation clearly recognises that healthy ecosystems are a prerequisite for sustainable and profitable fisheries.

In the PECH Committee last month, you said that improving daily life for small‑scale fishers is a priority for the Commission. However, the findings of the evaluation are stark. It finds that the CFP is not effectively supporting small‑scale coastal fishers, the value of their catches is declining, and there is no generational renewal, which is key to face the persistent challenges regarding access to fishing communities.

When I asked you last month if the Ocean Act would allocate preferential access to small‑scale, low‑impact fishers within the 12‑nautical‑mile zone, the reply was that it is up to Member States to designate areas at sea, which of course you are correct on. But no matter how much support for small‑scale fishers is expressed in policies and legislation, and it really is – you would be really positive if you read it and you thought it was going to happen – the reality is that the power to improve daily life for a small‑scale fisher largely lies with Member States, and we don't see that happening.

We need to be talking about access to quota, access to funding, and this should be a debate at home in Ireland, because all we hear at home in Ireland when it comes to the fisheries debate is: 'Ireland got a bad deal when it came to getting quota'. Yeah, I agree we should have more quota, but that does not seem to be changing. And to me it's just a populist debate that goes on and on. We need to discuss why more of the quota we have doesn't go to small‑scale fishers. Thank you for your work, Commissioner.

4-0055-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Herr Kommissar, verehrte Kollegen! Wir stehen erneut hier, diskutieren die sogenannten gemischten Ergebnisse der Gemeinsamen Fischereipolitik. Für Europas Fischer und Küstengemeinden sind diese Ergebnisse jedoch alles andere als gemischt; sie sind existenzbedrohend.

Das ist zutiefst ungerecht, denn Europas Fischer waren bereit, Opfer zu bringen, und glaubten den falschen Versprechen dieser EU. Sie akzeptierten geringere Fangmöglichkeiten, strengere Vorschriften und kostspielige Anpassungen, um die Ziele vor allem der Klimaideologie und den Nachhaltigkeitszirkus der Gemeinsamen Fischereipolitik zu erreichen. Ihnen wurde versprochen, dass diese Opfer zu reichhaltigeren Fischbeständen und besseren wirtschaftlichen Perspektiven führen.

Die europäischen Fischer warten bis heute vergebens. Selbst nach Berücksichtigung des Brexits fängt die EU-Fischereiflotte heute rund ein Viertel weniger Fische als noch vor zehn Jahren. 25 % weniger in zehn Jahren; das sollte uns in Alarmstimmung versetzen.

Wir erleben eine schrumpfende Flotte, sinkende Beschäftigung und eine alternde Belegschaft, die für ihre Kinder keine Zukunft mehr in der Fischerei sieht. Als die Gemeinsame Fischereipolitik 2014 reformiert wurde, gab es in Europa noch 150 000 Fischbetriebe; heute sind es nur noch rund 120 000, und diese sind permanent von Bürokratie, niedrigen Einkommen und immer strengeren Regeln bedroht, die die Realität gemischter Fischerei ignorieren.

Das ist keine Nachhaltigkeit; das ist ein gesteuerter Niedergang unserer Ernährungssicherheit; das muss uns klar sein. Brüssel hat immer neue Ebenen der Regulierung, Überwachung und Kontrolle geschaffen, während ausländische Importe unsere Märkte überschwemmen. Im Jahr 2000 importierte diese EU rund 40 % der konsumierten Meeresfrüchte; dieser Anteil ist heute auf 70 % gestiegen. 70 % – und wir haben eine eigene Fischindustrie: Das muss man sich mal vorstellen.

Und da sitzt der Kommissar für Fischerei und erzählt uns immer noch seine grünen Märchen. Gleichzeitig werden europäische Gewässer zunehmend von Drittstaaten befischt, was die Erholung der Bestände besonders im Mittelmeer erschwert. Die Antwort der EU darauf lediglich, die Fangtage für europäische Fischer weiter zu reduzieren, statt konsequent gegen illegale Fischerei vorzugehen.

Die Gemeinsame Fischereipolitik ist ein perfektes Symbol für alles, was in dieser Union schiefläuft: zentralisierte Macht in Brüssel, die nationales und regionales Wissen aushebelt; ideologische Umweltziele, die wirtschaftliche und soziale Realitäten ignorieren, und das Schlimmste ist die Weigerung, unsere eigenen europäischen Fischer an erste Stelle zu setzen.

Was ist zu tun? Was werden wir als Alternative für Deutschland tun? Ernährungssouveränität, Ernährungssicherheit ist für uns Priorität eins. Wettbewerbsfähige europäische Fischfangflotten und blühende Küstengemeinden müssen Vorrang bekommen vor einer globalistischen, grünen, weltfremden Ideologie – weg damit!

Herr Kommissar, die Bewertung ist eindeutig: Die Gemeinsame Fischereipolitik hat unsere Fischer im Stich gelassen; Sie und die Kommission sind der Untergang der europäischen Fischerei. Es tut mir leid, das kann ich Ihnen nicht ersparen.
4-0055-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues! We are standing here again, discussing the so-called mixed results of the Common Fisheries Policy. For Europe's fishermen and coastal communities, however, these results are anything but mixed; they are a threat to their existence.

This is deeply unfair, because Europe's fishermen were willing to make sacrifices and believed the false promises of this EU. They accepted lower fishing opportunities, stricter regulations, and costly adjustments in order to achieve the goals of climate ideology in particular and the sustainability circus of the Common Fisheries Policy. They were promised that these sacrifices would lead to richer fish stocks and better economic prospects.

European fishermen are still waiting in vain to this day. Even after taking Brexit into account, the EU fishing fleet catches around a quarter fewer fish today than it did ten years ago. 25% less in ten years; that should put us in a state of alarm.

We are experiencing a shrinking fleet, declining employment, and an aging workforce that no longer sees a future in fishing for its children. When the Common Fisheries Policy was reformed in 2014, there were still 150,000 fishing businesses in Europe; today there are only around 120,000, and these are permanently threatened by bureaucracy, low incomes, and increasingly strict rules that ignore the reality of mixed fisheries.

This is not sustainability; this is a managed decline of our food security; we must be clear about that. Brussels has created ever new levels of regulation, monitoring, and control, while foreign imports flood our markets. In 2000, this EU imported around 40% of the seafood consumed; this share has now risen to 70%. 70% - and we have our own fishing industry: you have to imagine that.

And there sits the Commissioner for Fisheries, still telling us his green fairy tales. At the same time, European waters are increasingly being fished by third countries, which makes the recovery of stocks particularly difficult in the Mediterranean. The EU's response to this is merely to further reduce the number of fishing days for European fishermen, instead of taking consistent action against illegal fishing.

The Common Fisheries Policy is a perfect symbol of everything that is going wrong in this Union: centralized power in Brussels that sidelines national and regional knowledge; ideological environmental targets that ignore economic and social realities, and worst of all, the refusal to put our own European fishermen first.

What is to be done? What will we as Alternative for Germany do? Food sovereignty, food security is priority number one for us. Competitive European fishing fleets and thriving coastal communities must be given priority over a globalist, green, unrealistic ideology - away with it!

Commissioner, the assessment is clear: the Common Fisheries Policy has let down our fishermen; you and the Commission are the downfall of European fishing. I am sorry, I cannot spare you that.

4-0056-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Monsieur le Commissaire, à la suite de la présentation de l’évaluation de la politique commune des pêches devant notre commission le 3 juin dernier, le PPE a souhaité ce débat avec vous en plénière. L’évaluation appelle désormais une évolution, guidée par un objectif: que les attentes des pêcheurs européens et de l’ensemble de la filière soient concrètement et enfin prises en compte.

À commencer par le renouvellement et la modernisation de la flotte, sans lesquels il est illusoire de croire que nous pourrons attirer des jeunes vers le métier. Nous avons identifié les articles de la PCP et du Feampa qu’il faut revisiter pour décarboner les navires et améliorer les conditions de travail. Rien ni personne ne devrait désormais faire obstacle à cette nécessité, et les moyens financiers pour y parvenir doivent être sanctuarisés. De même que le temps est venu de simplifier et de regrouper en un seul texte les révisions attendues: obligation de débarquement, contrôle des pêches, organisation commune des marchés… Autant de règles pour certaines inapplicables, pour d’autres inopérantes. Vous avez pu le constater vous-même, Monsieur le Commissaire, au cours de vos très nombreux déplacements à la rencontre des acteurs de la pêche.

D’où l’urgence à agir en conservant les avancées de la PCP – et il y en a –, mais en acceptant aussi de corriger ce qui doit l’être. Vous avez annoncé des amendements ciblés; notre groupe du PPE est prêt à y travailler sans tarder.
4-0056-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, following the presentation of the evaluation of the Common Fisheries Policy to our committee on 3 June last, the EPP requested this debate with you in plenary. The evaluation now calls for an evolution, guided by one objective: that the expectations of European fishermen and the entire sector are concretely and finally taken into account.

Starting with the renewal and modernization of the fleet, without which it is illusory to believe that we can attract young people to the profession. We have identified the articles of the CFP and the EMFAF that must be revisited to decarbonize vessels and improve working conditions. Nothing and no one should now stand in the way of this necessity, and the financial means to achieve this must be safeguarded. Just as the time has come to simplify and group together in a single text the expected revisions: landing obligation, fisheries control, common organization of markets... So many rules, some of which are inapplicable, others inoperative. You have been able to see this for yourself, Commissioner, during your very numerous trips to meet fisheries stakeholders.

Hence the urgency to act while preserving the advances of the CFP – and there are some – but also by accepting to correct what needs to be corrected. You have announced targeted amendments; our EPP group is ready to work on them without delay.

4-0057-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, como usted sabe, comisario, (el orador se expresa en una lengua no oficial).

Es cierto, la política pesquera común ha permitido mejorar la sostenibilidad de las capturas europeas. Pero ahora es importante garantizar la sostenibilidad de las comunidades pesqueras, porque eso es lo que está en peligro. Admitámoslo: la evaluación de la política pesquera común constata la destrucción de un 30 % del empleo del sector, pérdida de poder adquisitivo, falta de relevo generacional y obsolescencia de la flota. No hablamos de problemas de aplicación, hablamos de problemas de diseño y de nuevas realidades, problemas que se van a acrecentar con un recorte inadmisible de los fondos de la pesca que tenemos que impedir.

Comisario, es el momento de proponer de forma inminente una reforma específica de la política pesquera común para reequilibrar las tres dimensiones de la sostenibilidad, impulsar el relevo generacional, afrontar el envejecimiento de la flota con ayudas para la descarbonización de la misma, reformar el enfoque obsoleto de la capacidad pesquera, promover TAC plurianuales e introducir límites a las variaciones interanuales de TAC y cuotas.

Y es que al sector se le acaba la paciencia y créame, vuelvo al principio, soy gallego (el orador se expresa en una lengua no oficial).
4-0057-0000.englishText:
Mr President, as you know, Commissioner, (the speaker speaks in a non-official language).

It is true that the common fisheries policy has helped to improve the sustainability of European catches. But now it is important to guarantee the sustainability of fishing communities, because that is what is at stake. Let's admit it: the evaluation of the common fisheries policy notes the destruction of 30% of employment in the sector, a loss of purchasing power, a lack of generational renewal and the obsolescence of the fleet. We are not talking about implementation problems, we are talking about design problems and new realities, problems that are going to be exacerbated by an inadmissible cut in fisheries funds that we must prevent.

Commissioner, it is time to propose imminently a specific reform of the common fisheries policy to rebalance the three dimensions of sustainability, boost generational renewal, tackle the aging of the fleet with aid for its decarbonization, reform the obsolete approach to fishing capacity, promote multiannual TACs and introduce limits on year-on-year variations in TACs and quotas.

And the sector is running out of patience and believe me, I return to the beginning, I am Galician (the speaker speaks in a non-official language).

4-0058-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, aujourd’hui on doit parler de la politique commune de la pêche et de son évaluation depuis 2013. C’est un vaste programme, et qu’en dire réellement? Doit-on parler de l’inaction de la Commission, qui batifole d’évaluations en réunions, de réunions en résumés, de résumés en groupes de travail, de groupes de travail en évaluations, avant de recommencer le cycle infernal? Parce qu’en fait, Monsieur Kadis, rien ne bouge. À chaque audition, ce sont les mêmes termes creux, les mêmes impasses politiques qui mènent notre pêche à sa perte, et je pense sincèrement que c’est le but ultime: tuer notre pêche artisanale au profit d’une pêche financiarisée. Pour autant, ce serait trop facile de s’en tenir à la simple responsabilité de la Commission.

Je crois qu’il faut parler aussi ici – plutôt – de ceux qui n’ont jamais de mots assez durs sur le terrain pour dénoncer Bruxelles, mais qui ont voté et votent tout ce que la Commission impose à nos pêcheurs artisans. C’est en fait, je pense, de cela que meurt notre filière pêche, et ce sont eux qui portent l’entière responsabilité de la situation de nos pêcheurs aujourd’hui.

Alors notre engagement, il est tout autre: résister, défendre notre pêche, défendre notre souveraineté alimentaire, changer de cap et enfin porter l’espérance de nos pêcheurs pour demain. Car c’est à leurs côtés que nous nous battons. Nous ne lâcherons rien et tout est encore possible!
4-0058-0000.englishText:
Mr President, today we must talk about the common fisheries policy and its evaluation since 2013. It is a vast programme, and what can really be said about it? Should we talk about the inaction of the Commission, which flits from evaluations to meetings, from meetings to summaries, from summaries to working groups, from working groups to evaluations, before starting the infernal cycle all over again? Because in fact, Mr Kadis, nothing moves. At every hearing, it is the same empty terms, the same political dead ends that are leading our fisheries to their doom, and I sincerely believe that this is the ultimate goal: to kill our artisanal fisheries for the benefit of financialised fisheries. However, it would be too easy to stick solely to the responsibility of the Commission.

I believe we must also speak here – rather – of those who never have harsh enough words on the ground to denounce Brussels, but who have voted and vote for everything that the Commission imposes on our artisanal fishermen. This is in fact, I think, what our fisheries sector is dying of, and they bear full responsibility for the situation of our fishermen today.

So our commitment is quite different: to resist, to defend our fisheries, to defend our food sovereignty, to change course and finally to carry the hope of our fishermen for tomorrow. For it is by their side that we are fighting. We will give nothing up and everything is still possible!

4-0059-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, la valutazione della politica comune della pesca conferma ciò che i nostri pescatori stanno denunciando da anni.

La stessa Commissione riconosce che il settore soffre di un progressivo invecchiamento degli operatori, della difficoltà di attrarre giovani e di una redditività troppo modesta.

La relazione ammette sostanzialmente che gli obiettivi economici e sociali della riforma non sono stati raggiunti. Proprio per questo è arrivato il momento di cambiare passo. Un modello costruito quasi esclusivamente su vincoli, divieti e burocrazia finisce per indebolire l'intero comparto, rende più deboli le nostre marinerie e aumenta la dipendenza dall'Unione e dalle importazioni di prodotti ittici provenienti da paesi che non rispettano i nostri stessi standard ambientali e sociali, in Italia, il 70‑80 % del prodotto ittico è importato.

La sostenibilità non è solo ambientale: deve essere economica, sociale e alimentare. Senza imprese competitive, senza redditività e senza nuove generazioni disposte a impegnarsi nella pesca, non esiste alcuna transizione.

Con una revisione ci si aspettano più risorse per il settore, una radicale semplificazione delle regole superflue, il superamento di misure che hanno dimostrato tutti i loro limiti – come l'obbligo di sbarco – investimenti per il rinnovo della flotta, la sicurezza a bordo, l'innovazione e il rilancio della maricultura europea, che è essenziale.

Difendiamo la nostra sovranità alimentare, il lavoro delle comunità costiere e il futuro dei giovani che vogliono ancora impegnarsi in questa professione. La transizione sostenibile non può essere un percorso ideologico contro i pescatori, deve essere una transizione pragmatica.
4-0059-0000.englishText:
Mr President, honourable colleagues, the evaluation of the common fisheries policy confirms what our fishermen have been denouncing for years.

The Commission itself acknowledges that the sector suffers from the progressive aging of operators, the difficulty in attracting young people, and excessively modest profitability.

The report substantially admits that the economic and social objectives of the reform have not been achieved. Precisely for this reason, the time has come to change pace. A model built almost exclusively on constraints, bans, and bureaucracy ends up weakening the entire sector, makes our fishing fleets weaker, and increases dependence on the Union and on imports of fishery products from countries that do not respect our same environmental and social standards; in Italy, 70-80% of fishery products are imported.

Sustainability is not only environmental: it must be economic, social, and food-related. Without competitive businesses, without profitability, and without new generations willing to commit to fishing, there is no transition.

With a revision, we expect more resources for the sector, a radical simplification of superfluous rules, the overcoming of measures that have shown all their limits - such as the landing obligation - investments for fleet renewal, safety on board, innovation, and the relaunch of European mariculture, which is essential.

Let us defend our food sovereignty, the work of coastal communities, and the future of young people who still want to engage in this profession. The sustainable transition cannot be an ideological path against fishermen; it must be a pragmatic transition.

4-0060-0000.sourceText:
Hr. formand, hr. kommissær! Evaluering af den fælles fiskeripolitik giver en god anledning til at gøre status. Fiskeripolitikken skal bygge på en balance mellem det miljømæssige, økonomiske og social bæredygtighed. Vi skal beskytte fiskebestandene, men vi skal også sikre, at der fortsat er et erhverv og levende kystsamfund. I Danmark er fiskeriet en vigtig del af vores fødevareproduktion. Derfor skulle vi også turde tale om de reelle udfordringer, som vi står med. Fiskebestandene er under pres fra mange sider: forurening, iltsvind, en særlig voldsom skarvbestand påvirker bestandene markant.

Ny forskning i Danmark viser, at 88 % af torskeynglen og skrubberne, dem tager skarvene. Derfor løser vi ikke udfordringen ved at stille flere krav til fiskerne. Vi har brug for en fiskeripolitik, som tager fat på de faktorer, som påvirker livet nede i vandet. Sådan kan vi beskytte havmiljøet, sunde fiskebestande og bevare et konkurrencedygtigt erhverv.
4-0060-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Mr Commissioner! The evaluation of the Common Fisheries Policy provides a good opportunity to take stock. Fisheries policy must be based on a balance between environmental, economic and social sustainability. We must protect fish stocks, but we must also ensure that there is still an industry and vibrant coastal communities. In Denmark, fisheries are an important part of our food production. Therefore, we should also dare to talk about the real challenges we are facing. Fish stocks are under pressure from many sides: pollution, oxygen depletion, a particularly large cormorant population significantly affects the stocks.

New research in Denmark shows that 88% of cod fry and flounders are taken by cormorants. Therefore, we do not solve the challenge by imposing more requirements on fishermen. We need a fisheries policy that addresses the factors that affect life in the water. This is how we can protect the marine environment, healthy fish stocks and preserve a competitive industry.

4-0061-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, sehr geehrter Herr Kommissar, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Wissen Sie eigentlich, was Tomaten in Spanien mit dem Thema der heutigen Debatte zu tun haben? Eine ganze Menge. In Europa haben wir immer mehr Aquakulturen überall in unseren Ozeanen, beispielsweise für Lachse, und die werden sehr gerne als besonders nachhaltig deklariert. Aber auch diese Millionen Lachse müssen etwas essen, müssen Futter haben, und dafür werden tonnenweise Wildfische gefangen, nur um sie danach zu Fischmehl zu verarbeiten, um dieses dann zu verfüttern. Für diese Wildfische gibt es eine enorme Überfischung in allen Regionen, beispielsweise auch in den Küstenregionen Westafrikas, gerade bei Kleinfischern.

Die Fischerei in diesen Regionen ist teilweise komplett zusammengebrochen, und viele Menschen und ganze Familien verlieren ihre Lebensgrundlage dadurch und werden dadurch in die Migration getrieben, beispielsweise auf die Kanarischen Inseln. Und viele, die die gefährliche Überfahrt überleben, landen als Schwarzarbeiter illegal und unter prekären Arbeitsbedingungen in den Gewächshäusern der Tomatenproduktion in Regionen wie Almería und anderen Regionen in Spanien.

Der industrielle Fischfang, wie er gerade praktiziert wird, zerstört nicht nur Ozeane, Lebensräume, er schafft auch enorm viel menschliches Leid.

Lassen Sie uns hier im Haus endlich aufhören, ausschließlich auf die Interessen der Fischerinnen und Fischer und der Industrie zu schauen. Wir brauchen viel mehr Schutzgebiete, und wir brauchen viel weniger Fischfang. Es gibt viele Lebewesen im Meer, die auf Fische angewiesen sind; wir als Menschen sind das nicht.
4-0061-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear Commissioner, dear colleagues! Do you actually know what tomatoes in Spain have to do with the topic of today's debate? Quite a lot. In Europe, we have more and more aquaculture everywhere in our oceans, for example for salmon, and these are very often declared as particularly sustainable. But these millions of salmon also need something to eat, need feed, and for this, tonnes of wild fish are caught just to be processed into fishmeal afterwards in order to feed it to them. There is enormous overfishing of these wild fish in all regions, for example also in the coastal regions of West Africa, especially affecting small-scale fishers.

Fishing in these regions has partly completely collapsed, and many people and entire families are losing their livelihood as a result and are thereby driven into migration, for example to the Canary Islands. And many of those who survive the dangerous crossing end up as illegal undeclared workers and under precarious working conditions in the greenhouses of tomato production in regions like Almería and other regions in Spain.

Industrial fishing, as it is currently practiced, not only destroys oceans and habitats, it also creates an enormous amount of human suffering.

Let us finally stop here in the House looking exclusively at the interests of the fishers and the industry. We need many more protected areas, and we need much less fishing. There are many living creatures in the sea that depend on fish; we as humans do not.

4-0062-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Herr Kommissar, meine Damen und Herren! Die Fischer in der Ostsee tun alles, was Politik von ihnen verlangt: Die Fangquoten wurden gekürzt, Hering und Kabeljau wurden geschont – und doch haben sich die Bestände nicht erholt.

Was ist die Reaktion der EU? Prämien für das Stilllegen – in diesem Jahr zum letzten Mal. Die Entschädigungen für Robbenfraß laufen Ende 2027 aus. Und danach? Nichts mehr! Das ist keine Fischereipolitik, das ist ein Abgesang auf einen ganzen Berufsstand.

Dabei waren die Fischer nie das Problem. Es ist die Eutrophierung; es sind Robben und Kormorane, die mehr Fische fressen als die Flotte überhaupt fangen darf; in der Nordsee besetzen Windparks die Fischgründe; bei Raumordnungsplänen werden die Fischer als Letzte – wenn überhaupt – konsultiert.

Wir brauchen ein Prädatoren-Management, Finanzhilfen für die Flottenerneuerung, den Schutz der Fischgründe und Quoten, die Raubfische und Nährstoffeinträge ehrlich berücksichtigen.

Nichts davon findet sich in Ihrem Folgeprogramm. Diese Politik bestraft diejenigen, die sich an die Regeln halten, und ignoriert die wahren Ursachen des Rückgangs.

(Der Redner ist damit einverstanden, auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“ zu antworten.)
4-0062-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Mr Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen! The fishermen in the Baltic Sea are doing everything that politics demands of them: catch quotas have been cut, herring and cod have been protected - and yet stocks have not recovered.

What is the EU's reaction? Premiums for decommissioning - for the last time this year. Compensation for seal predation expires at the end of 2027. And after that? Nothing more! This is not fisheries policy, this is a swan song for an entire profession.

Yet the fishermen were never the problem. It is eutrophication; it is seals and cormorants eating more fish than the fleet is even allowed to catch; in the North Sea, wind farms are occupying the fishing grounds; in spatial planning, fishermen are the last - if at all - to be consulted.

We need predator management, financial aid for fleet renewal, the protection of fishing grounds and quotas that honestly take predatory fish and nutrient inputs into account.

None of this is to be found in your follow-up programme. This policy punishes those who abide by the rules and ignores the true causes of the decline.

(The speaker agreed to answer a blue-card question.)

4-0063-0000.sourceText:
��blauen Karte“. – Hallo, Herr Kollege! Ich wollte eigentlich gerade den Raum verlassen, aber ich musste einfach stehen bleiben, weil immer wieder von Ihnen und vielen anderen diese Scheindebatten geführt werden.

Immer werden Robben, Kormorane, immer werden die Tiere als Sündenböcke genommen. Können Sie das wissenschaftlich belegen? Weil es gibt nachweisliche Zahlen, beispielsweise von der Uni in Stockholm, die den Einfluss von Kormoranen minimalst machen.

Es ist Überfischung, es ist Klimawandel, es sind Düngemittel, es ist Müll – das ist das, was das Problem der Fischerei ausmacht, und doch bitte nicht die Tiere. Wenn Sie so etwas schon behaupten, dann bitte belegen!
4-0063-0000.englishText:
blue card". - Hello, dear colleague! I actually wanted to leave the room just now, but I simply had to stop because these sham debates are constantly being conducted by you and many others.

Seals, cormorants, animals are always being used as scapegoats. Can you prove that scientifically? Because there are verifiable figures, for example from Stockholm University, which show the impact of cormorants to be minimal.

It is overfishing, it is climate change, it is fertilizers, it is garbage - that is what constitutes the problem of fishing, and please not the animals. If you are going to claim something like that, then please provide proof!

4-0064-0000.sourceText:
��blauen Karte“. – Vielen Dank, Herr Kollege, für die Frage. Natürlich gibt es eine Vielzahl von Problemen, die die Fischer an den Rand des Ruins bringen; das habe ich auch nicht abgestritten. Aber es ist ganz klar, dass Robben und Kormorane auch zum Problemfeld dazugehören.

Ich komme direkt aus Schleswig-Holstein, ich wohne an der Ostsee, und die Fischer dort geben auf, weil die Kormorane ihnen wirklich die Fische wegfressen. Es ist eine Tatsache; da gibt es auch belegbare Studien und Zahlen, und das kann man nicht ignorieren.

Ich habe das andere nicht abgestritten, aber ich habe das betont, was meiner Ansicht nach nicht genügend berücksichtigt wird.
4-0064-0000.englishText:
Blue Card. - Thank you, colleague, for the question. Of course, there are a multitude of problems that are bringing fishermen to the brink of ruin; I did not dispute that either. But it is very clear that seals and cormorants are also part of the problem area.

I come directly from Schleswig-Holstein, I live on the Baltic Sea, and the fishermen there are giving up because the cormorants are truly eating their fish. It is a fact; there are also verifiable studies and figures, and that cannot be ignored.

I did not dispute the other, but I emphasized what in my view is not being sufficiently taken into account.

4-0065-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, Senhor Comissário, entre 2017 e 2023, o setor perdeu 15 % da sua força de trabalho e, neste momento, a nossa dependência externa é superior a 80 %. Baixos rendimentos, condições de trabalho pouco dignas, falta de renovação geracional e excesso de burocracia ameaçam o futuro da pesca e, consequentemente, das nossas comunidades costeiras.

Sei bem do seu empenho, Senhor Comissário. É importante que este seu empenho, e compromisso e defesa, do sector das pescas também seja seguido por outros. Como precisamos de estabilidade e previsibilidade regulatórias, defendo uma revisão da política comum das pescas focada em quatro prioridades.

Quotas de pesca plurianuais que garantam previsibilidade e conciliem os três pilares da sustentabilidade ambiental, mas também económica e social.

Simplificar a legislação e reduzir a carga administrativa. Precisamos de um verdadeiro pacote de simplificação para as pescas. O CATCH IT é importante e deve ser reavaliado para simplificar procedimentos. E a recente obrigatoriedade de eliminar a isenção de registo de descargas até 50 quilos foi também uma má medida que urge corrigir. Também o regime de ajudas deve ter por referência sempre a unidade de produção e não a empresa.

Temos de investir na renovação das embarcações e acabar com a limitação por referência ao peso bruto e potência do motor. Melhores embarcações garantem mais segurança, melhor armazenamento do pescado e mais rendimento para os pescadores.

É essencial manter o FEAMP autónomo e devidamente financiado para as pescas e para a aquacultura sustentável, e, neste momento, urge proteger as regiões ultraperiféricas ao restabelecer o POSEI Pescas.

Precisamos também de condições de concorrência justas. Não podemos exigir aos nossos pescadores os mais elevados padrões ambientais, sociais e laborais, e aceitar importações de países terceiros que não cumprem estas mesmas regras.

Sem pescadores não há pesca, sem pesca não há comunidades costeiras fortes, não há segurança alimentar, nem há soberania marítima europeia.

(O orador aceita responder a uma pergunta «cartão azul»)
4-0065-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, between 2017 and 2023, the sector lost 15% of its workforce and, at this moment, our external dependence is greater than 80%. Low incomes, undignified working conditions, a lack of generational renewal, and excessive bureaucracy threaten the future of fishing and, consequently, of our coastal communities.

I am well aware of your commitment, Commissioner. It is important that this commitment, and your defense and support of the fisheries sector, is also followed by others. As we need regulatory stability and predictability, I advocate a revision of the common fisheries policy focused on four priorities.

Multi-annual fishing quotas that guarantee predictability and reconcile the three pillars of environmental, but also economic and social, sustainability.

Simplify legislation and reduce administrative burden. We need a true simplification package for fisheries. CATCH IT is important and must be reassessed to simplify procedures. And the recent obligation to eliminate the exemption from registering landings up to 50 kilos was also a bad measure that urgently needs to be corrected. Furthermore, the aid regime must always take the production unit as its reference rather than the company.

We must invest in the renewal of vessels and put an end to the limitation by reference to gross weight and engine power. Better vessels guarantee greater safety, better storage of fish, and more income for fishermen.

It is essential to keep the EMFF autonomous and properly funded for fisheries and sustainable aquaculture, and, at this moment, it is urgent to protect the outermost regions by re-establishing POSEI Fisheries.

We also need a level playing field. We cannot demand the highest environmental, social, and labor standards from our fishermen, while accepting imports from third countries that do not comply with these same rules.

Without fishermen there is no fishing, without fishing there are no strong coastal communities, there is no food security, nor is there European maritime sovereignty.

(The speaker agrees to take a "blue card" question)

4-0066-0000.sourceText: ��cartonașului albastru”. – Sunt de acord cu ceea ce ați spus legat de politica pescuitului și revizuirea regulamentului. Nu ați spus însă nimic și mă interesează dacă grupul dumneavoastră politic, dacă dumneavoastră priviți toate reglementările în domeniul pescuitului și din perspectiva socială, pentru că în multe zone, așa cum este și în țara mea, este o sursă de venit pentru foarte mulți, pentru micii pescari. Și ați vorbit de nevoia de finanțare. Nu credeți sau credeți că ar trebui să existe o finanțare și pentru micii pescari? Cum se pot descurca în noianul de reglementări și, în același timp, fără posibilitatea de investiții?
4-0066-0000.englishText: of the "blue card". – I agree with what you said regarding fisheries policy and the revision of the regulation. However, you did not say anything and I am interested to know if your political group, if you view all fisheries regulations also from a social perspective, because in many areas, just as in my country, it is a source of income for very many, for small-scale fishermen. And you spoke about the need for financing. Do you not think, or do you think, that there should also be financing for small-scale fishermen? How can they manage in the maze of regulations and, at the same time, without the possibility of investments?

4-0067-0000.sourceText:
Totalmente de acordo, nós, no nosso grupo, defendemos ambas as possibilidades.

Num momento em que temos uma dependência externa superior a 80 %, precisamos de ter aqui uma força de pesca muito mais forte, desde logo pela pequena pesca, a pesca artesanal, que é essencial e é o motor da pesca e das comunidades costeiras europeias.

Por exemplo, nos Açores, também tivemos aqui um trabalho muito grande na definição das áreas marinhas protegidas e isto tem de ser compensado. Conseguimos mobilizar financiamento público e privado, e não pode agora a Comissão Europeia também bloquear.

Portanto, é preciso agilizar procedimentos e que o dinheiro chegue efetivamente aos pequenos pescadores.
4-0067-0000.englishText:
Fully in agreement, we, in our group, defend both possibilities.

At a time when we have an external dependency of over 80%, we need to have a much stronger fishing force here, starting immediately with small-scale fishing, artisanal fishing, which is essential and is the engine of European fishing and coastal communities.

For example, in the Azores, we also had a very large body of work here in defining marine protected areas and this has to be compensated. We managed to mobilize public and private financing, and the European Commission cannot block it now either.

Therefore, it is necessary to streamline procedures and ensure that the money effectively reaches small-scale fishermen.

4-0068-0000.sourceText:
Sur President, ħa nibda b'mistoqsija sempliċi: jekk int tikkontrolla kemm tistad imma ta' madwarek ma jsegwux l-istess ambizzjoni, ħa jirnexxilek verament tipproteġi l-ħut?

Il-Politika Komuni tas-Sajd hija importanti, u l-prinċipji tagħha għandhom jibqgħu. Imma s-simplifikazzjoni hija wkoll importanti, b'aktar simplifikazzjoni, b'aktar ġustizzja u b'sostenn lis-sajjieda ż-żgħar tagħna li jiddependu mis-settur għall-għajxien tagħhom. Il-problema hawnhekk mhix neċessarjament il-liġi. Il-problema hija li l-liġi weħidha ma tistax tirnexxi fl-ambizzjoni ambjentali tagħha, jekk ma' min naqsmu l-baħar, m'għandux l-istess intenzjoni tagħna. Fil-Mediterran, naqsmu l-istess baħar u l-istess ħut. Għalhekk, ir-responsabbiltà trid tkun ta' kulħadd. L-Ewropa trid tkun aktar b'saħħitha mal-pajjiżi terzi fi ħdan l-għaqdiet reġjonali. Jien ħdimt biex nagħti lill-Ewropa l-aktar għodda b'saħħitha possibbli biex tieħu azzjoni kontra pajjiżi li jippermettu sajd li mhuwiex sostenibbli. Erba' ġimgħat oħra jibda l-istaġun tal-lampuki u s-sajjieda Maltin u Mediterranji se jerġgħu joħorġu jaħdmu.

Għażiż Kummissarju, ħa nerġgħu nħallu lis-sajjieda Maltin tagħna u Mediterranji jaffaċċjaw sajd illegali u mhux sostenibbli minn pajjiż terz fil-Mediterran? Nitolbok biex titkellem mal-pajjiżi terzi qabel jibda l-istaġun, iżżid il-patrols u tipproteġi lil min qed jimxi mar-regoli. Il-Politika Komuni tas-Sajd trid tkun garanzija li nipproteġu lis-sajjieda tagħna.

(Il-kelliem aċċetta li jwieġeb mistoqsija “karta blu”)
4-0068-0000.englishText:
Mr President, I will start with a simple question: if you control how much you fish but those around you do not follow the same ambition, will you really succeed in protecting the fish?

The Common Fisheries Policy is important, and its principles must remain. But simplification is also important, with more simplification, with more fairness and with support for our small fishermen who depend on the sector for their livelihood. The problem here is not necessarily the law. The problem is that the law alone cannot succeed in its environmental ambition if those with whom we share the sea do not have the same intention as us. In the Mediterranean, we share the same sea and the same fish. Therefore, responsibility must be everyone's. Europe must be stronger with third countries within regional organisations. I have worked to give Europe the strongest possible tool to take action against countries that allow unsustainable fishing. In another four weeks, the lampuki season starts and Maltese and Mediterranean fishermen will go out to work again.

Dear Commissioner, are we going to let our Maltese and Mediterranean fishermen face illegal and unsustainable fishing from a third country in the Mediterranean again? I ask you to speak to third countries before the season starts, increase patrols and protect those who follow the rules. The Common Fisheries Policy must be a guarantee that we protect our fishermen.

(The speaker agreed to take a 'blue card' question)

4-0069-0000.sourceText: Coincido con usted en hablar de la pesca ilegal y de las prácticas desleales comerciales, pero anteriormente, en otra intervención, el señor Everding se ha dedicado, en vez de a acompañar a la pesca en este debate tan importante, a atacar a la agricultura de Almería. Yo soy de allí. He visto que usted ha afirmado y ha tocado las palmas. ¿No estará usted de acuerdo en que allí se explota a los inmigrantes para cultivar tomates? Porque, si no, esa realidad se la podemos enseñar y verá usted que está ante una agricultura potente, la más importante y tecnificada y con respeto a los derechos humanos de Europa.
4-0069-0000.englishText: I agree with you in talking about illegal fishing and unfair commercial practices, but previously, in another speech, Mr. Everding dedicated himself, instead of supporting fishing in this very important debate, to attacking Almeria's agriculture. I am from there. I have seen that you have affirmed and applauded. Would you not agree that immigrants are exploited there to grow tomatoes? Because, otherwise, we can show you that reality and you will see that you are facing a powerful agriculture, the most important and technified and with respect for human rights in Europe.

4-0070-0000.sourceText: Naħseb li ma kinitx domanda diretta lejja u lanqas kienet domanda. Però nirrispetta lill-President tal-Kumitat tas-Sajd biex nirrispettaw ukoll id-diskussjoni li hija fuq is-settur tas-sajd. U hawnhekk irridu nkomplu naraw li nibqgħu ffukati, aħna d-deputati kollha tal-Kumitat tas-Sajd, biex nipproteġu lis-sajjieda tagħna. U ejja nibqgħu nagħmlu dan għaliex il-focus tagħna għandu jkun fuqhom u ejja ħa nkomplu nagħtu s-sapport tagħhom lejhom u lejn il-protezzjoni tal-baħar tagħna.
4-0070-0000.englishText: I think it was neither a direct question to me nor was it a question. However, I respect the Chair of the Committee on Fisheries so that we also respect the discussion which is on the fisheries sector. And here we must continue to see that we remain focused, all of us deputies of the Committee on Fisheries, to protect our fishermen. And let us continue to do this because our focus must be on them and let us continue to give our support to them and towards the protection of our sea.

4-0071-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señor comisario, Europa lleva ya más de 40 años con una política pesquera común y la promesa era muy sencilla inicialmente: proteger el mar sin abandonar a aquellos que viven de él.

Pues bien, la propia Comisión Europea acaba de reconocer que ha suspendido el examen. En la evaluación oficial publicada el pasado 30 de abril admite que 12 años después de la última gran reforma, los resultados económicos y sociales prometidos no han llegado. Hace apenas dos semanas, su primer informe social confirmó también lo que los pescadores llevan años denunciando: uno de cada seis empleos pesqueros ha desaparecido desde 2017, un pescador cobra de media menos de la mitad que un trabajador europeo y solo uno de cada cuatro tiene menos de 40 años. Es decir, obviamente los jóvenes no ven futuro en el mar.

El sector lo resume con una frase que yo creo que cualquiera entiende: cada vez hay más barcos para los que salir a faenar cuesta más que quedarse amarrados en puerto. Pero, no se equivoquen, porque además este no es un problema exclusivo de los pescadores, es un problema de todos los europeos, ya que siete de cada diez pescados que consumimos ya vienen de fuera, de países a los que no exigimos las mismas normas sanitarias, ni medioambientales, ni laborables y que sí que imponemos —como siempre— a los nuestros con dureza.

Mientras aquí reducimos nuestra capacidad de producir alimentos, miren al otro lado del estrecho: Marruecos tiene cerca ya de 17 000 embarcaciones artesanales, un 370 % más que en 1980. Ellos amplían su flota, nosotros pagamos por desguazar la nuestra. Sin pescadores no hay pescado europeo. Ellos decidirán cómo, cuándo y dónde comeremos pescado.
4-0071-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, Europe has had a common fisheries policy for over 40 years and the promise was very simple initially: to protect the sea without abandoning those who live from it.

Well, the European Commission itself has just admitted that it has failed the exam. In the official evaluation published on 30 April last, it admits that 12 years after the last major reform, the promised economic and social results have not arrived. Just two weeks ago, its first social report also confirmed what fishermen have been denouncing for years: one in six fishing jobs has disappeared since 2017, a fisherman earns on average less than half of what a European worker earns, and only one in four is under 40 years old. In other words, young people obviously see no future at sea.

The sector summarises it with a phrase that I believe anyone understands: more and more boats find that going out to fish costs more than staying moored in port. But make no mistake, because this is not an exclusive problem for fishermen, it is a problem for all Europeans, since seven out of ten fish we consume now come from outside, from countries to which we do not demand the same health, environmental or labour standards that we do impose — as always — harshly on our own.

While here we reduce our capacity to produce food, look across the strait: Morocco now has close to 17,000 artisanal vessels, 370% more than in 1980. They expand their fleet, we pay to scrap ours. Without fishermen there is no European fish. They will decide how, when and where we will eat fish.

4-0072-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, wie de evaluatie van het gemeenschappelijk visserijbeleid leest, zou zomaar de indruk kunnen krijgen dat het vooral de lidstaten zijn die steken laten vallen. Wat echter totaal ontbreekt, is een kritische blik op het Europees beleid zelf. Sluit dat nog wel aan op de praktijk? Daar moet het debat nu over gaan. Onze vissers willen verantwoord omgaan met de zee, maar ze hebben ook recht op regels die uitvoerbaar zijn en niet verzanden in bureaucratie.

Een grondige vereenvoudiging van het gemeenschappelijk visserijbeleid is daarom dringend geboden. Zo moet de aanlandplicht worden teruggedraaid. En dat geldt ook voor het verbod op de pulsvisserij. Dat nota bene een techniek die zorgt voor verlaging van het brandstofgebruik en die selectiever vissen bevordert, geen ruimte krijgt, is echt niet meer uit te leggen. Kortom, laten we onze vissers weer perspectief bieden met een beleid dat realistisch, uitvoerbaar en toekomstbestendig is.

(De spreker stemt ermee in om te antwoorden op een “blauwe kaart”-vraag)
4-0072-0000.englishText:
Mr President, anyone who reads the evaluation of the Common Fisheries Policy might easily get the impression that it is primarily the member states that are falling short. What is completely missing, however, is a critical look at European policy itself. Does it still connect with practice? That is what the debate should be about now. Our fishermen want to treat the sea responsibly, but they are also entitled to rules that are workable and do not bog down in bureaucracy.

A thorough simplification of the Common Fisheries Policy is therefore urgently needed. For instance, the landing obligation must be reversed. And the same applies to the ban on pulse fishing. The fact that this technique, of all things, which ensures lower fuel consumption and promotes more selective fishing, is given no room is truly no longer justifiable. In short, let us offer our fishermen a perspective again with a policy that is realistic, workable, and future-proof.

(The speaker agrees to take a "blue card" question)

4-0073-0000.sourceText: I think we share the ambition that we want to have a lot of fish in the ocean and profitable fishermen. But how do you foresee that we will have more fish in the ocean and more profitable fishermen with fewer rules? Is that really something that you believe in? Because what we need is, in fact, a level playing field for all the fishermen, that all the fishermen abide by the same rules, and that we really get stocks back into a good shape.

4-0074-0000.sourceText: ��blauwe kaart”-antwoord. – Dank u wel voor deze mooie vraag. U vraagt naar de noodzaak van regels en of er geen behoefte is aan regels. Ik zou dit willen zeggen: regels zie ik eerst en vooral als gestold wantrouwen. En ik denk dat we weer terug moeten naar de gedachte dat we ook de ondernemer, de visser weer vertrouwen moeten geven. En dat betekent dus dat je moet durven snijden in bureaucratie, dat je moet durven snijden in regelgeving. Wat ik constateer, is dat we te maken hebben met diverse regels die juist contraproductief werken en die de duurzame visserij die we eigenlijk met zijn allen al willen, helemaal niet bevorderen. Denk aan zo'n aanlandplicht, die is gewoon contraproductief. Daar moeten we de discussie over aangaan.
4-0074-0000.englishText: Blue-card answer. – Thank you very much for this nice question. You are asking about the necessity of rules and whether there is a need for rules. I would like to say this: I see rules first and foremost as solidified mistrust. And I think we need to go back to the idea that we must also give trust back to the entrepreneur, to the fisherman. And that means that you must dare to cut red tape, that you must dare to cut regulations. What I observe is that we are dealing with various rules that actually work counterproductively and that do not promote sustainable fisheries at all, which we all actually want. Consider something like the landing obligation; that is simply counterproductive. We need to enter into a discussion about that.

4-0075-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, dos mensajes muy claros para el día de hoy.

El primero, con respecto al marco financiero plurianual: rechazamos absolutamente la centralización y la reducción de los fondos de pesca en esas dotaciones nacionales que, en nuestro caso, supondría que todo se decidiría desde Madrid. Tenemos un sector en Euskadi que merece ser escuchado desde la proximidad.

El segundo, con respecto a la política pesquera común: creemos que debe revisarse profundamente para hacer frente a los retos que tiene el sector y que ponen en serias dificultades su viabilidad en el futuro. Y hablamos de precios de la energía, relevo generacional, descarbonización de la flota, definición de capacidad pesquera, lucha contra la pesca ilegal y revisión de obligaciones de desembarque. Queremos simplificación administrativa —también para nuestros arrantzales— y queremos y necesitamos equilibrio entre los objetivos medioambientales, económicos y sociales. Y el informe que se presentaba en el mes de abril lo que hacía es evidenciar que existen deficiencias que debemos abordar cuanto antes.

Señor comisario, sabemos que usted tiene voluntad política para afrontarlos, pero es que el tiempo de reflexión ha finalizado y necesitamos actuar ya.

(La oradora acepta responder a una pregunta formulada con arreglo al procedimiento de la «tarjeta azul»)
4-0075-0000.englishText:
Mr President, two very clear messages for today.

The first, regarding the multiannual financial framework: we absolutely reject the centralization and reduction of fisheries funds in those national allocations, which, in our case, would mean everything being decided from Madrid. We have a sector in the Basque Country that deserves to be listened to from proximity.

The second, regarding the common fisheries policy: we believe it must be thoroughly revised to face the challenges the sector is experiencing, which are seriously jeopardizing its viability in the future. And we are talking about energy prices, generational replacement, fleet decarbonization, definition of fishing capacity, the fight against illegal fishing, and the review of landing obligations. We want administrative simplification —also for our fishers— and we want and need a balance between environmental, economic, and social objectives. And the report presented in the month of April demonstrated that there are shortcomings that we must address as soon as possible.

Mr Commissioner, we know that you have the political will to address them, but the time for reflection is over and we need to act now.

(The speaker agrees to take a blue-card question)

4-0076-0000.sourceText:
Usted, como yo, defiende aquí la pesca y defiende además a los pescadores, a las mariscadoras y también a las redeiras —que no sé cómo se dice en vasco, pero me lo dirá usted ahora—.

Nosotros consideramos que no se ha tenido en cuenta la sostenibilidad social en la política pesquera común. Por tanto, es algo que llevamos mucho tiempo reclamando al comisario, porque ha habido normas, decisiones —como las vedas—, en las que no se ha tenido en cuenta la sostenibilidad social.

Vemos cómo está ahora el sector del marisqueo, que está ahogado. Entonces, le quería preguntar: ¿qué opina sobre la inclusión de la sostenibilidad social?
4-0076-0000.englishText:
You, like me, defend fishing here and also defend fishermen, shellfish gatherers and also net makers - I do not know how it is said in Basque, but you will tell me now. 

We consider that social sustainability has not been taken into account in the common fisheries policy. Therefore, it is something that we have been demanding from the Commissioner for a long time, because there have been rules, decisions - such as fishing bans -, in which social sustainability has not been taken into account. 

We see how the shellfish sector is now, which is suffocated. So, I wanted to ask you: what is your opinion on the inclusion of social sustainability?

4-0077-0000.sourceText:
Creo que es algo que tenemos clarísimo quienes tenemos sector en nuestras regiones y naciones y quienes queremos defender tanto la sostenibilidad de los océanos como la sostenibilidad de la actividad económica y social, poniendo en valor también a las mujeres, que las mencionaba y que es importante reconocerlas también en este momento.

Y desde ahí trabajaremos y pelearemos de la mano, porque sabemos que, además, los arrantzales —el sector pesquero— son los primeros interesados en garantizar la viabilidad y el cuidado del océano, porque eso es lo que les garantiza el futuro realmente, de manera que eso es lo que creemos que tenemos que defender.
4-0077-0000.englishText:
I believe this is something very clear to those of us who have a sector in our regions and nations and those of us who want to defend both the sustainability of the oceans and the sustainability of economic and social activity, also valuing women, whom I mentioned and whom it is important to recognize at this time as well.

And from there we will work and fight hand in hand, because we know that, furthermore, the fishermen — the fishing sector — are the first interested in guaranteeing the viability and care of the ocean, because that is what truly guarantees their future, so that is what we believe we must defend.

4-0078-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, jaarlijks worden wereldwijd miljarden vissen uit zee gevangen en vervolgens weer overboord gegooid. Vissers gooien die vissen terug als ze te klein zijn, of domweg omdat ze te weinig geld opleveren. Meer dan 70 % van alle vissen die overboord worden gegooid, sterft daarna alsnog. Voor niets.

In 2015 heeft Europa daarom deze verspillende praktijk verboden. Maar nu, elf jaar later, worden ongewenste vissen in Europa nog steeds massaal overboord gegooid. In plaats van strenger te controleren op illegale praktijken, overweegt Europa nu om het wangedrag van deze visserij-industrie te belonen en het lozen van vissen waaraan weinig waarde wordt toegekend, maar weer toe te staan.

Een vis heeft de meeste waarde als hij gezond en wel in zee zwemt en daar het ecosysteem gezond houdt. Onze zeeën worden nog steeds ernstig overbevist. Bescherm onze zeeën en bescherm de strenge visserijregels. We hebben ze hard nodig.

(De spreker stemt ermee in om te antwoorden op een “blauwe kaart”-vraag)
4-0078-0000.englishText:
Mr President, every year, billions of fish are caught from the sea worldwide and then thrown overboard again. Fishermen throw those fish back if they are too small, or simply because they yield too little money. More than 70% of all fish thrown overboard still die afterwards. For nothing.

That is why Europe banned this wasteful practice in 2015. But now, eleven years later, unwanted fish are still being thrown overboard en masse in Europe. Instead of exercising stricter control over illegal practices, Europe is now considering rewarding the misconduct of this fishing industry and allowing the dumping of fish of low value to be permitted again.

A fish has the most value when it swims healthy and well in the sea and keeps the ecosystem healthy there. Our seas are still being seriously overfished. Protect our seas and protect the strict fisheries rules. We desperately need them.

(The speaker agrees to take a "blue card" question)

4-0079-0000.sourceText: ��blauwe kaart”-vraag. – Mevrouw Hazekamp, weer doet u het, weer viseert u onze duurzame Nederlandse en Europese visserij, die aan strenge regels moet voldoen en die selectiever wil vissen. Weer viseert u onze vissers. Hoe reflecteert u eigenlijk op uw erfenis in de afgelopen jaren en het feit dat u pleit voor nog strengere regels, nu de EU al voor 70 % afhankelijk is van visimport uit derde landen, waar — inderdaad, u heeft gelijk — niet altijd duurzaam wordt gevist. Maar waarom viseert u onze visserijsector? U zou trots moeten zijn op onze Europese en Nederlandse vissers.
4-0079-0000.englishText: Blue card question. - Mrs Hazekamp, once again you are doing it, once again you are targeting our sustainable Dutch and European fisheries, which have to comply with strict rules and want to fish more selectively. Once again you are targeting our fishermen. How do you actually reflect on your legacy over the past years and the fact that you are calling for even stricter rules, now that the EU is already 70% dependent on fish imports from third countries, where - indeed, you are right - fishing is not always sustainable. But why are you targeting our fishing sector? You should be proud of our European and Dutch fishermen.

4-0080-0000.sourceText: ��blauwe kaart”-antwoord. – Ja, die Nederlandse vissers. Laat ik daarbij wel voorop stellen dat die de grootste schepen ter wereld hebben, die in heel veel andere delen van de wereld schepen uit de hel worden genoemd en die inderdaad onder andere vlaggen varen, bijvoorbeeld die van Panama. En laten we niet vergeten dat van alle visserij, laten we kijken naar de Oostzee, daar leeft bijna geen kabeljauw meer. Middellandse Zee: meer dan de helft van de vissen wordt nog steeds overbevist. De Noordzee: schol en tong worden al decennia lang overbevist. Laten we elkaar nu gewoon even eerlijk de cijfers noemen en zeggen dat er iets moet veranderen.
4-0080-0000.englishText: Blue card" answer. – Yes, those Dutch fishermen. Let me first state that they have the largest ships in the world, which in many other parts of the world are called ships from hell and which indeed sail under other flags, for example that of Panama. And let us not forget that of all fisheries, let us look at the Baltic Sea, there is almost no cod left there. Mediterranean Sea: more than half of the fish are still being overfished. The North Sea: plaice and sole have been overfished for decades. Let us just give each other the figures honestly now and say that something has to change.

4-0081-0000.sourceText: Gospod predsednik, poštovani povjereniče Kadis, deset godina zajedničke ribarstvene politike jasno je pokazalo što našim ribarima danas treba, a to ste vidjeli prigodom obilaska Hrvatske, na čemu Vam zahvaljujem. Jednostavnija pravila, pravedni uvjeti na tržištu i manje administrativnog opterećenja. Kao izvjestiteljica za primjene pravila ribarstva u Sredozemlju, pozivam ponovo da se ribarima osigura više fleksibilnosti i pravila prilagođena stvarnim uvjetima na moru, posebno hrvatskim ribarima koji većinom love malim obalnim plovilima. Članstvo Hrvatske u Europskoj uniji donijelo je konkretne rezultate. Kroz europske fondove i politike modernizirana je flota, luke i akvakultura i osigurano je više od 700 milijuna eura potpore. Hrvatsko ribarstvo danas je otpornije, konkurentnije i održivije. Ali ribari moraju ostati u središtu europske ribarstvene politike. Govorimo o održivim radnim mjestima, opstanku naših obalnih zajednica i sigurnosti opskrbe hranom. Novi europski proračun zato mora pratiti ambicije koje stavljamo pred ovaj sektor. Od ribara ne možemo tražiti više ako im ne osiguramo odgovarajuću financijsku potporu. Samo politika koja istodobno štiti naše more i ljude koji od njega žive može osigurati budućnost europskog ribarstva.
4-0081-0000.englishText: Mr. President, esteemed Commissioner Kadis, ten years of the Common Fisheries Policy have clearly shown what our fishermen need today, which you saw during your visit to Croatia, for which I thank you. Simpler rules, fair market conditions, and less administrative burden. As rapporteur for the implementation of fisheries rules in the Mediterranean, I call once again to ensure more flexibility for fishermen and rules adapted to the actual conditions at sea, especially for Croatian fishermen who mostly fish with small coastal vessels. Croatia's membership in the European Union has brought concrete results. Through European funds and policies, the fleet, ports, and aquaculture have been modernized, and more than 700 million euros in support have been secured. Croatian fisheries today are more resilient, competitive, and sustainable. But fishermen must remain at the center of European fisheries policy. We are talking about sustainable jobs, the survival of our coastal communities, and food security. The new European budget must therefore match the ambitions we place before this sector. We cannot ask more from fishermen if we do not provide them with appropriate financial support. Only a policy that simultaneously protects our sea and the people who live from it can secure the future of European fisheries.

4-0082-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, Senhor Comissário, nos últimos anos, o setor das pescas europeu perdeu rentabilidade, a frota envelheceu e muitos armadores não conseguem investir na modernização, nem avançar com a melhoria de condições a bordo, essenciais para atrair novas gerações para este setor.

O Parlamento alertou, no seu relatório sobre a descarbonização e modernização das pescas, que o quadro atual restringe ou impede a ajuda pública, o que afasta o investimento privado e trava a renovação das frotas.

Tudo isto afeta, de forma desproporcional, pequenas comunidades que dependem do setor, como acontece na minha região: a Madeira.

Em termos de orçamento, é também incompreensível que a Comissão Europeia proponha uma redução de mais de 66 % da verba para o fundo dedicado às pescas no próximo quadro financeiro plurianual.

Se queremos ter um setor das pescas revitalizado e a contribuir decisivamente para o reforço da nossa autonomia estratégica, precisamos de ambição acompanhada de meios financeiros e instrumentos adequados.
4-0082-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, in recent years the European fisheries sector has lost profitability, the fleet has aged and many shipowners are unable to invest in modernization or to improve conditions on board, which are essential to attract new generations to this sector.

Parliament warned in its report on the decarbonization and modernization of fisheries that the current framework restricts or prevents public aid, which deters private investment and stalls fleet renewal.

All of this disproportionately affects small communities that depend on the sector, as is the case in my region: Madeira.

In terms of the budget, it is also incomprehensible that the European Commission should propose a reduction of more than 66% in the allocation for the fisheries fund in the next multiannual financial framework.

If we want to have a revitalized fisheries sector that contributes decisively to strengthening our strategic autonomy, we need ambition accompanied by financial resources and appropriate instruments.

4-0083-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señor comisario, la semana pasada embarqué en un barco de pescadores en Calpe, en una pequeña población del Mediterráneo. Me levanté de madrugada con ellos y vi cómo trabajan, cómo planifican cada lance, cómo controlan cada captura y cómo cumplen con unas normas cada vez más exigentes.

Salí de allí con una reflexión: nuestros pescadores no se sienten parte de la solución, se sienten permanentemente bajo sospecha. Llevan años haciendo sacrificios enormes y, sin embargo, cada año tienen menos días para faenar, más incertidumbre, más dificultades para mantener a flote sus empresas familiares y realmente piensan que la Unión Europea quiere acabar con el sector.

Mientras hablamos de sostenibilidad, muchos puertos desaparecen, muchos barcos también desaparecen, muchos empleos también desaparecen y, lo que es más preocupante, desaparecen los jóvenes que quieren continuar con esta profesión. Por eso, necesitamos que la sostenibilidad tenga tres pilares: el ambiental, el económico y el social. Y necesitamos una revisión profunda de la política pesquera común, una política que deje de medir únicamente toneladas y empiece a medir también personas, empleos y comunidades.
4-0083-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, last week I boarded a fishing boat in Calpe, a small Mediterranean town. I got up at dawn with them and saw how they work, how they plan each haul, how they monitor each catch and how they comply with increasingly demanding rules.

I left there with a reflection: our fishermen do not feel part of the solution, they feel permanently under suspicion. They have been making huge sacrifices for years and yet, every year they have fewer days to fish, more uncertainty, more difficulties in keeping their family businesses afloat and they genuinely think that the European Union wants to finish off the sector.
