While we talk about sustainability, many ports are disappearing, many boats are also disappearing, many jobs are also disappearing and, most worryingly, the young people who want to continue with this profession are disappearing. That is why we need sustainability to have three pillars: environmental, economic and social. And we need a deep review of the common fisheries policy, a policy that stops measuring only tons and also begins to measure people, jobs and communities.

4-0084-0000.sourceText:
Herr talman! När vi äntligen blir lediga och ska njuta av sol och bad, ja då får vi stanna på land. För Östersjöns algblomning sätter stopp och är ett tecken på hur illa det är. I decennier har Östersjön misshandlats och fungerat som slutstation för avlopp och utsläpp. Nu är dessutom Putins skuggflotta en tickande miljöbomb.

Fisken har betraktats som en resurs som aldrig tar slut, men nu är den akut hotad. Det vet vi, och att vi måste få en helt ny fiskeripolitik som bygger på verklighet och vetenskap, det vet alla. En bräckt skärgårdsvik i Roslagen är något helt annat än det salta, djupa Medelhavet, och vi måste anpassa politiken därefter. Vi måste få ett stopp på bottentrålningen.

Kommissionen måste utvärdera, men framför allt agera, och medlemsländerna måste börja ta ansvar.

(Talaren godtog en fråga ("blått kort").)
4-0084-0000.englishText:
Mr President! When we finally get time off and are to enjoy sun and swimming, well then we have to stay on land. Because the Baltic Sea's algal bloom puts a stop and is a sign of how bad things are. For decades, the Baltic Sea has been mistreated and functioned as the final station for sewage and emissions. Now, Putin's shadow fleet is also a ticking environmental bomb.

Fish has been regarded as a resource that never runs out, but now it is acutely threatened. We know that, and that we must get a completely new fisheries policy based on reality and science, everyone knows that. A brackish archipelago bay in Roslagen is something completely different from the salty, deep Mediterranean, and we must adapt the policy accordingly. We must put a stop to bottom trawling.

The Commission must evaluate, but above all act, and the member states must start taking responsibility.

(The speaker accepted a question ("blue card").)

4-0085-0000.sourceText: Jako poseł z Polski, kraju, który ma dostęp do Morza Bałtyckiego, chciałbym zapytać koleżankę, która reprezentuje również kraj, który ma dostęp do Morza Bałtyckiego, o politykę Unii Europejskiej wobec tego morza, a zwłaszcza politykę rybacką. Słuchając tutaj dyskusji koleżanek i kolegów z różnych krajów Unii Europejskiej, widzę, że wszyscy krytykują politykę Unii Europejskiej. Pytanie: dlaczego tak jest, że polityka Komisji Europejskiej, Unii Europejskiej jest przeciwko rybakom europejskim? Dlaczego ściągamy więcej ryb z krajów spoza Unii, a nie z krajów Unii?
4-0085-0000.englishText: As an MEP from Poland, a country that has access to the Baltic Sea, I would like to ask my female colleague, who also represents a country that has access to the Baltic Sea, about the European Union's policy towards this sea, and especially the fisheries policy. Listening to the discussions here of female and male colleagues from various countries of the European Union, I see that everyone is criticizing the European Union's policy. Question: why is it that the policy of the European Commission, of the European Union, is against European fishermen? Why do we import more fish from countries outside the Union rather than from Union countries?

4-0086-0000.sourceText:
Tack för din fråga, det här är någonting vi behöver debattera. Vi kan tycka olika om hur politiken ska utformas, men jag skulle önska att vi kunde enas kring ett gemensamt mål för Östersjön. Att det ska vara ett friskt och sunt innanhav och att vi har en politik som gör att våra fiskebestånd överlever till kommande generationer.

Så är det inte idag, och det finns inget land runt Östersjön som kan klara av att lösa det här stora problemet på egen hand. Därför måste vi samarbeta, och det är därför den här debatten är så viktig.
4-0086-0000.englishText:
Thank you for your question, this is something we need to debate. We may have different opinions on how policy should be formulated, but I would wish that we could agree on a common goal for the Baltic Sea: that it should be a healthy and sound inland sea and that we have a policy that ensures our fish stocks survive for future generations.

It is not like that today, and there is no country around the Baltic Sea that can manage to solve this major problem on its own. Therefore, we must cooperate, and that is why this debate is so important.

4-0087-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señor comisario, la evaluación de la PPC ofrece un diagnóstico acertado: flota extractiva en declive, acuicultura estancada e industria transformadora más próspera, pero no puedo compartir las conclusiones, demasiado autocomplacientes.

En mi opinión, señor comisario, la Comisión tendría que hacer dos cosas. En primer lugar, un ómnibus de simplificación para la pesca. Celebro su intención, señor comisario, de reformar el plan plurianual del Mediterráneo —es algo urgente que llevamos reclamando tiempo— y el FEMPA, pero no me parece suficiente. El ómnibus debe abordar como mínimo otros dos asuntos: la exclusión del palangre del Reglamento sobre aguas profundas y la revisión de algunos aspectos concretos del Reglamento de control, que se han demostrado de muy difícil —o incluso imposible— cumplimiento. Por ejemplo, el artículo 14, en lo relativo a la obligación de registrar las capturas desde el primer kilo. Además, el ómnibus debe presentarse cuanto antes. Los pescadores no pueden esperar más.

En segundo lugar, además del ómnibus, necesitamos una reforma de la PPC, que debe abordar los siguientes elementos: flexibilizar tanto la obligación de desembarque como la aplicación del rendimiento máximo sostenible. En segundo lugar, reformar el concepto de capacidad pesquera para permitir la descarbonización y la modernización de la flota, esenciales para el relevo generacional. También redefinir el concepto de pesca artesanal, para que no se base exclusivamente en la eslora. Y también introducir consideraciones socioeconómicas a la hora de fijar TAC y cuotas.

Señor comisario, es la hora de actuar, de tomar de una vez decisiones políticas. Usted mismo lo acaba de decir y es la Comisión la que tiene el monopolio de la iniciativa legislativa.
4-0087-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, the evaluation of the CFP offers an accurate diagnosis: a declining extractive fleet, stagnant aquaculture and a more prosperous processing industry, but I cannot share the conclusions, which are too self-complacent.

In my opinion, Commissioner, the Commission should do two things. First, a simplification omnibus for fisheries. I welcome your intention, Commissioner, to reform the multiannual management plan for the Mediterranean —something urgent that we have been demanding for a long time— and the EMFF, but it does not seem sufficient to me. The omnibus must address at least two other issues: the exclusion of longliners from the Deep-Sea Regulation and the revision of certain specific aspects of the Control Regulation, which have proven very difficult —or even impossible— to comply with. For example, Article 14, regarding the obligation to record catches from the first kilo. Furthermore, the omnibus must be presented as soon as possible. Fishermen cannot wait any longer.

Secondly, in addition to the omnibus, we need a reform of the CFP, which must address the following elements: making both the landing obligation and the application of maximum sustainable yield more flexible. Secondly, reforming the concept of fishing capacity to allow for the decarbonisation and modernisation of the fleet, which are essential for generational renewal. Also redefining the concept of small-scale coastal fishing, so that it is not based exclusively on length. And also introducing socioeconomic considerations when setting TACs and quotas.

Commissioner, it is time to act, to finally make political decisions. You yourself have just said it, and it is the Commission that has the monopoly on legislative initiative.

4-0088-0000.sourceText:
IN THE CHAIR: CHRISTEL SCHALDEMOSE

Vice-President

4-0089-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, την περασμένη εβδομάδα, και πιο συγκεκριμένα την Κυριακή, συναντήθηκα με εκπροσώπους των αλιέων στον Άγιο Ρέντη, στην Αττική. Μου ζήτησαν να σας μεταφέρω —και στην Ευρωπαϊκή Επιτροπή και σε σας προσωπικά— τη φωνή και την αγωνία τους· νομίζω ότι την ξέρετε αρκετά καλά. Μου μίλησαν για το υψηλό κόστος καυσίμων, τον γερασμένο στόλο, την ασφυκτική γραφειοκρατία, τη δυσκολία των νέων να μπουν στο επάγγελμα και τον αθέμιτο ανταγωνισμό, την παράνομη αλιεία από τρίτες χώρες και ειδικά από την Τουρκία, που δεν εφαρμόζει τους ίδιους κανόνες.

Η αξιολόγηση της Κοινής Αλιευτικής Πολιτικής δείχνει πρόοδο στη διαχείριση των ιχθυαποθεμάτων. Αυτό είναι σημαντικό, όμως η επιτυχία της δεν μπορεί να κρίνεται μόνο από τους περιβαλλοντικούς δείκτες. Πρέπει λοιπόν να κρίνεται και από το αν ένας επαγγελματίας αλιείας μπορεί να ζήσει με αξιοπρέπεια από αυτή τη δουλειά του και αν οι παράκτιες κοινότητες έχουν μέλλον.

Κύριε Επίτροπε, οι αλιείς δεν ζητούν προνόμια. Το λέμε και το ξαναλέμε. Ζητούν δίκαιους κανόνες, λιγότερη γραφειοκρατία, ουσιαστική στήριξη και ίσους όρους ανταγωνισμού. Γνωρίζω, κύριε Επίτροπε, την αξιόλογη, αξιολογότατη, δουλειά σας και θέλω να σταθείτε δίπλα στους ανθρώπους της θάλασσας με ουσιαστικές πρωτοβουλίες.
4-0089-0000.englishText:
Madam President, last week, and more specifically on Sunday, I met with representatives of fishermen in Agios Ioannis Rentis, in Attica. They asked me to convey to you—both to the European Commission and to you personally—their voice and their anguish; I think you know it quite well. They spoke to me about the high cost of fuel, the aging fleet, the suffocating bureaucracy, the difficulty for young people to enter the profession and unfair competition, illegal fishing from third countries and especially from Turkey, which does not apply the same rules.

The evaluation of the Common Fisheries Policy shows progress in stock management. This is important, but its success cannot be judged solely by environmental indicators. It must therefore also be judged by whether a professional fisherman can make a decent living from their work and whether coastal communities have a future.

Mr Commissioner, fishermen are not asking for privileges. We say it again and again. They are asking for fair rules, less bureaucracy, substantial support and a level playing field. I know, Mr Commissioner, your remarkable, highly remarkable work and I want you to stand by the people of the sea with substantive initiatives.

4-0090-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, de eigen evaluatie van de Commissie bevestigt wat onze vissers al jaren constateren: de aanlandplicht heeft gefaald. Gefaald. Ze heeft niet geleid tot meer selectiviteit. Als de regelgeving haar doelstellingen overduidelijk niet haalt, kan de oplossing niet bestaan uit betere uitvoering. Dan moeten de regels zelf worden herzien. Onze vissers vragen om oplossingen, niet om papierwerk.

De EU heeft behoefte aan een visserij-omnibus, herziening van de aanlandplicht, generatievernieuwing en realisme over de energietransitie. Europa is nu al voor 70 % van onze vis afhankelijk van import van buiten. Commissie, verdedigt u regels die aantoonbaar niet werken? Of heeft u eindelijk de moed om de concurrentiekracht van de sector te herstellen via een omnibus? Vissers rekenen op u.

(De spreker stemt ermee in om te antwoorden op een “blauwe kaart”-vraag)
4-0090-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the Commission's own evaluation confirms what our fishermen have been observing for years: the landing obligation has failed. Failed. It has not led to greater selectivity. If the legislation clearly fails to achieve its objectives, the solution cannot be better enforcement. Then the rules themselves must be revised. Our fishermen are asking for solutions, not paperwork.

The EU needs a fisheries omnibus, revision of the landing obligation, generational renewal and realism about the energy transition. Europe is already 70% dependent on imports from outside for our fish. Commission, do you defend rules that demonstrably do not work? Or do you finally have the courage to restore the sector's competitiveness via an omnibus? Fishermen are counting on you.

(The speaker agrees to take a "blue card" question)

4-0091-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Deputado, falou da questão da burocracia, falou da questão da dependência externa, e deixe-me dar-lhe dois exemplos claros.

Nos Açores, por liderança do Governo de José Manuel Bolieiro, definimos 300 000 quilómetros quadrados de áreas marinhas protegidas e estas compensações, através da mobilização de fundos privados e públicos, estão paradas na Comissão Europeia.

Na Madeira, temos financiamento público para a renovação das embarcações e, mais uma vez, estas decisões estão paradas na Comissão Europeia, não no Comissário das Pescas (sei que tudo tem feito), mas na estrutura da Comissão.

Como é que acha que nós podemos agilizar estes procedimentos?
4-0091-0000.englishText:
Mr. Member, you spoke about the issue of bureaucracy, you spoke about the issue of external dependence, and let me give you two clear examples.

In the Azores, under the leadership of José Manuel Bolieiro's Government, we defined 300,000 square kilometers of protected marine areas and these compensations, through the mobilization of private and public funds, are stalled in the European Commission.

In Madeira, we have public financing for the renewal of vessels and, once again, these decisions are stalled in the European Commission, not in the Commissioner for Fisheries (I know he has done everything), but in the Commission's structure.

How do you think we can streamline these procedures?

4-0092-0000.sourceText: ��blauwe kaart”-antwoord. – Ja, dat is een heel terecht punt van de heer do Nascimento Cabral. Ik denk dat ultraperifere regio's en gebieden absoluut steun verdienen in hun specifieke uitdagingen, en ik denk dat de Commissie als zodanig ook daarop moet reflecteren. De Europese Unie is niet alleen op het continent, maar ook op eilanden in overzeese gebiedsdelen, dus daarvoor ook de volle aandacht mijnerzijds. En ik hoop ook op dit vlak met u te kunnen samenwerken in de toekomst.
4-0092-0000.englishText: "blue card" answer. – Yes, that is a very valid point by Mr do Nascimento Cabral. I think that outermost regions and areas definitely deserve support in their specific challenges, and I think the Commission as such should also reflect on that. The European Union is not only on the continent, but also on islands in overseas territories, so they also have my full attention. And I also hope to be able to cooperate with you in this area in the future.

4-0093-0000.sourceText:
A Uachtaráin, a Choimisinéir, fáiltím roimh an meastóireacht seo ar an gComhbheartas Iascaigh. Ach cúis imní iad na torthaí seo, dáiríre, d'iascairí na hEorpa agus iascairí na hÉireann. Inbhuanaitheacht comhshaoil, ar ndóigh, fíorthábhachtach. Ach gan inbhuanaitheacht shóisialta agus eacnamaíoch, ní bheidh aon chosaint don chomhshaol ann.

Tá iascairí na hÉireann tar éis glacadh leis na cinntí deacra a bhí is atá rompu, dul in oiriúint dóibh agus beart a dhéanamh de réir a mbriathair. Ach mar sin féin, tá brú millteanach millteanach mór orthu le cuótaí, le méadú maorlathais, costais, éiginnteacht faoina dtodhchaí, agus an rud is measa ná an mbeidh báid fágtha don chéad ghlúin eile in Éirinn?

Bímis macánta, ní beartas rathúil iascaigh é beartas a laghdaíonn cabhlaigh, a bhaineann an bonn de ghnólachtaí agus a fholmhaíonn ár mbailte cósta. A Choimisinéir Kadis, iarraim ort ceithre rud a dhéanamh: Roghanna na Háige a chosaint, tacú le hathnuachan cabhlaigh, maorlathas a laghdú agus, uimhir a ceathair, cothrom na Féinne a chinntiú d'iascairí na hÉireann agus na hEorpa.

(Ghlac an cainteoir le ceist cárta ghoirm)
4-0093-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, I welcome this evaluation of the Common Fisheries Policy. But these results are genuinely a cause for concern for European fishers and Irish fishers. Environmental sustainability, of course, is of vital importance. But without social and economic sustainability, there will be no protection for the environment at all.

Irish fishers have accepted the difficult decisions that were and are before them, adapted to them, and walked the walk. But nevertheless, there is immense, immense pressure on them with quotas, increased bureaucracy, costs, uncertainty about their future, and worst of all, will there be boats left for the next generation in Ireland?

Let's be honest, a fisheries policy that reduces fleets, undermines businesses, and empties our coastal towns is not a successful policy. Commissioner Kadis, I ask you to do four things: protect the Hague Preferences, support fleet renewal, reduce bureaucracy, and, number four, ensure a fair deal for Irish and European fishers.

(The speaker agreed to take a blue-card question)

4-0094-0000.sourceText:
A Cynthia, tá ceist an-tábhachtach agam.

Eighty-seven percent of fishers in Ireland are small-scale fishers. There is nothing stopping the Irish state from giving small-scale, low-impact fishers access to more quota. Nothing stopping us.

There is nothing stopping the Irish state from providing small-scale fishers in Ireland with funding, front-loaded. But it isn't happening. And you can actually do it. So the question is: why don't you do that? Because they can't get this funding for their marketing plans – 87 % of the fishers and they have less than 10 % of the quota...

(The President cut off the speaker)
4-0094-0000.englishText:
Cynthia, I have a very important question.

Eighty-seven percent of fishers in Ireland are small-scale fishers. There is nothing stopping the Irish state from giving small-scale, low-impact fishers access to more quota. Nothing stopping us.

There is nothing stopping the Irish state from providing small-scale fishers in Ireland with funding, front-loaded. But it isn't happening. And you can actually do it. So the question is: why don't you do that? Because they can't get this funding for their marketing plans – 87 % of the fishers and they have less than 10 % of the quota...

(The President cut off the speaker)

4-0096-0000.sourceText:
'Ní neart go cur le chéile.' 'Unity with strength.' As you know, Mr Ming Flanagan, that is mana Uachtaránacht na hÉireann. All of our fishers are being looked after by Minister Timmy Dooley – my government, Fianna Fáil, who is now leading out on the Council of the EU. Rest assured, all efforts are being made.

All work is being done go dian dícheallach ar son gach iascaire in Éirinn. Ní hamháin na hiascairí móra ach na hiascairí beaga chomh maith.
4-0096-0000.englishText:
There is no strength without unity. Unity with strength. As you know, Mr Ming Flanagan, that is mana Uachtaránacht na hÉireann. All of our fishers are being looked after by Minister Timmy Dooley – my government, Fianna Fáil, who is now leading out on the Council of the EU. Rest assured, all efforts are being made.

All work is being done diligently on behalf of every fisher in Ireland. Not only the large fishers but the small fishers as well.

4-0098-0000.sourceText:
Fru talman! Herr kommissionär! Jag vill börja med att tacka kommissionen för utvärderingen. En hållbar och konkurrenskraftig fiskesektor är avgörande för Sveriges och Europas beredskap och för vår livsmedelssäkerhet.

Varje hav är unikt. Det är inte något som ett enskilt land kan hantera på egen hand. Haven tillhör oss alla och därför krävs samarbete för att förvalta dem. Här spelar EU en viktig roll, men även länder utanför EU påverkar våra hav. När vi utvecklar framtidens fiskepolitik behöver vi också se konsekvenserna av andra länders agerande.

Det innebär bland annat att vi måste arbeta aktivt med regionala fiskeorganisationer, men också att vi måste vara beredda att använda hårdare verktyg mot länder som inte respekterar internationella regler.

I Östersjön gäller det särskilt Ryssland. Ryssland fiskar i dag inte på ett hållbart sätt, och den ryska skuggflottan fortsätter att utsätta oss och Östersjön för risker. Det här behöver framtidens havs- och fiskepolitik räkna med. Vi måste sätta stopp för att haven fyller den ryska krigskassan. Vår säkerhet och våra hav är förenade.

Ett livskraftigt och säkert Östersjön är en förutsättning för ett säkert Europa.

(Talaren godtog en fråga ("blått kort").)
4-0098-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mr Commissioner, I want to start by thanking the Commission for its evaluation. A sustainable and competitive fisheries sector is crucial for Sweden's and Europe's preparedness and for our food security.

Every sea is unique. That is not something an individual country can handle on its own. The seas belong to us all, and therefore cooperation is required to manage them. The EU plays an important role here, but countries outside the EU also affect our seas. When we develop the fisheries policy of the future, we also need to see the consequences of other countries' actions.

This means, among other things, that we must work actively with regional fisheries organisations, but also that we must be prepared to use tougher tools against countries that do not respect international rules.

In the Baltic Sea, this particularly applies to Russia. Russia is currently not fishing in a sustainable way, and the Russian shadow fleet continues to expose us and the Baltic Sea to risks. The maritime and fisheries policy of the future needs to take this into account. We must put a stop to the seas filling the Russian war chest. Our security and our seas are united.

A viable and secure Baltic Sea is a prerequisite for a secure Europe.

(The speaker accepted a question ("blue card").)

4-0099-0000.sourceText: Gerbiama pranešėja, Lietuva ribojasi su Baltijos jūra ir su Kuršių mariomis, kartu su Rusija. Ar jums neatrodo keista, kad, remiantis Europos Sąjungos reikalavimais, Lietuva uždraudė pramoninę žvejybą, o šalia Rusija tos žvejybos neuždraudė? Aš, būdamas Parlamento narys, negalėjau remti tokio kvailo įstatymo, nes žuvys iš Lietuvos patenka į Rusiją. Rusija gaudo, žvejoja, o Lietuva negali žvejoti tų žuvų. Kaip vertinate šitokį, sakyčiau, gana kvailą sprendimą?
4-0099-0000.englishText: Respected speaker, Lithuania borders the Baltic Sea and the Curonian Lagoon, together with Russia. Does it not seem strange to you that, based on European Union requirements, Lithuania banned industrial fishing, while nearby Russia did not ban that fishing? I, as a Member of Parliament, could not support such a stupid law, because the fish from Lithuania end up in Russia. Russia catches, fishes, and Lithuania cannot fish for those fish. How do you assess such a, I would say, rather stupid decision?

4-0100-0000.sourceText:
Tack för frågan. Ja, jag tror att vi är ense om just det här. Det var just det jag också påpekade i mitt tal, det vill säga att länderna runt Östersjön måste se till vad vi behöver göra, och det kan inte utnyttjas av till exempel Ryssland.

Därför måste vi fortsätta vidta sanktioner och se till att vi inte göder den ryska krigskassan utifrån vad Östersjön kan erbjuda i form av transport och fiske.
4-0100-0000.englishText:
Thank you for the question. Yes, I believe we agree on precisely this. That was precisely what I also pointed out in my speech, namely that the countries around the Baltic Sea must consider what we need to do, and it cannot be exploited by, for example, Russia.

Therefore, we must continue to implement sanctions and ensure that we do not fuel the Russian war chest based on what the Baltic Sea can offer in terms of transport and fishing.

4-0101-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, quel avenir pour la politique commune de la pêche si nous oublions le marché? Décarbonation, renouvellement des générations, adaptation au changement climatique: toutes ces ambitions resteront des promesses si nos pêcheurs sont victimes d’une concurrence déloyale.

Aujourd’hui, des produits importés qui ne respectent ni nos normes environnementales, ni nos exigences sociales, parfois même issus de la pêche illégale, concurrencent ceux de nos professionnels. La concurrence régulée, oui; le dumping, non!

Les solutions sont connues: renforcer les contrôles aux frontières, imposer le respect de nos normes minimales pour accéder au marché européen, mieux informer les consommateurs et promouvoir nos produits. L’Europe ne peut pas être exigeante avec ses pêcheurs et indulgente avec leurs concurrents. Pour une filière jeune, innovante et durable, soyons enfin cohérents. Protéger notre marché, c’est aussi protéger notre avenir.
4-0101-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, what future for the common fisheries policy if we forget the market? Decarbonisation, generational renewal, adaptation to climate change: all these ambitions will remain promises if our fishermen are victims of unfair competition.

Today, imported products that respect neither our environmental standards nor our social requirements, sometimes even coming from illegal fishing, compete with those of our professionals. Regulated competition, yes; dumping, no!

The solutions are known: strengthen border controls, impose compliance with our minimum standards to gain access to the European market, better inform consumers and promote our products. Europe cannot be demanding with its fishermen and indulgent with their competitors. For a young, innovative and sustainable sector, let us finally be coherent. Protecting our market also means protecting our future.

4-0102-0000.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, Euroopan unionin pohjoisimpana parlamentaarikkona tuon teille nyt terveiset Atlantin luonnonlohen kutujoelta. Tämä on todella kriittinen asia. Olen kasvanut tuon Euroopan suurimman lohijoen, Tornionjoen, varrella, enkä vähättele yhtään kalateollisuuden enkä ammattikalastajien näkökulmaa, mutta lohikannat ovat niin hälyttävällä tasolla, että jos Itämerellä lohenkalastusta ei rajoiteta, niin minun elinaikanani edessä saattaa olla todella ympäristöllinen katastrofi ja näemme Atlantin luonnonlohen sukupuuton.

Jos näin käy, niin silloin kalaa ei kalasteta yhtään missään muuallakaan, ei etelämmässä, jos lohi ei pääse nousemaan pohjoisen kutujokiin. Siksi tämä on niin suuri kysymys, koska kysymyksessä on siis todella ympäristöllinen katastrofi, jos luonnonlohet eivät pääse nousemaan näihin pohjoisiin jokiin monista eri syistä – on tehty patoja, on kalastettu liikaa. Ja nyt me täällä debatoimme ajasta toiseen siitä, onko kalastettu liikaa vai liian vähän. Me tiedämme, että kalakannat ovat romahtaneet, joten vetoan teihin Atlantin luonnonlohen puolesta.
4-0102-0000.englishText:
Mr President, as the European Union's northernmost parliamentarian, I bring you greetings from the spawning river of the Atlantic wild salmon. This is a truly critical matter. I have grown up along that European largest salmon river, the Torne River, and I do not downplay the perspective of the fishing industry nor professional fishermen at all, but salmon stocks are at such an alarming level that if salmon fishing in the Baltic Sea is not restricted, an environmental catastrophe may lie ahead in my lifetime and we will see the extinction of the Atlantic wild salmon.

If this happens, then fish will not be caught anywhere else either, not further south, if the salmon cannot ascend to the northern spawning rivers. That is why this is such a big issue, because it is truly an environmental catastrophe if wild salmon cannot ascend to these northern rivers for many different reasons – dams have been built, there has been overfishing. And now we here debate time and time again whether there has been too much or too little fishing. We know that fish stocks have collapsed, so I appeal to you on behalf of the Atlantic wild salmon.

4-0103-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, αξιότιμε κύριε Επίτροπε, είναι ξεκάθαρο ότι η Κοινή Αλιευτική Πολιτική είναι αναγκαία για να προστατεύσει τα ιχθυαποθέματα και να διασφαλίσει ένα βιώσιμο μέλλον για την αλιεία. Ωστόσο, οφείλουμε να αναρωτηθούμε γιατί τόσοι πολλοί αλιείς αισθάνονται ότι αυτή η πολιτική λειτουργεί εις βάρος τους, γιατί ο κλάδος παρακμάζει. Η προστασία του περιβάλλοντος και των ειδών προς εξαφάνιση δεν μπορεί να θεωρείται πιο σημαντική από την επιβίωση των ψαράδων μας. Οι αυστηροί περιορισμοί σε συνδυασμό με το διαρκώς αυξημένο ενεργειακό κόστος και τη ραγδαία εξάπλωση των ξενικών ειδών πιέζουν ασφυκτικά τα εισοδήματά τους.

Κύριε Επίτροπε, γνωρίζετε πολύ καλά τη σημασία που έχει η αλιεία για τις παράκτιες και νησιωτικές κοινωνίες της Μεσογείου. Για πολλές από αυτές αποτελεί τη μοναδική πηγή εισοδήματος. Αν λοιπόν θέλουμε να διατηρήσουμε ζωντανές τις θάλασσές μας, πρέπει να προστατεύσουμε και τους ανθρώπους που αφιερώνουν τη ζωή τους σε αυτές. Το πραγματικά απειλούμενο είδος σήμερα είναι οι ίδιοι οι αλιείς.
4-0103-0000.englishText:
Madam President, honorable Commissioner, it is clear that the Common Fisheries Policy is necessary to protect fish stocks and ensure a sustainable future for fishing. However, we must ask ourselves why so many fishermen feel that this policy works against them, why the sector is in decline. Environmental protection and endangered species cannot be considered more important than the survival of our fishermen. Strict restrictions combined with constantly increasing energy costs and the rapid spread of alien species are suffocatingly pressing their incomes.

Commissioner, you know very well the importance that fishing has for the coastal and island communities of the Mediterranean. For many of them it is the sole source of income. If therefore we want to keep our seas alive, we must also protect the people who dedicate their lives to them. The truly endangered species today are the fishermen themselves.

4-0104-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta señor comisario, los desafíos nos obligan a mirar al futuro y la política pesquera común diseñada hace más de una década necesita actualizarse.

Los arrantzales vascos esperan respuestas de Europa y, sin embargo, hoy tenemos una política desfasada e infrafinanciada. No se trata de empezar de cero. La política pesquera común ha impulsado una pesca más sostenible, ha mejorado la gestión con criterios científicos y ha reforzado el control y la gobernanza internacional, y esto hay que preservarlo. Pero nos quedan retos: una aplicación eficaz de las normas, renovación de la flota, falta de relevo generacional y pérdida de rentabilidad de muchas comunidades costeras.

Sostenibilidad y rentabilidad son dos caras de la misma moneda. La política pesquera común ha recuperado los recursos, pero ahora debe centrarse en la viabilidad económica y en el futuro de las comunidades costeras. Europa debe reconocer la pesca como sector estratégico y tiene que dotarla de recursos y reducir las cargas administrativas innecesarias.

Pero simplificar no puede significar debilitar los objetivos ambientales y sociales de la política pesquera común. Necesitamos más presupuesto, no menos, señor comisario.
4-0104-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, challenges force us to look to the future, and the Common Fisheries Policy designed more than a decade ago needs to be updated.

Basque fishermen are waiting for answers from Europe, and yet today we have an outdated and underfunded policy. It is not a matter of starting from scratch. The Common Fisheries Policy has promoted more sustainable fishing, improved management with scientific criteria, and strengthened international control and governance, and this must be preserved. But challenges remain for us: effective enforcement of the rules, fleet renewal, lack of generational handover, and loss of profitability in many coastal communities.

Sustainability and profitability are two sides of the same coin. The Common Fisheries Policy has recovered resources, but now it must focus on economic viability and the future of coastal communities. Europe must recognize fishing as a strategic sector and must provide it with resources and reduce unnecessary administrative burdens.

But simplifying cannot mean weakening the environmental and social objectives of the Common Fisheries Policy. We need more budget, not less, Commissioner.

4-0105-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, fairness and burden‑sharing should be at the heart of the common fisheries policy, if we were truly to live in a European Union where we try to treat all citizens and all sectors fairly. But, Commissioner, there has been an unfair burden placed on the Irish fishing communities: a 23 % decrease in direct gross value added and a 15 % drop in numbers employed over the last number of years. We have 12 % of the waters, but we catch less than 4 % of the fish. And at the same time, in the North East Atlantic Fisheries Commission, Russia, Norway, Faro, Greenland, Iceland and the UK continue to fish in an unsustainable way. Migratory patterns of fish species are changing dramatically due to global warming and temperature rises and seas, and yet there has been no solid review of quota allocation and new quota allocation because of changing fishing patterns. For example, bluefin tuna off the coast of Ireland is now very prevalent – something we would not have seen 50 years ago.

So, Commissioner, in doing the evaluation, we also have to look at a review to make sure that we have sustainable fishing in all parts of the European Union, not on sustainable fishing in the North East Atlantic and undermining fishing stocks in Irish waters.

4-0106-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Pochodzę z Darłowa. To jest takie niewielkie miasteczko nad Morzem Bałtyckim. Obok mamy Dąbki, potem mamy Mielno, Dźwirzyno, Kołobrzeg, Świnoujście. To są miasteczka, miasta i wioski nad polskim morzem i ja tam robię spotkania z ludźmi.

Na każdym z tych spotkań spotykam setki – jeśli nie tysiące – byłych rybaków i ich rodzin, którzy musieli sprzedać albo zezłomować swoje kutry w ramach kwot, które narzuca Unia Europejska. Ci ludzie pewnie nie byliby przeciw i rozumieją konieczność ekologii i ochrony środowiska, walki o kwoty ryb i tak dalej, gdyby nie to, że wzdłuż tych plaż w tych miejscowościach powstały setki dymiących palonym olejem smażalni ryb, w których właściciele tych samych smażalni ryb kupują dokładnie te same ryby z tego samego morza, zamrożone, od dostawców spoza Unii Europejskiej za cztery razy wyższą cenę, często pod ruską banderą.

Ja jestem lekarzem i wiem jedną rzecz: że jak człowiek sobie wmawia nieprawdę, kiedy jest chory, i udaje, że się leczy, to to się musi źle skończyć.
4-0106-0000.englishText:
Madam President! I come from Darłowo. This is a small town on the Baltic Sea. Next to us we have Dąbki, then we have Mielno, Dźwirzyno, Kołobrzeg, Świnoujście. These are towns, cities and villages by the Polish sea and I hold meetings with people there.

At each of these meetings, I meet hundreds – if not thousands – of former fishermen and their families who had to sell or scrap their cutters as part of the quotas imposed by the European Union. These people probably wouldn't be against it and understand the need for ecology and environmental protection, the fight for fishing quotas and so on, if it weren't for the fact that along these beaches in these towns, hundreds of fish fryers smoking with burnt oil have been built, where the owners of these same fish fryers buy the exact same fish from the exact same sea, frozen, from suppliers outside the European Union at four times the higher price, often under the Russian flag.

I am a doctor and I know one thing: that when a person convinces themselves of an untruth when they are sick, and pretends to be treating themselves, it must end badly.

4-0107-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señor comisario, creo que la política pesquera común debe adaptarse pero manteniendo sus principios fundamentales, porque la Comisión concluye en su evaluación que muchos de los problemas actuales no se deben a falta de legislación, sino a una aplicación —dice— insuficiente y desigual.

Un ejemplo son las áreas marinas protegidas. La legislación permite adoptar medidas de conservación —por cierto, también sobre la pesca de arrastre—. Pero demasiadas veces esas decisiones se bloquean o se retrasan durante años. Por eso, la Ley de Restauración de la Naturaleza refuerza el procedimiento, fija plazos claros para las recomendaciones conjuntas y da a la Comisión más capacidad para actuar cuando no hay acuerdos.

Por tanto, el camino es la aplicación, más cooperación y más decisiones basadas en la ciencia. La futura Ley del Océano debe servir para reforzar este marco, pero no para debilitarlo.

Señorías, si no tenemos mares sanos no habrá pesca sostenible ni tampoco futuro para nuestros pescadores.
4-0107-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mr Commissioner, I believe that the common fisheries policy must be adapted while maintaining its fundamental principles, because the Commission concludes in its evaluation that many of the current problems are not due to a lack of legislation, but rather to insufficient and uneven implementation, as it says.

An example is marine protected areas. The legislation allows conservation measures to be adopted—incidentally, also regarding bottom trawling—. But too often these decisions are blocked or delayed for years. Therefore, the Nature Restoration Law reinforces the procedure, sets clear deadlines for joint recommendations, and gives the Commission more capacity to act when there are no agreements.

Therefore, the way forward is implementation, more cooperation, and more science-based decisions. The future Ocean Law must serve to reinforce this framework, not to weaken it.

Ladies and gentlemen, if we do not have healthy seas there will be no sustainable fishing nor any future for our fishermen.

4-0108-0000.sourceText:
Fru talman! Tack för ordet. Ungefär 1,1 miljoner svenskar fiskade på sin fritid förra året. De spenderade över 9 miljarder kr på spön, fiskekort och drag. På båtar, flytvästar och guidade turer.

Men sportfiske är ju större än så. Det är ett barns glädjetjut när abborrn nappar för första gången. Det är fiskevårdsföreningar som tar hand om sjöar och tjärnar. Det är eldsjälar som inkluderar fler. Lokalsamhällen som får besökare. Det är generation på generation som lär sig om livet i vattnet.

Och ändå, när EU talar om fisket blir sportfisket nästan alltid bortglömt. Osynliggjort. Det lär vi ändra på. Sportfiske borde vara en given del av den gemensamma fiskeripolitiken. Jag tror att det skulle kunna leda till fler jobb på mindre orter, fler barn och unga som tar del av naturen och en bättre ekonomi för vårt fritidsfiske.
4-0108-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Thank you for the floor. Approximately 1.1 million Swedes fished in their spare time last year. They spent over 9 billion SEK on rods, fishing permits, and lures. On boats, life jackets, and guided tours.

But sport fishing is bigger than that. It is a child's shout of joy when a perch bites for the first time. It is fisheries conservation associations that take care of lakes and tarns. It is enthusiasts who include more people. Local communities that receive visitors. It is generation upon generation learning about life in the water.

And yet, when the EU talks about fishing, sport fishing is almost always forgotten. Made invisible. We need to change that. Sport fishing should be a given part of the Common Fisheries Policy. I believe that could lead to more jobs in smaller localities, more children and young people experiencing nature, and a better economy for our recreational fishing.

4-0110-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señor comisario, la propia evaluación de la Comisión dibuja un panorama preocupante para la pesca europea. Reconoce la caída de los desembarques, el deterioro de la rentabilidad, el envejecimiento de la flota, la pérdida de empleo, el aumento de la dependencia de las importaciones y el deterioro de la competitividad de nuestro sector.

Sin embargo, pese a todas estas constataciones, la conclusión política de la Comisión sigue siendo la misma: no hace falta reformar la política pesquera común y basta con aplicarla plenamente. Ahí reside la principal contradicción de esta evaluación. En lugar de preguntarse si alguna de las decisiones adoptadas en 2013 debe revisarse, la Comisión vuelve a atribuir las dificultades a los Estados miembros y al propio sector.

Señor comisario, si los problemas de aplicación son persistentes y generalizados en toda la Unión, ¿no cree que, quizá, el problema no sea solo de aplicación, sino también el propio diseño de la política pesquera común? ¿Está la Comisión realmente dispuesta a revisar algunos de los pilares de la reforma de 2013, como la inflexible prohibición de los descartes, la aplicación rígida del rendimiento máximo sostenible o las normas sobre la capacidad pesquera?
4-0110-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, the Commission's own assessment paints a worrying picture for European fisheries. It acknowledges the drop in landings, the deterioration in profitability, the ageing of the fleet, the loss of jobs, the increase in dependence on imports, and the deterioration in the competitiveness of our sector.

However, despite all these findings, the Commission's political conclusion remains the same: there is no need to reform the common fisheries policy and it is enough to fully implement it. Therein lies the main contradiction of this assessment. Instead of asking whether any of the decisions adopted in 2013 should be revised, the Commission once again blames the difficulties on the Member States and the sector itself.

Commissioner, if the implementation problems are persistent and widespread throughout the Union, do you not think that perhaps the problem is not only implementation, but also the very design of the common fisheries policy? Is the Commission really willing to revise some of the pillars of the 2013 reform, such as the inflexible discards ban, the rigid application of maximum sustainable yield or the rules on fishing capacity?

4-0111-0000.sourceText: Madam President, during a working visit to the fisheries last week, it became clear once again that the sector is struggling significantly with the landing obligation and associated camera monitoring. The fisheries do have more challenges, but the most urgent to solve is the landing obligation. In practice, the landing obligation is simply unworkable. When can we expect an opportunity to adjust this regulation? Commissioner, can this be placed on the agenda as soon as possible?

4-0112-0000.sourceText: Gerbiama Pirmininke, gerbiamas komisare. Dėkoju už iš tikrųjų labai dalykiškai pristatytą bendrosios žuvininkystės politikos apžvalgą. Aš gerai atsimenu Jūsų pirmtaką Karmenu Vellą – jis buvo atsakingas iš Maltos komisaras, buvo atsakingas už bendrą žuvininkystės politiką ir kėlė tuos pačius klausimus, kuriuos dabar mano kolega Bajada kelia dėl trečiųjų šalių žvejybos problemų Viduržemio jūroje ir kitose jūrose. Visiškai suprantama, kad mes turime labai daug dėmesio skirti santykiams tarp Europos Sąjungos ir trečiųjų šalių – ar tai Baltijos jūroje, ar Viduržemio jūroje, ar kitur. Juk mes gauname importo iš žuvininkystės labai daug ir tuo pačiu trečiosios šalys labai eksploatuoja žuvų kaimenes ir iš tiesų kelia daug problemų. Ir čia turėtų būti labai didelis dėmesys, kad šiame tarptautiniame aspekte bendroji žuvininkystės politika Europos Sąjungoje būtų dar labiau pažangesnė ir kartu tvirtesnė. Mums reikia aktyvių veiksmų.
4-0112-0000.englishText: Madam President, dear Commissioner. Thank you for a truly very substantive presentation of the review of the Common Fisheries Policy. I remember well your predecessor Karmenu Vella – he was the Commissioner responsible from Malta, responsible for the common fisheries policy, and he raised the same issues that my colleague Bajada is now raising regarding third-country fishing problems in the Mediterranean and other seas. It is completely understandable that we must pay a lot of attention to the relations between the European Union and third countries – whether in the Baltic Sea, the Mediterranean, or elsewhere. After all, we receive a very large amount of imports from fisheries, and at the same time, third countries heavily exploit fish stocks and indeed cause many problems. And there should be a very high focus here so that in this international aspect, the common fisheries policy in the European Union would be even more progressive and at the same time stronger. We need active action.

4-0113-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señor comisario, de las consideraciones de esta evaluación de la política pesquera me quedo con las que hacen referencia a las regiones ultraperiféricas, como Canarias, donde la pesca artesanal es una contribución no solamente a la economía o al empleo, sino, sobre todo, a la cultura, además de a la sostenibilidad y hasta a la propia soberanía alimentaria.

Pero la pesca artesanal requiere respuestas que escuchen no solamente al sector, sino a las autoridades locales y regionales, que tienen demandas muy fundadas en relación con la sobrecarga que suponen las obligaciones de desembarco anticipado y, sobre todo, el cuaderno digital. Son obligaciones que resultan desproporcionadas para lo que representa la pesca artesanal y, desde luego, además requieren apoyo financiero en el próximo marco financiero plurianual.

Se ha dicho con claridad y suscribo el mensaje. Es inaceptable la fusión de la política pesquera en sobres nacionales que obligue a las regiones ultraperiféricas a competir con otras regiones ignorando su singularidad jurídica. Debe haber una dotación financiera necesaria para apoyar al sector y su sostenibilidad.
4-0113-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, from the considerations in this evaluation of the fisheries policy, I take note of those referring to the outermost regions, such as the Canary Islands, where artisanal fishing is not only a contribution to the economy or employment, but above all to culture, as well as to sustainability and even food sovereignty itself.

However, artisanal fishing requires responses that listen not only to the sector, but also to local and regional authorities, who have very well-founded demands regarding the burden imposed by early landing obligations and, above all, the electronic logbook. These obligations are disproportionate to what artisanal fishing represents and, of course, they also require financial support in the next multiannual financial framework.

It has been clearly stated, and I subscribe to the message. The merger of fisheries policy into national envelopes that forces the outermost regions to compete with other regions, ignoring their legal singularity, is unacceptable. There must be the necessary financial allocation to support the sector and its sustainability.

4-0114-0000.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, vihreä suojeluaate merimetsojen ja valkoposkihanhien kohdalla on saanut suurta vahinkoa aiheuttavat mittasuhteet. Kuvitelkaa saaristossa elävä kalastaja, joka varhain aamulla vetää verkot vesiltä vain huomatakseen, ettei saalista ole. Merimetsokannat ovat räjähtäneet käsiin ja ne nokkivat tuhoa kalakantoihin ja koko elinkeinon kannattavuuteen. Maataloudessa sen sijaan valtavat valkoposkihanhilaumat parturoivat peltoja kynittyyn kuntoon.

Sekä merimetso että valkoposkihanhi ovat rauhoitettuja EU:n lintudirektiivin turvin. Molemmat ovat elinvoimaisia lajeja ja ovat vieläpä runsastuneet viime vuosina huomattavasti. Jos EU:lta puuttuu järki, Suomen hallitukselta sitä löytyy. Suomen hallitus ajaa molempien lajien EU-suojelun alentamista. Tämä ei ole vihreä linja, tämä on tolkun linja.
4-0114-0000.englishText:
Mr Speaker, the green conservation ideology regarding cormorants and barnacle geese has reached proportions that cause massive damage. Imagine a fisherman living in the archipelago who early in the morning pulls his nets from the water only to find there is no catch. Cormorant populations have exploded and they peck and destroy fish stocks and the profitability of the entire livelihood. In agriculture, on the other hand, huge flocks of barnacle geese graze fields down to a barren state.

Both the cormorant and the barnacle geese are protected under the EU Birds Directive. Both are viable species and have even increased significantly in recent years. If the EU lacks common sense, the Finnish government has it. The Finnish government is pushing to lower the EU protection status of both species. This is not a green line, this is a line of reason.

4-0115-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, Commissioner, this planned reform of common fisheries policy is not just a test for fisheries, in my mind. It is a test for fairness and trust in Europe.

As a result of Brexit, Irish fishermen lost quota, and boats were decommissioned. And then last December, when Ireland needed help, the long‑established Hague preferences – that safeguard meant to protect us in a quota crisis – were blocked by a minority group of other Member States. Now we hear reports of fisheries flexibility for Iceland, ahead of their referendum on 29 August.

Now let's be straight. Ireland is not against Iceland. We support sustainable fishing, science and a strong North Atlantic. But do not tell Irish fishermen that rules are fixed and then go and bend them for somebody else. Any deal must be open, fair and not at Ireland's expense.

Commissioner, this matter matters for all future accessions. Europe cannot attract countries in with flexibility, then leave existing Member States frozen into unfairness.

4-0116-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Senhor Comissário responsável pelas Pescas e pelos Oceanos, como eurodeputada galega, se perguntar a um marinheiro, a uma mariscadora do meu país, vai dizer que a PCP nos afundou. Precisamos de uma reforma da PCP urgente.

Mas hoje, Senhor Comissário, vou falar-lhe de um tema da atualidade que no meu país está a ter muita repercussão. Há muitos anos que houve 222 000 tambores de resíduos radioativos nucleares despejados na fossa atlântica. O instituto francês CNRS foi vê-los à fossa atlântica e investigar esse lixo radioativo e esses tambores de resíduos radioativos despejados.

Eu pergunto: como é que esta situação pode ser considerada compatível com o objetivo de proteger a saúde, a sustentabilidade e a segurança dos nossos oceanos, das zonas de pesca e das comunidades costeiras.

Vai começar a avaliar as potenciais implicações destas descobertas para as pescas europeias e a segurança no mar?
4-0116-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner responsible for Fisheries and Oceans, as a Galician MEP, if you ask a sailor, a shellfish gatherer from my country, they will say that the CFP sank us. We urgently need a reform of the CFP.

But today, Commissioner, I am going to talk to you about a current topic that is having a lot of repercussion in my country. Many years ago, there were 222,000 drums of nuclear radioactive waste dumped in the Atlantic trench. The French CNRS institute went to see them in the Atlantic trench and investigate this radioactive waste and these dumped radioactive waste drums.

I ask: how can this situation be considered compatible with the objective of protecting the health, sustainability and safety of our oceans, fishing areas and coastal communities?

Will you begin to assess the potential implications of these discoveries for European fisheries and safety at sea?

4-0117-0000.sourceText: Gerbiama Pirmininke, gerbiamas komisare. Čia tikrai nemažai išsakė parlamentarai problemų, susijusių su žuvininkyste. Aš jau minėjau – Lietuva ribojasi Baltijos jūroje ir Kuršių mariose su Rusija. 2023 m. Lietuva uždraudė verslinę žuvininkystę, kuo labai džiaugiasi Rusija. Dar to negana – daugelio mūsų žvejų pareikalavo, kad jie supjaustytų laivus. Žinoma, davė kompensaciją iš Europos Sąjungos. Tam, reikia tai suprasti logiškai, kad pagerintų Rusijos žvejų išteklius. Kaip vertinate šią politiką? Ir ar jūs nežadate peržiūrėti savo žuvininkystės politikos, kuri labai nenaudinga Europos Sąjungos šalims, taip pat ir mūsų valstybei Lietuvai? Apie tai kalba beveik kiekvienas europarlamentaras.
4-0117-0000.englishText: Madam President, dear Commissioner. The members of parliament here have indeed expressed quite a few problems related to fisheries. I have already mentioned – Lithuania borders Russia in the Baltic Sea and the Curonian Lagoon. In 2023, Lithuania banned commercial fishing, which Russia is very happy about. That is not enough – many of our fishermen were required to cut up their ships. Of course, they gave compensation from the European Union. For this, it needs to be understood logically, in order to improve Russia's fishing resources. How do you assess this policy? And do you not plan to review your fisheries policy, which is very disadvantageous for the European Union countries, as well as for our state Lithuania? Almost every Member of the European Parliament talks about this.

4-0118-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, κύριε Επίτροπε, η κλιματική αλλαγή μεταβάλλει ήδη τη θερμοκρασία και τη χημεία των θαλασσών. Προκαλεί μετατόπιση των ειδών, απώλεια βιοποικιλότητας και αυξανόμενη πίεση στα παράκτια οικοσυστήματα. Παρά ταύτα, η Κοινή Αλιευτική Πολιτική εξακολουθεί να αντιμετωπίζει τα θαλάσσια οικοσυστήματα κυρίως ως ενδιαίτημα των αλιευτικών πόρων και όχι ως κρίσιμες υποδομές για την αντιμετώπιση της κλιματικής κρίσης. Ιδιαίτερα, τα οικοσυστήματα «blue carbon», όπως τα λιβάδια ποσειδωνίας, οι παράκτιοι υγρότοποι, οι εκβολές ποταμών και οι λιμνοθάλασσες αποτελούν σημαντικές φυσικές δεξαμενές αποθήκευσης διοξειδίου του άνθρακα. Συμβάλλουν στην προστασία των ακτών, στη βελτίωση της ποιότητας των υδάτων και στη διατήρηση των ιχθυοαποθεμάτων. Ωστόσο, παρά τη σημασία τους για την επίτευξη των στόχων της Ένωσης για την κλιματική ουδετερότητα, η προστασία και η αποκατάστασή τους εξακολουθούν να είναι ανεπαρκείς, ιδίως στην Ελλάδα. Η αξιολόγηση της Κοινής Αλιευτικής Πολιτικής αποτελεί συνεπώς ευκαιρία...

(Η Πρόεδρος αφαιρεί τον λόγο από την ομιλήτρια)
4-0118-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, climate change is already altering the temperature and chemistry of the seas. It causes species migration, biodiversity loss, and increasing pressure on coastal ecosystems. Nevertheless, the Common Fisheries Policy continues to treat marine ecosystems primarily as a habitat for fishery resources and not as critical infrastructure for tackling the climate crisis. In particular, "blue carbon" ecosystems, such as Posidonia meadows, coastal wetlands, river estuaries, and lagoons, are important natural carbon storage reservoirs. They contribute to coastal protection, water quality improvement, and the maintenance of fish stocks. However, despite their importance for achieving the Union's climate neutrality targets, their protection and restoration remain inadequate, particularly in Greece. The evaluation of the Common Fisheries Policy is therefore an opportunity...

(The President cuts off the speaker)

4-0119-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, Commissioner, the common fisheries policy has failed to deliver, and while there is no silver bullet, CFP reform must address the following.

One, levelling the playing field post-Brexit.

Two, protecting the Hague preferences. It cannot continue to become an annual bargaining chip.

Three, the EU budget: while we in Parliament have restored Commission cuts, we need to deliver as part of an overall package, including small-scale fishers.

Finally, overfishing: Norway, the Faroe Islands, Iceland, setting unilateral quotas and getting away with it. The EU must better leverage its own influence in international negotiations.

Yes, we want sustainable fisheries, but let me be clear, Commissioner. There are two components to that concept: 'sustainable' and 'fisheries'. The Commission cannot keep forgetting about the latter.

4-0120-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Panie Komisarzu! Rozmawiamy dziś o ewaluacji wspólnej polityki rybołówstwa, ale na Bałtyku nie ma już czego ewaluować. Bałtyk umiera. Przez lata cięliśmy kwoty połowowe, łudząc się, że to odbuduje stada dorsza i śledzia. Ale ryb jak nie było, tak nie ma, bo ignorujemy prawdziwe przyczyny katastrofy: martwe strefy, brak tlenu, zanieczyszczenia chemiczne i rolnicze spływające do morza. Polscy rybacy tracą dorobek życia nie z własnej winy.

Dlatego wzywam Komisję do konkretnych działań. Po pierwsze, elastycznego wsparcia z funduszu morskiego na rekompensaty i przekwalifikowanie. Po drugie, faktycznego podejścia ekosystemowego. Zamiast dobijać rybaków restrykcjami, zacznijmy ratować morze przed uduszeniem. Zostawienie Bałtyku samemu sobie to nie polityka. To jest wyrok na całe wybrzeże.
4-0120-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Commissioner! Today we are discussing the evaluation of the Common Fisheries Policy, but there is nothing left to evaluate in the Baltic Sea. The Baltic Sea is dying. For years we have cut fishing quotas, deluding ourselves that this would rebuild cod and herring stocks. But fish are still as absent as before because we ignore the true causes of the catastrophe: dead zones, lack of oxygen, chemical and agricultural pollution flowing into the sea. Polish fishermen are losing their life's work through no fault of their own.

Therefore, I call on the Commission for concrete actions. First, flexible support from the maritime fund for compensation and retraining. Second, an actual ecosystem approach. Instead of finishing off fishermen with restrictions, let us start saving the sea from suffocation. Leaving the Baltic Sea to its own devices is not a policy. It is a sentence on the entire coast.

4-0121-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Jestem tu kolejnym mówcą, który zwraca uwagę na absolutnie tragiczną sytuację polskiego rybołówstwa na Bałtyku. Znajduje się ono w gigantycznym kryzysie. W samym tylko 2025 r. liczba jednostek połowowych spadła o 5%. Limity, które są narzucane Polsce, restrykcje, regulacje – to wszystko dobija polskie rybołówstwo. Rybacy, którzy tracą dorobek swojego życia, trafiają do urzędów pośrednictwa pracy. Czy tak ma wyglądać polityka Unii Europejskiej wobec tego ważnego sektora?

Z drugiej strony do Unii Europejskiej wpływają importowane ryby spoza Unii Europejskiej i turyści na polskim wybrzeżu jedzą nie polskie ryby z Bałtyku, ale importowane, mrożone ryby spoza Unii Europejskiej. Czy tak ma wyglądać polityka Unii Europejskiej? Jaka jest strategia Komisji Europejskiej, ażeby uratować polskie rybołówstwo na Bałtyku?
4-0121-0000.englishText:
Madam President! I am another speaker here who draws attention to the absolutely tragic situation of Polish fisheries in the Baltic Sea. It is in a giant crisis. In 2025 alone, the number of fishing vessels fell by 5%. The limits that are imposed on Poland, restrictions, regulations - all this is finishing off Polish fisheries. Fishermen who are losing their life's work end up in employment offices. Is this what the European Union's policy towards this important sector is supposed to look like?

On the other hand, imported fish from outside the European Union flow into the European Union and tourists on the Polish coast do not eat Polish fish from the Baltic, but imported, frozen fish from outside the European Union. Is this what the European Union's policy is supposed to look like? What is the European Commission's strategy to save Polish fisheries in the Baltic Sea?

4-0123-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, honourable Members, I have listened very carefully to your remarks, and let me recall that this is the first time since the 2013 reform that the CFP Regulation is evaluated with such comprehensive data and trend. Based on this diagnosis, but also on your views and the positions of the Member States and all stakeholders, we will take a political decision as to the follow‑up, including on whether addressing the challenges and shortcomings identified in the evaluation requires any legislative changes, and to which extent. Issues you raised, such as the need for modernisation and the decarbonisation of the fishing fleet, generational renewal, securing a level playing field for our sector, simplification, fair treatment and further support to the small‑scale fishers, the consideration of socio‑economic elements in the scientific advice that we receive for developing our proposals for fishing opportunities and better implementation and enforcement of our legal framework, will be at the centre of our attention.

On the landing obligation, the evaluation shows that it did not deliver the expected results for several reasons. In particular, there was a low uptake in buying at the industry level. However, it is clear that we cannot go back to the old situation of massive and unreported discarding, and our sector agrees on that principle. And that is why I have invited the representatives of the sector to discuss their and our ideas on how we can address this challenge. It is important that the measures that we will develop are applicable and well received by those who will implement them at the end of the day.

Having all this in mind. I will consider making a proposal to the College of Commissioners for a targeted amendment of the CFP Regulation, subject to the Commission's better regulation procedures. Combating IUU fishing is one of our top priorities. We are proud of the first‑ever digital certification system – IT CATCH – which has been operational for six months and ensures that no product stemming from IUU fishing enters the European Union market. IT CATCH has already proven a success thanks to real‑time EU‑wide data. We are also strengthening the legal and governance frameworks for fighting IUU fishing through bilateral agreements and our participation in regional fisheries management organisations.

Honourable Members, the findings of the evaluation will also feed into the Commission's Vision 2040 for fisheries and aquaculture, which will include the external action strategy and the energy transition roadmap in the early autumn. Parallel to this work, we are proceeding with our simplification initiatives, listening also to your calls, and particularly the simplification of the multiannual fisheries management plans – we want to make them easier to implement and to address the challenges identified so far – and the European Maritime Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund Regulation, to align it with the new WTO agreement on fisheries subsidies and to simplify its implementation.

Honourable Members, I assure you that your feedback is highly respected and will be taken into account in the development and implementation of these policy initiatives.

4-0124-0000.sourceText:
The debate is closed.

The vote will be held at the next part-session.

4-0124-5000.sourceText:
La evaluación de la política pesquera común (PPC) ha constatado que esta ha permitido mejorar la sostenibilidad de las capturas europeas: se ha producido una sustancial reducción de la sobrepesca y se ha multiplicado la proporción de poblaciones explotadas en niveles de rendimiento máximo sostenible, además de haberse mejorado el conocimiento científico.

Pero la PPC no ha funcionado como se predijo: mientras la evaluación de impacto preveía un aumento salarial del 125 %, los salarios han perdido poder adquisitivo real, el empleo ha caído un 30 % y hoy dependemos más que nunca de las importaciones de pescado. Además, el sector no es atractivo para las nuevas generaciones y existen tantas cortapisas a la renovación de la flota que esta está obsoleta, con más de treinta años de media de edad.

No hablamos solo de problemas de implementación. Hablamos de problemas de diseño y nuevas realidades a las que hay que hacer frente; problemas que se van a acrecentar con el recorte presupuestario inadmisible propuesto por la Comisión y que los socialistas rechazamos. Por tanto, urge una reforma específica de la PPC para reequilibrar las tres dimensiones de la sostenibilidad, impulsar el relevo generacional, afrontar el envejecimiento de la flota, promover TAC plurianuales e introducir límites a las variaciones interanuales de los mismos.
4-0124-5000.englishText:
The evaluation of the Common Fisheries Policy (CFP) has confirmed that it has made it possible to improve the sustainability of European catches: there has been a substantial reduction in overfishing and the proportion of stocks exploited at maximum sustainable yield levels has multiplied, in addition to an improvement in scientific knowledge.

But the CFP has not functioned as predicted: while the impact assessment anticipated a 125% increase in salaries, wages have lost real purchasing power, employment has fallen by 30% and today we depend more than ever on fish imports. Furthermore, the sector is not attractive to new generations and there are so many obstacles to fleet renewal that it is obsolete, with an average age of over thirty years.

We are not just talking about implementation problems. We are talking about design problems and new realities that must be addressed; problems that will be exacerbated by the inadmissible budget cut proposed by the Commission and which we socialists reject. Therefore, a specific reform of the CFP is urgently needed to rebalance the three dimensions of sustainability, boost generational renewal, address the ageing of the fleet, promote multiannual TACs and introduce limits on their year-on-year variations.

4-0126-0000.sourceText:
The next item is the debate on the report by Ľudovít Ódor, on behalf of the Committee on Economic and Monetary Affairs, on the feasibility of a 28th tax regime and its potential to support EU competitiveness (2025/2211(INI)) (A10-0167/2026).

I would like to remind speakers that, given the test measures currently in place and the fixed end time of debate, strict observance to speaking time will be required for all of you. Thank you very much for your understanding.

4-0127-0000.sourceText:
Dear President, Commissioner, colleagues, Europe is facing a new geopolitical and economic reality. Rules matter less than they once did. Power and scale matters more. In this context, our single market remains one of the most underutilised assets at our disposal. The European Union is clearly punching below its weight. We are failing to fully leverage the strength that comes with providing access to a market of 450 million consumers.

The evidence is striking: among the world's 50 largest companies by market capitalisation, only one is European. In 2025, Europe had just 331 unicorns, compared with almost 2 000 in the United States. Since 2008, nearly 30 % of European unicorns have relocated their headquarters outside the EU. Venture capital investment in Europe amounts to around EUR 30 billion, compared with USD 177 billion in the United States. The million dollar question is, why? The answer, from my perspective, is twofold. First, the EU lacks sufficient high risk investments due to the absence of a genuine savings and investment union. Second, even in areas requiring lower-risk investment, we underperform because of fragmentation.

What are the main obstacles to cross-border growth? When we ask SMEs, start-ups and scale-ups, they consistently identify three major challenges. First, navigating different business environment across Member States. Second, the complexity of accessing information, understanding rules and complying with administrative procedure. Third, taxation.

I welcome the Commission's proposal for an 'EU Inc.'. It really represents an important first step towards creating a genuine single market for start-ups and scale-ups. Its objective is to enable companies to operate seamlessly across borders without unnecessary barriers. However, the proposal is not ambitious enough, as it focuses primarily on corporate law. This presents two shortcomings. First, without addressing the entire lifecycle of a company, its impact will inevitably remain limited. Second, the proposal should draw more extensively on successful international best practices.

In our report, we advocate a modular approach that builds on the corporate law framework as its foundation. At the same time, to ensure political feasibility, the tax module should initially apply only to a limited group of companies such as growth oriented start-ups and scale-ups. These companies usually generate only a marginal share of overall tax revenues.

I would like to highlight a few points from the report. First, we propose a framework based on fully digital procedures, a one-stop shop, harmonised templates. Second, we call for a single consolidated corporate tax base and the uniform methodology for determining taxable income. Third, we propose effective measures to eliminate double taxation. Fourth, we support the creation of a centralised VAT framework. Fifth, we recommend introducing a mandatory employee stock option. Sixth, we call for targeted rules to provide tax certainty for employees moving between Member States. Finally, we encourage better coordination of tax incentives across the union.

4-0128-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, honourable Members, in March this year, the Commission adopted the proposal for the 28th regime corporate legal framework – 'EU Inc.'. The 'EU Inc.' initiative is a key measure aimed at enhancing Europe's competitiveness and improving the business environment for EU companies. As part of the broader instrument, it includes limited ancillary tax measures designed to support businesses.

As you know, the 'EU Inc.' proposal is based on five main pillars. First, digital-by-default procedures throughout the lifecycle of 'EU Inc.' companies. Second, extension of the 'once only' principle for provision of information. Third, facilitation of investment. Fourth, support for the attraction and retention of talent. And fifth, access to digital and simplified insolvency procedures for innovative start‑ups.

I am pleased to address you today at the occasion of the debate of the own initiative, which is, of course, a different subject entirely. We thank the European Parliament, in particular MEP Ľudovít Ódor and his team for the important work. We are pleased to see that the report welcomes the Commission proposal on 'EU Inc.'. The message we received from stakeholders was clear: companies need EU‑wide rules that are harmonised and simple. Companies also pointed to the need for more digital processes in Europe. The 'EU Inc.' proposal responds to these needs. It provides for an ambitious, harmonised corporate legal framework which will be available in each Member State for both founders and existing companies.

From a tax perspective, the proposal already includes two concrete, but strictly ancillary, measures:

First, the application of the 'once only' principle to reduce the administrative burden on 'EU Inc.' companies. This means that, in the registration process, the 'EU Inc.' information submitted to the business register will be automatically shared with tax authorities in view of obtaining the tax identification number (TIN) and the VAT identification number. There will be no need for 'EU Inc.' companies to resubmit paperwork multiple times.

Second is a tax deferral for employee stock options to support the ability of 'EU Inc.' to attract and retain talent. This means that employees investing in an 'EU Inc.' through an EU employee stock option plan will benefit from a simpler scheme with a harmonised set of characteristics. From the tax perspective, it also means that the employees to whom warrants under the stock option plan are issued will not be taxed until the actual sale of the underlying shares. The tax elements in the 'EU Inc.' proposal strike exactly the right balance. They deliver highly targeted and practical measures that support our broader objective, but by enabling businesses to reap the full benefit of the single market, while respecting Member States' competences in tax matters.

The own‑initiative report highlights the room for simplification. We agree with that. We also concur that there is room for additional and more targeted harmonisation, as you rightly said, of tax matters to improve the business environment in the single market. So we can we can improve this.

4-0129-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, the Commission proposal for the creation of the 28th regime is one of the most visible, important and possibly impactful proposals that we have got on the table in this term. It would make the single market much stronger and it will provide start-ups and scale-ups with a better framework on how to keep their activity within the EU, because this is a very substantial problem.

We have in Europe excellent education. We are rich in ideas and innovations. We have entrepreneurship, but unfortunately most of the companies, when they are starting to take off and are on the way to success, they are leaving our market. The Commission proposal that is now being discussed is a first step towards creating such a regime. Digitalisation is very good because it will provide companies with a simplified environment. A key component is clarity in the regime of employees' shares.

This is a very good proposal and I just call on our House and the Council not to water it down: make it stronger and pass it quickly. But this is by far not enough, especially for scale-ups to stay in Europe. Better to have a tax regime that will simplify life, especially for the companies operating across several Member States. Clarity of taxation, avoidance of double taxation, a good regime for R&D expenditures and many other aspects are very important to enable them to stay in our market. So that's why we will ask today the House to vote for the proposal that will allow all of this.

We opt for the CCCTB to simplify the life of companies operating across the market. We call for reducing the risk of double taxation and the creation of uncertainty, and for the expenditures to be dealt with. This is the way to create a genuine market for successful start-ups in Europe; to allow them to flourish, but also allow European investors to invest safely in these companies and not go abroad. I hope we will we will succeed in that, and I hope the Commission will come with more modules that will make this regime more usable and richer.

4-0130-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Caros Colegas, vivemos um momento histórico. E, como nos avisou Mario Draghi, a União Europeia avança para uma nova era de competitividade ou arriscamo-nos a ficar definitivamente para trás. E é para isso que, hoje, desafiamos 27 Estados-Membros que representam 450 milhões de pessoas, mas também 450 milhões de consumidores.

Este é o primeiro sinal para que as start-ups, pequenas e médias empresas que na Europa queiram crescer possam inovar e possam criar emprego. Em vez de 27 regimes burocráticos, defendemos a criação de uma via alternativa que permita operar imediatamente em todos os países, de uma forma ágil e de uma forma rápida.

Esta é a hora de acabar com os egoísmos nacionais que impedem um sistema de impostos menos complexo, mas, inevitavelmente também, mais eficaz; com menos papelada, mas também com menos evasão fiscal.

Este 28.º regime não serve para contornar as regras e, por isso, deixamos claro que se mantêm vivas as proteções sociais, nomeadamente as laborais para o trabalhador, e que se evitam os esquemas de planeamento fiscal. Não será o dumping social, nem o dumping fiscal, nem a capacidade para preencher papelada que podem definir quais são as empresas mais competitivas na União Europeia.

Para que as start-ups e empresas pequenas familiares possam competir com as mais poderosas, nós precisamos de lhes oferecer formas de atrair talento e de reter os mais brilhantes. Foi, aliás, para isso, que aceitámos, que concordámos e que negociámos uma modernização do rendimento do trabalho, admitindo que as stock options dos trabalhadores não sofram uma penalização em face dos investidores que compram e vendem ações. Isto é, sim, defender trabalhadores, defender os mais jovens, mas esta é, sim, também uma nova agenda trabalhista para os mais jovens.

Este incentivo é um caso específico e isolado, mas que nos deve motivar para uma reflexão mais abrangente. Que sentido faz taxar mais um trabalhador que decidiu apostar em si e numa start-up promissora do que um especulador que apenas compra e vende ações? A resposta é muito simples: não faz sentido nenhum.

O momento e o desejo é que a Comissão e o Conselho possam trabalhar neste grande desafio e que comecemos a pensar no grande desafio que é o desafio comum europeu.
4-0130-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, we are living in a historic moment. And, as Mario Draghi warned us, the European Union is moving towards a new era of competitiveness, or we risk falling behind definitively. And that is why today we challenge 27 Member States representing 450 million people, but also 450 million consumers.

This is the first sign so that start-ups, small and medium-sized enterprises in Europe that want to grow can innovate and create jobs. Instead of 27 bureaucratic regimes, we advocate the creation of an alternative pathway that allows operating immediately in all countries, in an agile and fast way.

This is the time to put an end to the national egoisms that prevent a less complex, but inevitably also more effective tax system; with less paperwork, but also less tax evasion.

This 28th regime is not meant to circumvent the rules and, therefore, we make it clear that social protections, namely labor protections for the worker, remain alive, and that tax planning schemes are avoided. Neither social dumping, nor fiscal dumping, nor the ability to fill out paperwork can define which are the most competitive companies in the European Union.

So that start-ups and small family businesses can compete with the most powerful ones, we need to offer them ways to attract talent and retain the brightest. It was precisely for this reason that we accepted, agreed, and negotiated a modernization of labor income, admitting that workers' stock options should not suffer a penalty compared to investors who buy and sell shares. This is indeed defending workers, defending the youngest, but this is also a new labor agenda for the youngest.

This incentive is a specific and isolated case, but one that should motivate us for a broader reflection. What sense does it make to tax a worker more who decided to invest in themselves and a promising start-up than a speculator who just buys and sells shares? The answer is very simple: it makes no sense at all.

The moment and the desire is for the Commission and the Council to work on this great challenge and for us to begin thinking about the great challenge that is the common European challenge.

4-0131-0000.sourceText:
Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! Az adópolitika nem véletlenül tartozik tagállami hatáskörbe. A szerződések egyértelműen tiszteletben tartják a nemzeti fiskális szuverenitást, a tagállamok eltérő gazdasági adottságait és a tisztességes versenyt. A Parlament nagykoalíciója, a baloldaltól a Néppártig, mégis újabb és újabb kísérleteket tesz ennek a hatáskörnek a kiüresítésére. Ez a jelentés valójában nem a versenyképességről szól. Ez a tagállami adópolitika lassú felszámolásának mesterterve. Először egy önkéntesen alkalmazható, úgynevezett 28. adózási rezsimet vezetnének be.
