4-0171-0000.sourceText: ��blauwe kaart”-antwoord. – Ja, ik ben het helemaal eens met uw analyse, maar dat is helemaal geen reden om niet voor een 28e regime te gaan. Dat is nog een grotere reden om te zeggen: laat ons ambitieuzer zijn op economisch vlak, om te harmoniseren wat er geharmoniseerd moet worden. Als we Europa één grote dienst kunnen bewijzen voor onze economische groei — en dat betekent voor onze welvaart, voor ons sociaaleconomisch marktmodel — dan is het wel economische harmonisatie.
4-0171-0000.englishText: "blue card" answer. - Yes, I completely agree with your analysis, but that is no reason at all not to go for a 28th regime. That is an even greater reason to say: let us be more ambitious in the economic field, to harmonize what needs to be harmonized. If we can do Europe a huge service for our economic growth - and that means for our prosperity, for our socio-economic market model - it is economic harmonization.

4-0173-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, my colleague Ressler said Europe was a sleeping giant. And this is a sleep that is self-inflicted because of overregulation etc. So now we need to wake up and get rid of the sleeping tablets.

I think the report by Mario Draghi has been followed through very sensibly by the Commission in relation to omnibuses and now the 28 tax regime. But also crucial to that is investment money, and that can come from the savings and investment union, which is a priority for the Irish Presidency over the next six months. And if we get the cooperation we need and require, then the billions of euros that citizens have in banks, sleeping there, losing money for them, can be utilised to create the investment that will help us to not only research, but also innovate, scale up and manufacture in Europe, and that will benefit all of us.

4-0174-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señora comisaria, el vigésimo octavo régimen —EU Inc.— es un objetivo ambicioso: crear reglas armonizadas para la constitución, la gobernanza y las estructuras de capital de las empresas innovadoras coherentes con lo que proponen los informes Letta y Draghi —con los que arrancó esta legislatura— y, además, hacerlo por un reglamento, es decir, que solo requiera mayoría cualificada en el Consejo.

Bien, este Parlamento no solo lo apoya claramente, sino que quiere liderar esa iniciativa. Pero tenemos que ser conscientes de sus dificultades, porque lo haremos en coincidencia con la ausencia de armonización fiscal —que sigue perteneciendo a los Estados miembros como competencia—, laboral —igualmente 27 regímenes distintos— y, también, a pesar de que se armonice el registro de las empresas, convivirá con 27 modelos registrales diferentes en la Unión.

Por tanto, el objetivo es plausible pero hay que ser conscientes de las dificultades. Lo que hay que conseguir es que el resultado legislativo esté a la altura de la ambición proclamada.
4-0174-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, the twenty-eighth regime —EU Inc.— is an ambitious objective: to create harmonized rules for the constitution, governance, and capital structures of innovative companies consistent with what the Letta and Draghi reports propose —with which this term began— and, furthermore, to do so by means of a regulation, meaning it would only require a qualified majority in the Council.

Well, this Parliament not only clearly supports it, but wants to lead this initiative. But we must be aware of its difficulties, because we will do so concurrently with the absence of fiscal harmonization —which continues to belong to the Member States as a competence—, labor harmonization —likewise 27 different regimes— and, also, despite the fact that company registration is harmonized, it will coexist with 27 different registry models in the Union.

Therefore, the objective is plausible, but we must be aware of the difficulties. What must be achieved is that the legislative outcome lives up to the proclaimed ambition.

4-0175-0000.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, tämä talo ei pääse yli vihreästä vimmastaan. Kun käsitellään rajat ylittävän liiketoiminnan verotuksen yksinkertaistamista, samasta ovesta yritetään vetää punavihreän puolueohjelman kirjauksia. Nimittäin Euroopan eduskunnan kannaksi esitetään tähän yksinkertaisempaan verojärjestelmään liittyen seuraavaa: vihreän innovoinnin olisi voitava saada väliaikaisia lisävähennyksiä tai veronmaksun lykkäyksiä.

Minä kysyn, miksi ihmeessä tämä vihreä innovointi tarvitsee nämä kaikki lykkäykset, lisävähennykset ja valtiontuet, joita te jatkuvasti puskette? Ei kai vain ole niin, että vihreät hankkeet eivät pärjää kilpailussa ja niitä pitää siksi tukea kaikin mahdollisin keinoin. Eurooppa odottaa edelleen sitä vihreää kasvua, jota te olette vuosikausia luvanneet. Realismia on lakata odottamasta sitä ja alkaa kunnioittamaan markkinatalouden periaatteita, jotka eivät rakennu vihreän tukihumpan varaan.
4-0175-0000.englishText:
Mr President, this house cannot get over its green craze. When discussing the simplification of cross-border business taxation, entries from the red-green party program are being dragged in through the same door. Namely, in connection with this simpler tax system, it is proposed as the position of the European Parliament that green innovation should be able to receive temporary additional deductions or tax payment deferrals.

I ask, why on earth does this green innovation need all these deferrals, additional deductions, and state subsidies that you are constantly pushing? Could it be that green projects cannot survive in competition and therefore must be supported by all possible means. Europe is still waiting for that green growth that you have promised for years. Realism is to stop waiting for it and start respecting market economy principles, which are not built on the foundation of green subsidy dance.

4-0176-0000.sourceText:
A Uachtaráin, agus Éire ag glacadh Uachtaránacht an Aontais chuici féin, tá treisiú iomaíochas na hEorpa go mór chun tosaigh. Mar sin, fáiltím roimh an tuairisc seo ag an bhFeisire Ódor, rapóirtéir ó mo ghrúpasa féin, Renew Europe, agus gabhaim buíochas leis as an ngrinnstaidéar atá déanta aige faoin 28ú réimeas cánach atá roghnach - roghnach dár SMEs.

Tosú san Eoraip, fás san Eoraip, fanacht san Eoraip agus gan imeacht ó bhaile. Níl an margadh scoilte san Eoraip ag feidhmiú ar son ár SMEs ar feadh i bhfad, ach a mhalairt, is ag feidhmiú ina n-aghaidh atá sé.

Molaim an chreatlach Eorpach roghnach seo chun na córais éagsúla ionchorpraithe, mhaoinithe, infheistíochta, dócmhainneachta, dhlíthiúla, saothair agus chánach a chomhoiriúnú, agus ag aithint ag an am céanna an íogaireacht pholaitiúil a bhaineann le cúrsaí cánach ag leibhéal náisiúnta na mBallstát.
4-0176-0000.englishText:
Mr President, as Ireland takes over the Presidency of the Union, strengthening Europe's competitiveness is a major priority. Therefore, I welcome this report by MEP Ódor, rapporteur from my own political group, Renew Europe, and I thank him for the in-depth study he has carried out on the 28th tax regime which is optional - optional for our SMEs.

Start in Europe, grow in Europe, stay in Europe and do not leave home. The fragmented market in Europe has not been working for our SMEs for a long time, but rather it has been working against them.

I commend this optional European framework to harmonize the various incorporation, financing, investment, insolvency, legal, labor and tax systems, while recognizing the political sensitivity surrounding tax matters at the national level of the Member States.

4-0177-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, obstacles to businesses, cross-border operations and expansion constitute a major hurdle to an effective single market. We complain a lot about the 15 % US tariffs, but we tend to forget that existing barriers in our own single market account to much more.

And yes, a single business code would be a game changer. Today, a company expanding across Europe must navigate different tax procedures, authorities and reporting requirements. This is where the 28th regime can make a practical difference by simplifying this procedure through a one-stop shop, a single interface and stronger coordination between tax authorities.

But if a company can register under one European framework and still has to navigate a different national rules every time it hires, raises capital or expands into a new market, we will have changed the rulebook without changing the reality of doing business in Europe.

The question is simple: will this regime remove complexity or merely add another layer of it? Let's do our best to achieve the first, because its success will ultimately depend on whether companies can operate more easily across our single market and compete more effectively.

4-0178-0000.sourceText: Gerbiama Pirmininke, gerbiama komisare. Siekiant bendros rinkos, aš manau, kad mes turėtume vienodinti ir mokesčius. Lietuvoje pridėtinės vertės mokestis yra vienas aukštesnių Europos Sąjungoje. Ypač pridėtinės vertės mokestis yra aukštas maisto produktams. Daugelyje Europos Sąjungos šalių pridėtinės vertės mokestis maisto produktams yra daug žemesnis, bet Lietuvoje tam nedaroma išlygų. Aš manau, būtina siekti, kad maisto produktams pridėtinės vertės mokestis būtų nulinis tarifas, ypač būtiniausiems maisto produktams. Ne kartą siūliau, būdamas europarlamentaras, kad tie mokesčiai būtų mažesni, bet, deja, nepritardavo nei viena, nei kita vyriausybė. Ar nemano Europos Sąjunga, kad maisto produktams būtina mažinti mokesčius? Tuo labiau, kad Lietuvoje yra atskirtis turtinė labai didelė ir skurstančių arti 20 proc. žmonių.
4-0178-0000.englishText: Madam President, esteemed Commissioner. In pursuit of a single market, I believe that we should also standardise taxes. In Lithuania, the value added tax is one of the highest in the European Union. In particular, the value added tax is high on food products. In many European Union countries, the value added tax on food products is much lower, but no exceptions are made for this in Lithuania. I believe it is necessary to seek that the value added tax on food products has a zero rate, especially for essential food products. I have repeatedly suggested, as a Member of the European Parliament, that these taxes be lower, but unfortunately neither the one nor the other government would agree. Does the European Union not think that it is necessary to reduce taxes on food products? Especially since in Lithuania there is a very large wealth disparity and nearly 20 percent of people are impoverished.

4-0179-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Επίτροπε, σας καλώ να αποσύρετε αυτή την πρόταση. Το λεγόμενο 28ο καθεστώς δεν είναι μια αθώα διοικητική αλλαγή. Είναι μια επικίνδυνη πόρτα για τις εταιρείες-γραμματοκιβώτια, το κοινωνικό ντάμπινγκ και την αποδυνάμωση των συλλογικών δικαιωμάτων. Η ίδια η Ευρωπαϊκή Συνομοσπονδία Συνδικάτων ETUC προειδοποιεί ότι δεν υπάρχουν δεσμευτικές εγγυήσεις για τους εργαζομένους. Το Ευρωπαϊκό Συνδικαλιστικό Ινστιτούτο προειδοποιεί ότι ανοίγει ο δρόμος για τον ανταγωνισμό εις βάρος των μισθών και των δικαιωμάτων.

Λέμε όχι στο «race to the bottom». Αν η Επιτροπή πιστεύει ότι τα δικαιώματα των εργαζομένων δεν κινδυνεύουν, τότε κατοχυρώστε ρητά στον κανονισμό ότι θα εφαρμόζεται πάντοτε το εργατικό δίκαιο και οι συλλογικές συμβάσεις της χώρας όπου εργάζεται πραγματικά ο εργαζόμενος. Μέχρι να κατοχυρωθούν δεσμευτικές εγγυήσεις για κάθε εργαζόμενο, η θέση μας είναι ξεκάθαρη: Αποσύρετε αυτή την πρόταση.
4-0179-0000.englishText:
Madam Commissioner, I call on you to withdraw this proposal. The so-called 28th regime is not an innocent administrative change. It is a dangerous door for letterbox companies, social dumping and the weakening of collective rights. The European Trade Union Confederation ETUC itself warns that there are no binding guarantees for workers. The European Trade Union Institute warns that it paves the way for competition at the expense of wages and rights.

We say no to the "race to the bottom". If the Commission believes that workers' rights are not at risk, then explicitly enshrine in the regulation that the labor law and collective agreements of the country where the worker actually works will always apply. Until binding guarantees are enshrined for every worker, our position is clear: Withdraw this proposal.

4-0181-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, honourable Members, thank you for your valuable remarks and for your recognition that this proposal is a good step in the right direction. 'EU Inc.' is a corporate‑law proposal, which is part of a broader strategy to strengthen the competitiveness of the European economy. Yes, we want to remove complexities and we want to simplify but not lower our standards in combating tax evasion.

We will ensure fair taxation and a level playing field, and maintain a high level of protection against tax fraud. The objective is to enable companies to operate under a single, harmonised set of EU‑wide rules, instead of having to navigate different corporate‑law frameworks of the Member States.

We commend the fact that the European Parliament recognises 'EU Inc.' as a strategic step forward towards a further deepening and improvement of the single market and competitiveness. We also acknowledge the Parliament's general call for further legislative actions related to the 28th regime. We are ready to listen to the businesses and work together with the Member States to create an environment in which companies can thrive.

Thank you for your exchange, and all the best.

4-0182-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, first, I wanted to thank all the shadow rapporteurs and also MEPs for the lively debate. I think it also showed that this is an important topic.

Second, I wanted to highlight maybe three issues which are really important, and I felt a little bit of misunderstanding in the plenary.

The first one, the regime is optional. It is optional not only for the companies but also for the Member State to opt into this regime. So, this is not forcing targeted harmonisation among Member States.

The second one, it is not mainly about tax revenues, since start-ups and scale-ups usually generate at the beginning of their life very, very limited revenues.

The third one is that it is important to highlight that we are not an isolated island somewhere in the Pacific, but we need to be competitive internationally. What are the benchmarks internationally? If you look at the situation in the US, they have a special regime for scale-ups, start-ups and innovative companies. It is called the Delaware regime. I do not advocate to simply copy that situation, mainly because of worker rights and others, but still, we need one regime for having scale in Europe, because what is the alternative? If we are not able to create big companies, globally competitive companies, if we are not able to utilise the full single market, then of course somebody else will decide about our future. And that is at least not what I want for the future of Europe.

So, thank you once again very much for the constructive discussion.

4-0183-0000.sourceText:
The debate is closed.

The vote will be held today.

4-0186-0000.sourceText:
IN THE CHAIR: SOPHIE WILMÈS

Vice-President

4-0190-0000.sourceText: The EPP and Renew Europe groups have notified the President of decisions relating to changes to appointments within committees. The decisions will be set out in the minutes of today’s sitting and take effect on the date of this announcement.

4-0191-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, I rise under Rule 202(1) and (4), and Rule 180(1) in conjunction with Rule 202(4).

On Monday, the President reminded us that there should be no chanting in this Chamber. Yesterday, it happened again. The reaction of the sitting President? Nothing.

Later, a colleague requested a personal statement. Under the plenary reforms that were introduced, it should be granted immediately. He was ignored.

And finally, yesterday evening, a colleague said, talking about Muslims – and I ask the interpreters to make it very clear that this is a quote – he said, about Muslims, 'They spend a lot of time with goats'. The reaction of the sitting President: 'We will look into that'.

Let me be very clear: I do not blame the sitting presidents. I blame the culture. Breaches of our Rules of Procedure are rarely addressed in this Chamber. They disappear into administrative procedures instead of being dealt with transparently. If we want the plenary reform to succeed, we need to change the culture together.

4-0192-0000.sourceText:
A Uachtaráin, beidh mé chomh tapaidh agus is féidir liom.

Yesterday, at the first debate on the conclusions of the European Council meeting, a lot of Members – understandably at the time – were critical of the non-attendance of the Irish Presidency. Having already looked at the reason, I can now assure Members that it was not the fault of the Irish Presidency. The European Council decided, because it was the conclusion of the meetings in the relation to the Council, that that only President Costa, who was in Ankara at the NATO summit, could attend. The Irish minister was here and available to attend the meeting, but he was not allowed.

To be fair to the Irish Government, we had a meeting with our Prime Minister, Micheál Martin, on Monday night, and there we discussed the need to attend and show respect to Parliament. The Irish Presidency will attend all meetings that they are required and allowed to attend here in Parliament.
4-0192-0000.englishText:
Mr President, I will be as quick as I can.

Yesterday, at the first debate on the conclusions of the European Council meeting, a lot of Members – understandably at the time – were critical of the non-attendance of the Irish Presidency. Having already looked at the reason, I can now assure Members that it was not the fault of the Irish Presidency. The European Council decided, because it was the conclusion of the meetings in the relation to the Council, that that only President Costa, who was in Ankara at the NATO summit, could attend. The Irish minister was here and available to attend the meeting, but he was not allowed.

To be fair to the Irish Government, we had a meeting with our Prime Minister, Micheál Martin, on Monday night, and there we discussed the need to attend and show respect to Parliament. The Irish Presidency will attend all meetings that they are required and allowed to attend here in Parliament.

4-0194-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! W oparciu o art. 2 Regulaminu Parlamentu Europejskiego dotyczący niezależności mandatu posła do Parlamentu Europejskiego, który właśnie został złamany, wnoszę o natychmiastowe zatrzymanie przyspieszonej akcesji Ukrainy do Unii Europejskiej.

Ukraińskie służby prowadzą listę Myrotworeć, na której umieszczają nazwiska ludzi zgłoszonych do nękania, zastraszania i eliminowania. Dziś na tę listę zostałam wpisana ja. Wcześniej zostali wpisani moi koledzy z Patriotów Dla Europy. To zamach na unijnych dyplomatów, których życie i bezpieczeństwo może być zagrożone. To gangsterka i łajdactwo.

Oczekuję reakcji szefowej Parlamentu Europejskiego w celu ochrony dyplomatów z tej instytucji, ponieważ nasze życie i nasze bezpieczeństwo jest w tym momencie zagrożone.
4-0194-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Based on Article 2 of the Rules of Procedure of the European Parliament regarding the independence of the mandate of a Member of the European Parliament, which has just been violated, I request the immediate halt of the accelerated accession of Ukraine to the European Union.

The Ukrainian services maintain the Myrotvorets list, on which they place the names of people reported for harassment, intimidation, and elimination. Today, I was added to this list. Previously, my colleagues from Patriots for Europe were added. This is an attack on EU diplomats, whose lives and security may be endangered. This is gangsterism and scumbaggery.

I expect a reaction from the head of the European Parliament in order to protect diplomats from this institution, because our lives and our security are currently endangered.
4-0194-0000.factCheck: Although the speaker claims that Ukrainian state services maintain the Myrotvorets website, the platform is actually an independent, non-governmental database run by a public NGO, and the Ukrainian government has repeatedly dissociated itself from the site, clarifying that its activities are not related to state institutions.

4-0195-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, colleagues, I rise for a point of order under Rule 202, regarding Rules 60, 73 and 170, regarding the derogation that we will be voting today. This House has already sovereignly expressed its position and voted down this extension twice. The President had no mandate to ask the Council to proceed to a second reading, yet we are here today. This urgent procedure hit our agenda before we even received the Council's position, and then the required plenary debate under Rule 170(4) never even took place.

We cannot rubber‑stamp the mass surveillance of our citizens. Furthermore, by rushing this temporary, flawed fix, we drastically weakened Parliament's position on the long‑term file, which is exactly where we should come to a conclusion to protect our children. The Council had every opportunity to find a reasonable middle ground and even now they can still adopt our position if we amend this text. So colleagues, please help us save the face of this House, protect our children and secure the privacy of our citizens.

4-0196-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, mon intervention se fonde sur l’article 202 du règlement intérieur et sur notre obligation de respecter l’article 2 du traité qui nous lie tous quant au respect de la démocratie, de l’état de droit et des valeurs de l’Union européenne, et sur l’article 10 du traité, qui stipule que le fonctionnement de l’Union européenne est fondé sur la démocratie représentative.

Mais comment, chers collègues, les parlementaires pourraient-ils remplir ces conditions avec tout le sérieux que cela exige, lorsque nous, parlementaires, recevons des listes de vote qui changent souvent jusqu’au dernier instant? Ce n’est pas sérieux. Les listes de vote, les amendements devraient être figés quelques jours avant le vote.

Je vous appelle, chers collègues, à œuvrer tous pour faire évoluer nos règles de fonctionnement, de manière à ce que nous puissions voter avec le sérieux que cela exige, aussi par respect pour tous les citoyens de l’Union européenne.
4-0196-0000.englishText:
Madam President, my intervention is based on Rule 202 of the Rules of Procedure and on our obligation to respect Article 2 of the Treaty which binds us all regarding respect for democracy, the rule of law and the values of the European Union, and on Article 10 of the Treaty, which stipulates that the functioning of the European Union is based on representative democracy.

But how, dear colleagues, can parliamentarians fulfill these conditions with all the seriousness that this requires, when we, parliamentarians, receive voting lists that often change until the very last moment? This is not serious. Voting lists and amendments should be frozen a few days before the vote.

I call on you, dear colleagues, to all work to change our operating rules, so that we can vote with the seriousness that this requires, also out of respect for all citizens of the European Union.

4-0198-0000.sourceText: The next item is the vote.

4-0200-0000.sourceText:
The first vote is on the provision of digital euro services by payment services providers incorporated in Member States whose currency is not the euro and amending Regulation (EU) 2021/1230 of the European Parliament and the Council (see minutes, item 9.1).

Before we vote on the decision to enter interinstitutional negotiations, we will have one round of political group speakers on the establishment of the digital euro.

4-0201-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señorías, pagar y acceder al efectivo es cada vez más difícil para los ciudadanos.

Europa depende de proveedores de pago digitales controlados por terceros países. Ignorar esto ya no es una opción. Este paquete protege el efectivo como nunca antes lo ha hecho el Derecho comunitario y ofrece, además, el euro digital: una alternativa más, no una imposición.

Sin embargo, estimados ciudadanos, algunos prefieren atemorizarles con un mundo distópico en el que el euro digital se utiliza como herramienta de control. No sé si se confunden de continente, de realidad o simplemente quieren una ciudadanía asustada a la que ellos puedan controlar.

Les aseguro que mienten, porque una mayoría de esta Cámara ha diseñado un sistema con los más altos estándares de privacidad; estándares más altos que los de los medios de pago que ya utilizamos. Nadie ni sabrá ni decidirá en qué gastamos nuestro dinero.

Efectivo y euro digital: dos formas de pagar una sola libertad, la de cada ciudadano para elegir. Sigamos trabajando para hacerlo realidad.
4-0201-0000.englishText:
Madam President, honourable members, paying and accessing cash is becoming increasingly difficult for citizens.

Europe depends on digital payment providers controlled by third countries. Ignoring this is no longer an option. This package protects cash like Community law has never done before and also offers the digital euro: just another alternative, not an imposition.

However, dear citizens, some prefer to frighten you with a dystopian world in which the digital euro is used as a tool of control. I do not know if they are confusing the continent, reality, or simply want a frightened citizenry that they can control.

I assure you that they are lying, because a majority of this House has designed a system with the highest privacy standards; standards higher than those of the payment methods we already use. No one will know or decide what we spend our money on.

Cash and the digital euro: two ways to pay for a single freedom, that of each citizen to choose. Let us continue working to make it a reality.

4-0202-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, the digital euro answers a simple question: who should control Europe's financial future? The answer is Europe.

To those behind the motion to block over there, when amendments weaken access to cash by reducing ATMs, you remain silent. When we challenge the foreign payments duopoly, you sided with the status quo. When we fought to cut fees for merchants, you opposed us – even today with your motion.

You claim to stand with ordinary Europeans, but too often you stand with powerful financial interests. Enjoy the rewards of populism while they last. The people of Europe will see through the contradiction sooner than you think.

4-0203-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, Patriots raise objection to the mandate to enter interinstitutional negotiations on the digital euro, as it fails to strike the right balance between strengthening Europe's strategic autonomy and safeguarding innovation, competition and security in the European payments market.

I mention just two reasons. First, the Parliament's draft would exempt unidentified asylum seekers from standard customer identification requirements, while law-abiding European citizens must comply with strict identification rules. This is a clear and nonsense discrimination against respect for European citizens.

Secondly, separating the digital euro's offline and online functionalities would have reduced Europe's dependence on non-European payment providers, while allowing European private payment solutions to innovate and grow. EPP, together with the leftist groups, have impeded that.

So, for these reasons, I urge this House to support this objection.

4-0204-0000.sourceText:
Poštovana predsjedavajuća, kolegice i kolege, uvođenje digitalnog eura nije tehničko pitanje nego prvorazredno političko pitanje i zaslužuje odgovor cijelog ovog Parlamenta. Dok na ovom mjestu raspravljamo o brojnim izvještajima, jedan od najvažnijih zakonodavnih prijedloga, stvaranje novca u digitalnom obliku, ne dolazi pred cijeli dom na otvorenu raspravu. Postavlja se pitanje zašto?

Sudjelovao sam u pregovorima i mislim da se ovaj projekt ne može spasiti. Čuli smo od Europske središnje banke, po njihovim vlastitim procjenama, ovo će koštati između četiri i šest milijardi eura. To nije zanemariv iznos, pogotovo u trenutku kada Europska unija zaostaje u konkurentnosti s drugima.

Na kraju treba reći da jedina velika zemlja koja je uvela digitalni novac u ovom obliku je komunistička Kina.
4-0204-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, the introduction of the digital euro is not a technical issue but a first-rate political issue and deserves the response of this entire Parliament. While we are discussing numerous reports in this place, one of the most important legislative proposals, the creation of money in digital form, is not coming before the full house for an open debate. The question is why?

I participated in the negotiations and I think this project cannot be saved. We have heard from the European Central Bank, according to their own estimates, this will cost between four and six billion euros. That is not a negligible amount, especially at a time when the European Union is lagging behind others in competitiveness.

Finally, it must be said that the only major country that has introduced digital money in this form is communist China.

4-0205-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, nous sommes aujourd’hui trop dépendants des moyens de paiement non européens, en particulier américains, et cette dépendance, mes chers collègues, doit cesser.

Les solutions privées se développent, et c’est très bien, mais nous devons aussi doter l’Union d’une monnaie publique numérique, paneuropéenne, souveraine, qui sera l’équivalent numérique de notre argent liquide – un moyen de paiement supplémentaire et garanti à la disposition de tous les citoyens européens, même ceux qui sont aujourd’hui privés de l’accès à un compte bancaire.

C’est un outil de souveraineté, un outil de liberté, et je vous invite à voter en faveur du mandat de négociation pour que ce beau projet devienne une réalité.
4-0205-0000.englishText:
Madam President, today we are too dependent on non-European payment methods, particularly American ones, and this dependence, dear colleagues, must end.

Private solutions are developing, and that is very well, but we must also provide the Union with a public digital, pan-European, sovereign currency, which will be the digital equivalent of our cash – an additional and guaranteed payment method available to all European citizens, even those who are currently deprived of access to a bank account.

It is a tool of sovereignty, a tool of freedom, and I invite you to vote in favour of the negotiating mandate so that this fine project becomes a reality.

4-0206-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, dear colleagues challenging the digital euro. I have listened carefully, but your arguments simply don't add up.

First, you call yourself patriots, and yet you oppose the one instrument that could loosen the grip that Donald Trump has on all our payments. If you are true European patriots, vote for the anti-Trump coin.

Second, you tell us how much you love the privacy of cash. And who doesn't love cash? And yet you oppose the one instrument that could bring that privacy and anonymity into the digital world. If you like cash, vote for the anonymous digital coin.

And third, you claim to stand with ordinary people and businesses, and yet you oppose the one instrument that would make digital payments finally affordable for your bakery, for your corner store and for your cafe. If you like your bakery, vote for the affordable digital coin.

Sovereignty, privacy, affordability – colleagues, why are you opposing these three? Think harder, stop the conspiracy theory, read the law and vote for the digital euro.

4-0207-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, se oggi pagate in contanti, domani potrete continuare a pagare in contanti, esattamente come fate oggi.

Ma, se scegliete di pagare in elettronico – in digitale – l'euro digitale vi offrirà la possibilità europea, pubblica e indipendente che i vostri dati rimangano in Europa e di pagare in Europa, piuttosto che lasciare milioni di dati e milioni di euro in commissioni passare oltreoceano, principalmente a vantaggio di Visa e Mastercard.

L'introduzione dell'euro digitale è una risposta principalmente a questo. Non vuole e non può sostituire il contante, vuole affiancarlo, sostituire invece Visa e Mastercard, offrire un'alternativa pubblica indipendente.

L'euro digitale rappresenta il tentativo di ridurre la nostra dipendenza e mente chi dice che è un regalo alle banche. L'euro digitale è il tentativo europeo di recuperare sovranità monetaria e autonomia strategica. Proprio coloro che si dicono sovranisti e patrioti dovrebbero votarlo. Se siete sovranisti con i confini, dovreste esserlo anche sui dati dei cittadini europei.

Votate per l'euro digitale.
4-0207-0000.englishText:
Madam President, honourable colleagues, if today you pay in cash, tomorrow you can continue to pay in cash, exactly as you do today.

But, if you choose to pay electronically - digitally - the digital euro will offer you the European, public and independent possibility for your data to remain in Europe and to pay in Europe, rather than letting millions of data and millions of euros in commissions pass overseas, mainly to the benefit of Visa and Mastercard.

The introduction of the digital euro is a response mainly to this. It does not want to and cannot replace cash, it wants to flank it instead, to replace Visa and Mastercard, and to offer a public independent alternative.

The digital euro represents the attempt to reduce our dependence and those who say it is a gift to banks are lying. The digital euro is the European attempt to recover monetary sovereignty and strategic autonomy. Precisely those who call themselves sovereignists and patriots should vote for it. If you are sovereignists with borders, you should also be sovereignists regarding the data of European citizens.

Vote for the digital euro.

4-0208-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, verehrte Kollegen! Der vorgeschlagene Rechtsrahmen für den digitalen Euro umfasst Elemente wie verpflichtende Akzeptanzregelungen, die Einbindung digitaler Identitätssysteme, Identifikationsmechanismen sowie weitergehende Eingriffe in Zahlungsmarktstrukturen. Darüber hinaus könnte das Vorhaben erhebliche Auswirkungen auf das bestehende Bankensystem und die Struktur privater Einlagen haben sowie das Verhältnis zwischen Bürgern und öffentlichen Währungsinstitutionen grundlegend verändern.

Die Gesamtheit dieser Elemente begründet erhebliche Zweifel daran, dass Artikel 133 AEUV allein eine ausreichende Rechtsgrundlage für den derzeitig vorgesehenen Rechtsrahmen darstellt. Der digitale Euro birgt daher die Gefahr, den Umfang der unionsrechtlichen Währungskompetenz durch eine extensive Auslegung des Artikels 133 AEUV über die in den Verträgen vorgesehenen Grenzen hinaus auszudehnen. Ein Vorhaben mit derart weitschreitenden Auswirkungen auf Zahlungssysteme, Marktstrukturen, das Bankensystem und Zahlungsmechanismen darf in seiner derzeitigen Form nicht unterstützt werden.
4-0208-0000.englishText:
Madam President, esteemed colleagues! The proposed legal framework for the digital euro includes elements such as mandatory acceptance rules, the integration of digital identity systems, identification mechanisms, and further interventions in payment market structures. Furthermore, the project could have significant impacts on the existing banking system and the structure of private deposits, as well as fundamentally altering the relationship between citizens and public monetary institutions.

The totality of these elements gives rise to considerable doubts that Article 133 TFEU alone constitutes a sufficient legal basis for the currently proposed legal framework. The digital euro therefore carries the risk of extending the scope of Union competence in monetary law beyond the limits provided for in the Treaties through an expansive interpretation of Article 133 TFEU. A project with such far-reaching impacts on payment systems, market structures, the banking system, and payment mechanisms must not be supported in its current form.

4-0242-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, doamnă comisar, doamnelor și domnilor colegi, mulțumesc tuturor pentru participarea la această dezbatere despre un subiect foarte important, care frământă spațiul public agricol la nivel european. Stimați colegi, acum 20 de ani, un fermier din România își putea cumpăra o casă cu bani obținuți din vânzarea lânii de la 600 de oi. Astăzi, același fermier este obligat să scoată bani din buzunar doar pentru a scăpa de lâna produsă în propria fermă, transformând astfel o resursă valoroasă într-o povară economică.

În țările nordice, de exemplu, valoarea pierdută anual din cauza nevalorificării potențialului lânii este estimată la 120 de milioane de euro. Se pune întrebarea firească: cum am ajuns aici? Nu pentru că lâna și-a pierdut utilitatea. Ea poate să fie folosită în industria textilă, în construcții, ca material izolator, dar și ca îngrășământ natural. Însă problema este că legislația europeană a transformat valorificarea lânii într-un proces complicat și costisitor.

Regulamentul european 1069/2009 și Regulamentul 142/2011 clasifică lâna drept subprodus de origine animală din categoria 3, alături de sânge, de exemplu, de pene sau alte subproduse. Această clasificare impune condiții stricte și costisitoare de manipulare, depozitare, transport și procesare, inclusiv atunci când lâna provine de la animalele sănătoase. Apare întrebarea firească: cum justifică Comisia Europeană faptul că lâna provenită de la animalele sănătoase ajunge să fie tratată mai mult ca un deșeu decât o resursă agricolă valoroasă?

În același timp, din cauza cerințelor de mediu tot mai stricte și costurilor greu de suportat, Europa și-a pierdut o mare parte din capacitatea de spălare și procesare a lânii. Rezultatul este absurd. Producem lână în Europa, o transportăm mii de km până în Turcia pentru a fi spălată, apoi o aducem înapoi. Plătim mai mult, transportăm mai mult, poluăm mai mult și ne distrugem propria industrie, în timp ce vorbim despre durabilitate și economie circulară.

În aceste condiții, întreb Comisia Europeană dacă are în vedere să revizuiască de urgență regulamentele în cauză și să elimine barierele disproporționate aplicate lânii, deoarece o legislație care transformă o resursă valoroasă într-o povară economică nu protejează agricultura europeană, ci o condamnă. Fermierii, doamnă comisar, nu cer privilegii, ci doar dreptul de a valorifica munca și produsele lor.
4-0242-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, thank you all for participating in this debate on a very important subject that worries the agricultural public space at the European level. Dear colleagues, 20 years ago, a farmer in Romania could buy a house with money obtained from the sale of wool from 600 sheep. Today, the same farmer is forced to take money out of his pocket just to get rid of the wool produced on his own farm, thus transforming a valuable resource into an economic burden.

In the Nordic countries, for example, the value lost annually due to the failure to capitalize on the potential of wool is estimated at 120 million euros. The natural question arises: how did we get here? Not because wool has lost its utility. It can be used in the textile industry, in construction, as insulating material, but also as a natural fertilizer. But the problem is that European legislation has turned the valorization of wool into a complicated and costly process.

European Regulation 1069/2009 and Regulation 142/2011 classify wool as a Category 3 animal byproduct, alongside blood, for example, feathers or other byproducts. This classification imposes strict and costly conditions for handling, storage, transport and processing, even when the wool comes from healthy animals. The natural question arises: how does the European Commission justify the fact that wool from healthy animals ends up being treated more as waste than a valuable agricultural resource?

At the same time, due to increasingly stringent environmental requirements and hard-to-bear costs, Europe has lost a large part of its wool washing and processing capacity. The result is absurd. We produce wool in Europe, we transport it thousands of km to Turkey to be washed, then we bring it back. We pay more, we transport more, we pollute more and we destroy our own industry, while we talk about sustainability and circular economy.

Under these conditions, I ask the European Commission if it is considering urgently reviewing the regulations in question and eliminating the disproportionate barriers applied to wool, because legislation that turns a valuable resource into an economic burden does not protect European agriculture, but condemns it. Farmers, Madam Commissioner, do not ask for privileges, but only the right to capitalize on their work and products.

4-0243-0000.sourceText:
Trebuie să spun că este o onoare să conduc această dezbatere. Vin din familii de ciobani, din zona Sibiului, așa că este important, doamnă comisar...

It's very important to take this matter very seriously. I invite you to the microphone to speak to the sector and speak to our colleagues.
4-0243-0000.englishText:
I must say it is an honor to lead this debate. I come from shepherd families, from the Sibiu area, so it is important, Madam Commissioner...

It's very important to take this matter very seriously. I invite you to the microphone to speak to the sector and speak to our colleagues.

4-0245-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, dear Members, first of all, my thanks go to the honourable Members who tabled this oral question, especially MEP Buda.

The Commission recognises in our livestock strategy, which we just adopted this Tuesday, by-products such as wool or manure are not a waste, but rather a resource that has value and serves multiple purposes in a circular bioeconomy. This happened this Tuesday. By enabling the production of bio-based products and supporting circular resource use, wool contributes to the objectives of the bioeconomy and the circular economy. These products also create environmental, economic and rural development benefits.

In the meantime, the Regulation on animal by-products provides proportionate risk-based rules to protect animal and public health. The regulation includes flexible options to collect, transport and store wool, as well as options for other uses like fertilisers. In line with international standards and based on available scientific knowledge, wool is categorised among the animal by-products that represent the lowest but not insignificant risk for public and animal health. It is in the least restrictive category, with a wider range of options for its safe use and valorisation.

Many farmers do struggle to sell wool in the textile industry, which is itself facing difficulties. That means many farmers are instead disposing of their wool, but this is not stipulated by the Animal By-Products Regulation. Instead, it is a decision by farmers and businesses in the wool sector, forced by the problems of the textile industry.

Let me assure you that the Commission continues to work on providing new opportunities for wool producers. As announced in our livestock strategy, the Commission will work on facilitating the use of animal by-products without jeopardising animal health, food and feed safety standards and review potential regulatory bottlenecks. As they stand, animal by-product implementing rules already offer opportunities for different uses of wool. These include making fertilisers and other products from wool as long as specified animal diseases are not present.

The Commission is also exploring new options to help wool producers. This was part of the bioeconomy strategy that we adopted in November last year. That strategy includes a dedicated EU CAP network focus group on innovative and sustainable ways to strengthen the role of farmers in revitalising the European wool value chain. We will continue to look into these sorts of possibilities.

We are committed to supporting farmers to enable different uses of wool, while always accounting for any associated health risks. We are committed to maintaining the EU's highest standards for public health and animal health. We are also committed to fewer restrictions for farmers and wool producers whenever health risks and effective risk mitigations allow it. But we also need to be ready for the possibility of disease outbreaks because the level of risk is higher if that happens. This is what the Animal By-Product Regulation provides for.

I will now listen to your views.

4-0246-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, Commissioner, a recent study in Ireland found that almost half of our farmers want to add value to their wool, and yet more than 80 % are unable to do so. The big question is: why? Because there are too few markets, too little processing capacity and too much unnecessary bureaucracy.

For many sheep farmers, wool has become a cost rather than an income, and you'll hear that from colleagues today. Yet across Ireland, there are a number of ambassadors working incredibly hard to bring value to wool. In Galway there is Blátnaid Gallagher, who established the Galway Wool Co-op with LEADER support, connecting farmers with new markets for their wool and promoting the Galway wool as a sustainable and locally grown material.

Also in Galway we have Michael Burke, founder of Woolow, which is producing natural wool pillows that offer an alternative to synthetics for people with hay fever and dust allergies. Roscommon-owned business FertaWool is transforming wool into organic fertiliser pellets that can hold up to 20 times their weight in water, helping crops withstand droughts and extreme heat. Once again in Galway, we have Katarina Hruskova, who's leading a crowdfunding campaign to reopen a wool mill, bringing back much needed processing capacity for local farmers.

These are not just inspiring local projects; these are businesses creating tangible jobs in our rural areas. They unlock the value of a resource we already produce. So why are we making it so difficult? Too often, wool from healthy sheep is treated more like a waste than a valuable natural product, which we've heard from MEP Daniel Buda. That means more cost for farmers, more barriers for processors and fewer opportunities for our rural businesses.

If we're serious about supporting farmers, strengthening our rural economies and building a genuine circular economy, then our policies have to reflect those ambitions. That means cutting unnecessary red tape. It means investing in local processing. And it means creating new markets for wool. Let's stop treating wool as a problem. It's part of the solution.

4-0247-0000.sourceText:
�� Г-н Председател, днешният дебат е доказателство, че за Европейския парламент е важна всяка тема, която засяга хората.

На пръв поглед повдигнатите въпроси за вълната може да изглеждат чисто технически, но за много фермери в Европа, особено в планинските, полупланинските и по-бедните региони, това е въпрос на оцеляване. Овцевъдството не е просто един от секторите на животновъдството, то поддържа живота в селските райони, пази пасищата, съхранява местните породи и традиции, осигурява доходи там, където алтернативите често са малко. Това важи с особена сила за страни като България и за много региони в Източна и Южна Европа, където малките стопани продължават да носят основната тежест.

И точно тези стопани днес са поставени в абсурдна ситуация. Те са длъжни да стрижат овцете си, това е необходимо за здравето и хуманното отношение към животните, но след това вълната често не носи доход, а се превръща в разход. Стопаните плащат за стрижба, а после за съхранение, транспорт или дори за унищожаване, защото пазарът е слаб, преработката е недостатъчна, а правилата са прекалено тежки за реалния риск. Това не е справедливо. Вълната е естествен, възобновяем, биоразградим и устойчив материал.

В същото време Европа говори все повече за кръгова икономика, за устойчиви текстилни продукти и за намаляване на отпадъците. Но какъв е смисълът да говорим за устойчивост, ако оставяме собствената си европейска вълна да се обезценява, докато пазарът се залива с евтини и синтетични материи, бърза мода и дрехи, които се носят няколко пъти и след това се изхвърлят? Разбира се, трябва да бъдем отговорни и по отношение на здравето на животните. В България и в региона фермерите добре знаят колко тежки последици могат да имат заболявания като шарка по овцете и козите, чума по дребните преживни животни, син език. Една епидемия може да унищожи стада, доходи и години труд.

Затова не става дума за премахване на контрола. Става дума за по-разумен контрол. Комисията трябва да предложи по пропорционален, ясен и основан на риска режим за вълната от здрави животни. Когато няма реален ветеринарен риск, правилата не трябва да правят събирането и използването на вълната икономически безсмислено. Малките стопани не могат да бъдат третирани като големи индустриални оператори. Те нямат същия административен капацитет, нямат същия достъп до пазари и не могат да поемат всяка допълнителна тежест.

Затова очакваме от Комисията конкретни действия. Първо, преглед на действащите правила, така че вълната от здрави животни да бъде третирана като ресурс, а не като отпадък. Второ, подкрепа за регионални центрове за събиране, сортиране и първична обработка на вълна. Това е особено важно за малките стопанства, които поотделно не могат да изградят такава инфраструктура. Трето, по-добро свързване на земеделската политика с текстилната стратегия на Европейския съюз. Ако говорим за устойчив текстил, европейската вълна трябва да има реално място в тази политика. Четвърто, подкрепа за кооперативи, местни преработватели и малки предприятия, които могат да върнат добавената стойност в регионите, вместо суровината да бъде изоставена или продавана на безценица. И пето, по-силна ветеринарна подкрепа, ранно откриване на заболявания, по-добра трансгранична координация и справедливи обезщетения, когато стопаните са засегнати от мерки за контрол на болести.

Това не е носталгия по миналото, това е въпрос на разумна индустриална, земеделска и екологична политика. Ако Европа иска да бъде по-устойчива, тя трябва да започне с ресурсите, които вече има. Ако искаме да запазим живота в селските райони, трябва да помогнем на малките стопани не само да оцелеят, но и да получават справедлива стойност за своя труд. Ако искаме да ограничим бързата мода и културата на изхвърляне, трябва да подкрепим естествените и трайни материали. Овцете така или иначе трябва да бъдат стригани, въпросът е дали европейската политика ще остави вълната да бъде проблем за фермера или ще помогне тя отново да стане ценен продукт за Европа.
4-0247-0000.englishText:
Mr President, today's debate is proof that every topic affecting people is important to the European Parliament.

At first glance, the issues raised about wool may seem purely technical, but for many farmers in Europe, especially in mountain, semi-mountain and poorer regions, this is a matter of survival. Sheep farming is not just one of the livestock sectors, it sustains life in rural areas, preserves pastures, preserves local breeds and traditions, and provides income where alternatives are often few. This is especially true for countries like Bulgaria and for many regions in Eastern and Southern Europe, where smallholders continue to bear the brunt.

And it is precisely these farmers who are placed in an absurd situation today. They are obliged to shear their sheep, this is necessary for animal health and welfare, but afterwards the wool often brings no income, but turns into an expense. Farmers pay for shearing, and then for storage, transport or even destruction because the market is weak, processing is insufficient, and the rules are too burdensome for the real risk. This is not fair. Wool is a natural, renewable, biodegradable and sustainable material.

At the same time, Europe talks more and more about circular economy, sustainable textile products and waste reduction. But what is the point of talking about sustainability if we let our own European wool depreciate while the market is flooded with cheap and synthetic materials, fast fashion and clothes that are worn a few times and then thrown away? Of course, we must also be responsible regarding animal health. In Bulgaria and the region, farmers know very well what severe consequences diseases such as sheep and goat pox, peste des petits ruminants, and bluetongue can have. An epidemic can destroy herds, incomes and years of work.

Therefore, this is not about removing controls. It is about smarter controls. The Commission must propose a proportionate, clear and risk-based regime for wool from healthy animals. When there is no real veterinary risk, the rules should not make the collection and use of wool economically pointless. Smallholders cannot be treated as large industrial operators. They do not have the same administrative capacity, they do not have the same access to markets, and they cannot bear every additional burden.

Therefore, we expect concrete actions from the Commission. First, a review of the current rules so that wool from healthy animals is treated as a resource rather than waste. Second, support for regional collection, sorting and primary processing centers for wool. This is especially important for small holdings that cannot individually build such infrastructure. Third, a better connection of agricultural policy with the European Union's textile strategy. If we talk about sustainable textiles, European wool must have a real place in this policy. Fourth, support for cooperatives, local processors and small businesses that can bring added value back to the regions instead of the raw material being abandoned or sold for a pittance. And fifth, stronger veterinary support, early detection of diseases, better cross-border coordination and fair compensation when farmers are affected by disease control measures.

This is not nostalgia for the past, this is a matter of sound industrial, agricultural and environmental policy. If Europe wants to be more sustainable, it must start with the resources it already has. If we want to preserve life in rural areas, we must help smallholders not only survive, but also get fair value for their labor. If we want to curb fast fashion and throwaway culture, we must support natural and durable materials. Sheep have to be sheared anyway, the question is whether European policy will let wool be a problem for the farmer or help it become a valuable product for Europe again.

4-0248-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, ani de zile, din cauza unor reglementări absurde, lâna a fost tratată pe nedrept ca un deșeu de risc, forțând oierii să o îngroape sau să o ardă. Aceasta nu este protecția mediului, este o risipă curată. Regulamentul european 1069/2009 tratează lâna ca pe un deșeu, în loc să o vadă ca pe o resursă strategică valoroasă. Nu avem nevoie de constrângeri ideologice care îngroapă tradițiile și sufocă fermierii, ci de soluții inteligente, realiste.

Lâna are nenumărate avantaje și aplicații fantastice. Este un izolator termic excepțional pentru construcții, este un îngrășământ organic excelent în agricultură și o materie primă sustenabilă pentru textile. Omenirea se îmbracă de mii de ani cu lână și, deși combatem poluarea, practic, blocajul lânii nu face decât să încurajeze alte materiale sintetice, precum plasticul, și să accentueze poluarea.

Doamnă comisar, nu este suficient să avem o strategie europeană, din păcate. Vă solicităm un cadru de reglementare actualizat care să recalifice și să sprijine financiar valorificarea lânii. Este timpul să facem dreptate pentru crescătorii de animale și pentru toți cetățenii europeni care au dreptul să folosească produse naturale și sănătoase.
4-0248-0000.englishText:
Mr President, for years, due to absurd regulations, wool has been unfairly treated as a risk waste, forcing sheep farmers to bury or burn it. This is not environmental protection, it is sheer waste. European Regulation 1069/2009 treats wool as waste, instead of seeing it as a valuable strategic resource. We do not need ideological constraints that bury traditions and suffocate farmers, but intelligent, realistic solutions.

Wool has countless advantages and fantastic applications. It is an exceptional thermal insulator for construction, an excellent organic fertilizer in agriculture, and a sustainable raw material for textiles. Humanity has been clothing itself with wool for thousands of years and, although we are fighting pollution, practically, the blockage of wool only encourages other synthetic materials, such as plastic, and accentuates pollution.

Madam Commissioner, unfortunately, it is not enough to have a European strategy. We ask you for an updated regulatory framework to reclassify and financially support the valorization of wool. It is time to do justice to livestock farmers and to all European citizens who have the right to use natural and healthy products.

4-0249-0000.sourceText:
A Uachtaráin, sheep farmers have a responsibility to shear their sheep for animal welfare issues, and rightly so. But Commissioner, as it stands, farmers have to pay up to EUR 3.50 per sheep for shearing. In other words, it is a cost, and at the end of that shearing exercise, they have a product that's defined as being waste, as being a nuisance. I believe at this stage we really have to address this fundamental issue.

We have to accept from the very start that wool is a product that has huge potential, and in the past was a very valuable product that was used widely across Europe, primarily in the area of textiles and in other forms. But with the modern technologies that are available to us, the modern building programmes that we use, there are certainly opportunities for us to look at ways of being innovative and of creating new ways to use wool.

So when we look at the livestock strategy and it outlines some of the significant challenges that have been placed on the livestock sector, the area of sheep is quite evident. There are declining numbers, very often in regions that need not just sheep, but the people to look after them. And this is having a knock‑on negative effect in peripheral regions and remote regions of Europe that traditionally would have been very active in the context of sheep farming and shepherding.

So I would urge the Commission to look at the issue of the blocks that are being put on us in terms of the definition of what wool is, and if it is still the issue that it is creating difficulties, that we would reclassify to allow wool to be seen in a more positive light.

We also need to develop markets and processing capacity. In Ireland at one time, Commissioner, we had an exceptionally strong woollen industry. In 1984, when the National Wool Council – An Chomhairle Olla – was abolished as a cost‑saving exercise, we exported 5 895 tonnes at a value of 14 million. In today's terms that would be the equivalent of a value of 30 million. In 2019, we exported 5 641 tonnes, and its value was only 6.8 million. So there has been a significant decrease in the value of wool itself.

I would urge the Commission to look at this in a very proactive way. There are many people doing good work in Ireland in promoting wool.

Ba mhaith liom mo bhuíochas a thabhairt do John Joe Fitzgerald as Corca Dhuibhne, Contae Chiarraí, as ucht an mhéid oibre atá sé a dhéanamh ar son an tionscail olla in Éirinn - John Joe, Leas-Uachtarán den INHFA.

4-0252-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin! Und danke an alle Kolleginnen und Kollegen, die bei dieser letzten Debatte am letzten Tag vor der Sommerpause hier in Straßburg noch den Weg ins Plenum gefunden haben. Wir diskutieren ein Thema – Wolle. Man kann sagen, ja, wie detailliert wollen wir hier jetzt eingehen auf die Themen, aber Wolle ist ein zentrales Thema, das viele Auswirkungen auf unsere Landwirtschaft hat.

Besonders Landwirte in benachteiligten Gebieten sind in die Schafhaltung involviert. In vielen Bereichen ist nicht mehr viel mehr möglich als Schafhaltung, und es sind mitunter die am geringsten verdienenden landwirtschaftlichen Betriebe, die heute noch Schafhaltung betreiben. Und es ist eine der letzten Möglichkeiten, überhaupt noch ein Einkommen zu erzielen in benachteiligten Gebieten. Wie der Kollege Billy Kelleher schon dargestellt hat: Die Kosten, ein Schaf zu scheren, sind größer als das, was man für die Wolle bekommt.

Ein Thema, das noch nicht beleuchtet wurde: Schafhaltung hat eine äußerst positive Auswirkung auf die Biodiversität. Es ist eine der wenigen menschlichen Tätigkeiten, die zu mehr Biodiversität führen und nicht zu weniger Biodiversität. Aber bitte, Kommission, gehen Sie hier nicht raus und sagen Sie: Hier ist alles in Ordnung, es gibt hier nichts zu sehen.

Wir haben ein Problem, und das Problem ist, dass wir erstens zu wenig Verarbeitung haben für die Wolle, und zweitens haben wir das Problem, dass Wolle nicht direkt als Dünger verwendet werden kann. Wenn ich die Wolle zuerst transportieren, waschen, reinigen und pelletieren muss, dann ist es nicht mehr lohnend. Ich verstehe, dass man die Wolle nicht über Grenzen hinweg transportieren kann, aus sanitären Gründen; aber lassen Sie uns doch in der Landwirtschaft, im Gemüseanbau, im Obstbau die Wolle direkt als Dünger verwenden. Da bestehen keine Risiken, und es wäre eine sofortige Lösung für ein Problem, das wir quer durch die Europäische Union haben. Ich bitte Sie darum: Sehen Sie sich das an!
4-0252-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner! And thanks to all the colleagues who still found their way to the plenary for this last debate on the last day before the summer break here in Strasbourg. We are discussing a topic - wool. One can say, yes, how detailed do we want to go into the topics now, but wool is a central topic that has many impacts on our agriculture.

Particularly farmers in disadvantaged areas are involved in sheep farming. In many areas, not much more is possible than sheep farming, and they are sometimes the lowest-earning agricultural businesses that still engage in sheep farming today. And it is one of the last opportunities to still generate any income in disadvantaged areas. As my colleague Billy Kelleher has already outlined: The cost of shearing a sheep is greater than what you get for the wool.

One topic that has not yet been highlighted: Sheep farming has an extremely positive effect on biodiversity. It is one of the few human activities that leads to more biodiversity and not less biodiversity. But please, Commission, do not walk out here and say: Everything is fine here, there is nothing to see here.

We have a problem, and the problem is that firstly we have too little processing for the wool, and secondly we have the problem that wool cannot be used directly as a fertilizer. If I first have to transport, wash, clean, and pelletize the wool, then it is no longer worthwhile. I understand that wool cannot be transported across borders for sanitary reasons; but let us use the wool directly as fertilizer in agriculture, in vegetable growing, in fruit growing. There are no risks involved, and it would be an immediate solution to a problem that we have right across the European Union. I ask you: Please look into this!

4-0253-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, meine Damen und Herren! Die Notwendigkeit der heutigen Debatte ist ein weiterer Beleg dafür, dass sich die EU‑Kommission meilenweit von der Wirklichkeit der Menschen entfernt hat. Es ist völliger Unsinn, dass das wertvolle natürliche Produkt Schafswolle gemäß einer Verordnung der Kommission noch immer als tierisches Nebenprodukt der Kategorie 3 eingestuft wird – Wolle also als Abfallprodukt auf einer Stufe mit Blut oder Häuten. Mehr Verachtung für den traditionellen Beruf des Schäfers und für Wolle als wertvolle landwirtschaftliche Ressource ist fast nicht mehr möglich.

Eigentlich wird diese Verachtung nur noch getoppt davon, dass rund 700 Kollegen der heutigen wichtigen Debatte hier fernbleiben. Jetzt werden die Debatten sogar noch eingeschränkt, sodass man bis 20.00 Uhr die letzte Rede gehalten haben soll.

Meine sehr verehrten Damen und Herren, ich bin jetzt seit knapp zehn Jahren Mitglied der AfD und muss mir diesen Schwachsinn hier seit zehn Jahren anhören – dass wir die Demokratie verächtlich machen würden. Jetzt haben Sie am Dienstag hier mit Mehrheit beschlossen, dass Sie ein Prüfverfahren gegen unsere ESN‑Partei einleiten wollen, weil Sie Zweifel haben an den EU‑Werten.

Wenn Ihre EU‑Werte nunmehr Kontrollwut, Steuerverschwendung, Arbeitsverweigerung, Ausgrenzung unangenehmer politischer Konkurrenz oder aktive Förderung von Waffenlieferungen in Kriegsgebiete und damit verbunden Förderung von Korruption in diesen Kriegsgebieten sind, ja, dann bestehen noch erhebliche Zweifel an der Kommission und an gewissen linken Fraktionen hier im Parlament.

Zurück zur Wolle. Ich komme aus einem kleinen Bundesland in Deutschland, Sachsen‑Anhalt. Wie erklären Sie denn bitte dem Schäfer in Sachsen‑Anhalt, der bei Wind und Wetter 365 Tage im Jahr seine Schafe betreut, dass sich hier im Parlament offenbar kaum jemand für sein Schicksal interessiert? Wie erklären Sie diesem Schäfer, dass sein Produkt von der EU‑Kommission seit Jahren als Nebenprodukt und damit faktisch als Abfall eingestuft wird? Und wie erklären Sie diesem Schäfer mit seinen knapp 300 Schafen, ob er seinen Beruf in Zukunft aufgrund drohender neuer Bürokratie oder aber hoher Kosten durch den Herdenschutz noch wirtschaftlich ausüben kann?

Wolle ist eben nicht nur ein Nebenprodukt. Mützen, Schals, Handschuhe, Pullover, Jacken, Mäntel, Kleider, Hausschuhe, Hüte, Hosen, Matratzen, Kissen, Flugzeugsitze, Feuerwehruniformen, Kuscheltiere, Windeln, Billardtischbeläge, Puppen oder Teppiche – dies alles und vieles mehr wird mit hochwertiger Wolle produziert und damit aufgewertet.

Jetzt wäre es an der Zeit, dass wir hier im Europäischen Parlament auch die Schäfer wirtschaftlich stärken und die Einordnung der Wolle aufwerten. Wer Schafe mag, muss Schafe schützen; wer Wolle will, muss Schäfer stützen!
4-0253-0000.englishText:
Mr President, ladies and gentlemen! The necessity of today's debate is further proof that the EU Commission has moved miles away from the reality of the people's lives. It is complete nonsense that the valuable natural product sheep's wool is still classified by a Commission regulation as an animal byproduct of category 3 - meaning wool as a waste product on the same level as blood or hides. It is almost impossible to show more contempt for the traditional profession of the shepherd and for wool as a valuable agricultural resource.

Actually, this contempt is only topped by the fact that around 700 colleagues are staying away from today's important debate. Now the debates are even being restricted so that the last speech is supposed to have been given by 8:00 p.m.

Ladies and gentlemen, I have been a member of the AfD for almost ten years now and have had to listen to this bullshit here for ten years - that we would show contempt for democracy. Now, on Tuesday, you decided by a majority here that you want to initiate infringement or review proceedings against our ESN party because you have doubts about EU values.

If your EU values are now a mania for control, waste of taxpayers' money, refusal to work, exclusion of unwelcome political competition, or active promotion of arms deliveries to war zones and the associated promotion of corruption in those war zones, yes, then there are still considerable doubts about the Commission and certain left-wing parliamentary groups here in Parliament.

Back to the wool. I come from a small federal state in Germany, Saxony-Anhalt. How on earth do you explain to the shepherd in Saxony-Anhalt, who tends to his sheep in wind and weather 365 days a year, that apparently hardly anyone in this Parliament is interested in his fate? How do you explain to this shepherd that his product has been classified by the EU Commission as a byproduct and thus practically as waste for years? 4-0254-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Vielen Dank an Maria Walsh, Daniel Buda und Herbert Dorfmann, dass sie diese Debatte initiiert haben. Wir alle wissen, Europa ist wahrlich nicht mit Rohstoffen gesegnet. Wolle ist so ein Rohstoff: vielfältig einsetzbar, regional verfügbar, wasserabweisend, schwer entflammbar, biologisch abbaubar. Und was tun wir? Wir werfen die Wolle trotzdem einfach weg. Oder wir verkaufen sie zu Dumpingpreisen nach China. Die Folge: Bei deutschen Schäfern zum Beispiel macht der Erlös aus Wolle weniger als 2 % des Einkommens aus. Die Chinesen kaufen dagegen weltweit Wolle auf; dort ist Kleidung aus Wolle ein Statussymbol.

Es ist Zeit, dass wir den Wert unserer Wolle wieder erkennen. Das Timing ist gut; ich setze ja einige Hoffnungen in die irische Ratspräsidentschaft. In meiner Heimat Thüringen gibt es sehr interessante Ansätze, um Wolle zusammen mit Hanf zu verweben. Das Ergebnis ähnelt Baumwolle, ist aber nachhaltiger.

Wir müssen solche Projekte fördern und vorantreiben; es geht dabei auch um Wertschöpfungsketten und Arbeitsplätze. Verbraucher sind bereit, mehr Geld für nachhaltige, regional produzierte Kleidung auszugeben, und ebenso besteht in der Baubranche Bedarf an nachhaltigen Dämmstoffen. 4-0254-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear colleagues! Many thanks to Maria Walsh, Daniel Buda and Herbert Dorfmann for initiating this debate. When I first looked more deeply into the subject of wool, I couldn't believe what we as the EU are doing here – or rather, not doing.

We all know that Europe is truly not blessed with raw materials. Wool is one such raw material: versatile, locally available, water-repellent, flame-retardant, biodegradable. And what do we do? We simply throw the wool away anyway. Or we sell it to China at dumping prices. The consequence: for German shepherds, for example, the revenue from wool accounts for less than 2% of income. The Chinese, on the other hand, buy up wool worldwide; clothing made from wool is a status symbol there.

It is time for us to recognize the value of our wool again. The timing is good; I have some hopes for the Irish Presidency. In my home region of Thuringia, there are very interesting approaches to weaving wool together with hemp. The result is similar to cotton, but more sustainable.

We must promote and drive forward such projects; this is also about value chains and jobs. Consumers are willing to spend more money on sustainable, locally produced clothing, and there is also a demand for sustainable insulation materials in the construction sector. We also frequently discuss scarce fertilizer for our agriculture in this House. Since wool has a high nitrogen content, it is ideally suited in the form of pellets as a long-term fertilizer.

Much is possible if we now adapt the legal situation. I therefore ask the Commission to reconsider the classification of wool in Category 3 in the animal by-products regulation. Wool simply does not belong in the same risk group as animal blood or hides. Wool is not a danger, it is an opportunity: let's use it!

Mr President! How many more times will we hear lofty slogans about the Green Deal, while EU regulations punish what is truly ecological? Raw wool – a natural, renewable and fully biodegradable raw material – is still classified as waste. Surely this is absurd. Sheep farmers pay for the storage and disposal of wool. Why? Mr President, today it's easier to import virgin polyester than to move European wool around. The textile strategy made a promise: textiles on the European market should be sustainable, recyclable and, to a large extent, of recycled fibres. But wool, today, shows us how far we are from delivering on that promise.

We adapted health rules to stop animal disease spreading, rightly so. But wool from perfectly healthy sheep was swept into these same rules. So, in practice, raw wool cannot be sold or moved around like any other farm product. So instead of becoming a beautiful textile, it is thrown away. The paradox does not stop at the farm gate, because when wool comes back to us years later as worn‑out garments it hits the second wall: waste legislation.

There are 27 interpretations of what a textile is, if it's waste or it's a resource. Heavy procedures – every time feedstock crosses a border to a recycler. Two different rule books, the same result and natural recyclable material is treated like a liability at both ends of its life. Meanwhile, cheap fossil‑based synthetics that fuel fast fashion circulate freely all around Europe.

So the Commission should answer the question put forward on the table today, promise during this mandate a specific and proportionate framework for wool and, at the same time, also deliver on the waste criteria with the Circular Economy Act this fall.

Domnule președinte, stimată doamnă comisar, lâna este una dintre cele mai vechi și mai sustenabile resurse naturale ale Europei.
