Azi însă, din cauza reglementărilor europene aberante, ciobanii din România, de exemplu, efectiv aruncă lâna la gunoi, ceea ce este ilogic. Avem nevoie de modificarea normelor pentru a facilita colectarea, transportul și procesarea lânii. În același timp, trebuie sprijinite, în special în zonele rurale, investițiile în infrastructura de procesare și reciclare a lânii, ceea ce ar produce mai multe locuri de muncă, ar reduce risipa și ar oferi fermierilor resurse suplimentare de venit.

Lâna este regenerabilă, biodegradabilă și reprezintă o alternativă sustenabilă la materialele sintetice. În contextul Pactului verde european și al economiei circulare, este aberant să fie irosită această resursă naturală doar pentru că birocrații europeni nu știu câte picioare au oile.
4-0263-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear Commissioner, wool is one of Europe's oldest and most sustainable natural resources. Instead of being valued as a resource with significant economic and ecological potential, however, for 17 years wool has been considered agricultural waste in Europe, which is an aberration. If we keep talking about the circular economy, wool is the best example of a product to be processed in such an economy.

Our ancestors in Romania have given circular economic utility to wool for thousands of years. Today, however, due to aberrant European regulations, shepherds in Romania, for example, effectively throw wool in the trash, which is illogical. We need to amend the rules to facilitate the collection, transport and processing of wool. At the same time, investments in wool processing and recycling infrastructure must be supported, especially in rural areas, which would produce more jobs, reduce waste and provide farmers with additional sources of income.

Wool is renewable, biodegradable and represents a sustainable alternative to synthetic materials. In the context of the European Green Deal and the circular economy, it is aberrant for this natural resource to be wasted just because European bureaucrats do not know how many legs sheep have.

4-0265-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! Panie Komisarzu! Hodowla owiec jest fundamentem wielu terenów górskich w Polsce, moim kraju, od Podhala, Beskidów, przez Bieszczady do Sudetów. To nie tylko produkcja żywności, ochrona krajobrazu, bioróżnorodności, ale również europejskiego dziedzictwa kulturowego. Jednakże, jak wiemy, w Polsce hodowcy otrzymują 0,35 euro za kilogram wełny, podczas gdy strzyżenie jednej owcy kosztuje 3,70 euro. Oznacza to, że jest to proceder absolutnie nieopłacalny. Naturalny surowiec staje się zatem odpadem, choć Unia promuje gospodarkę o obiegu zamkniętym.

Dlatego, Panie Komisarzu, moje pytanie jest zasadnicze: jakie konkretne działania podejmie Komisja Europejska, aby przywrócić europejskiej wełnie wartość rynkową, poprawić dochody hodowców, ochronić tradycyjne pasterstwo w regionach górskich w Polsce i w całej Europie? To bardzo ważny problem. Jestem posłem wybranym z terenów górskich. Spotykam się z tymi sprawami bardzo często i to jest właśnie apel parlamentarzysty z terenów górskich, aby Komisja Europejska zajęła się tym problemem.
4-0265-0000.englishText:
Mr President! Commissioner! Sheep farming is the foundation of many mountainous areas in Poland, my country, from Podhale, the Beskids, through the Bieszczady to the Sudetenland. This is not only food production, landscape protection, biodiversity, but also European cultural heritage. However, as we know, in Poland breeders receive 0.35 euro per kilogram of wool, while shearing one sheep costs 3.70 euro. This means that this practice is absolutely unprofitable. The natural raw material therefore becomes waste, although the Union promotes a circular economy.

Therefore, Commissioner, my question is fundamental: what specific actions will the European Commission take to restore market value to European wool, improve the income of breeders, protect traditional pastoralism in mountain regions in Poland and across Europe? This is a very important problem. I am an MEP elected from mountainous areas. I encounter these matters very often and this is precisely the appeal of a parliamentarian from mountainous areas for the European Commission to address this problem.

4-0266-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, liebe Menschen Europas! Ich freue mich, als letzter Redner dem einen oder anderen hier noch ein paar gute Gedanken mitzugeben in die Sommerpause.

Herr Bausemer, ich bewundere ja immer wieder die mentale Akrobatik, die Sie hier betreiben in diesem Plenarsaal. Sie sprachen darüber, dass Abgeordnete ihre Arbeit nicht machen und hier Steuergelder verschwenden. Ich möchte Sie darauf hinweisen, dass Sie selbst nach den offiziellen Daten des Parlaments an 25 % der Abstimmungen in diesem Plenarsaal nicht teilnehmen; das geht besser. Ihr Busenfreund, der Herr Droese, nimmt nur an 7 % der Abstimmungen nicht teil. Ich würde sagen: Bevor Sie sich über die Abwesenheit anderer beschweren, sollten Sie den Anteil der Abstimmungen, an denen Sie teilnehmen, etwas erhöhen.

Herr Mularczyk, ich möchte Sie darauf hinweisen, dass wir als europäische Abgeordnete Abgeordnete des gesamten europäischen Volkes sind. Wir vertreten hier nicht nur Deutschland, wir vertreten alle Bürgerinnen und Bürger Europas.

Frau Kommissarin, wenn Sie sich mit Landwirtinnen und Landwirten unterhalten, dann ist es wichtig, dass diese Menschen das Gefühl bekommen, dass Sie es ehrlich meinen mit dem, was Sie sagen. Deswegen möchte ich Sie bitten, Ihre rhetorischen Fertigkeiten beim Ablesen Ihrer Rede etwas zu verbessern.
4-0266-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear people of Europe! As the final speaker, I am pleased to leave one or two good thoughts with some of you here for the summer break.

Mr Bausemer, I continually admire the mental acrobatics that you perform here in this hemicycle. You spoke about members not doing their work and wasting tax money here. I would like to point out to you that, according to the Parliament's official data yourself, you do not participate in 25% of the votes in this hemicycle; you can do better than that. Your bosom buddy, Mr Droese, does not participate in only 7% of the votes. I would say: Before you complain about the absence of others, you should increase the proportion of votes in which you participate somewhat.

Mr Mularczyk, I would like to point out to you that, as European members of Parliament, we are members of the entire European people. We do not just represent Germany here, we represent all citizens of Europe.

Madam Commissioner, when you talk to farmers, it is important that these people get the feeling that you are honest about what you are saying. Therefore, I would like to ask you to improve your rhetorical skills somewhat when reading your speech.

4-0268-0000.sourceText: Commissioner, you are welcome to use your rhetoric during your speeches, however, in a convincing and useful way for Europe's farmers.

4-0269-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, since this is the last session of this semester, maybe I can also speak a little bit more freely, if freedom can be compared at all. I am representing here my colleague, Mr Várhelyi, who is in charge of this file, but I will try my best to defend our position.

You know that I am Commissioner for the Mediterranean, but I am also Commissioner for demography, so I understand what is going on not only in urban areas, but also in rural areas. This is why I was listening to your proposals and to your concerns very carefully, and I think there is a lot of room to improve what we have been doing. So, I understand and I'll pass the message to my colleagues.

I really want to thank you, Mr Buda, for your perspectives. The debate was very constructive so far as I could hear from across the plenary. I understood your political messages, but in fact, there was support for farmers from all of you and for high standards of animal health, which can open pathways for wool producers. You know, we, as the Commission, share the same position. We are not two sides. We want farmers to be able to sell their wool while also maintaining animal health centres.

Now, a few defensives. First, while several farmers may dispose of wool as waste, that is not required by Regulation (EC) No 1069/2009. Second, the Animal By-Products Regulation provides for a specific and proportionate regulatory framework for wool to mitigate public and animal health risks. Within that framework of that Regulation, several options exist for alternative uses as fertilisers and even others, what is suggested in your oral question.

I can understand the urgency. This is why, alongside Commissioner Hansen, who is the Commissioner for agriculture, he is also involved here, we support the acceleration of practical pilots and knowledge exchange, such as the CAP network focus group, which is very important, and workable solutions can start before new rules are in place, but let's see.

I agree that the methods need to to better reflect issues such as microplastic release and biogenic carbon. The Commission is working on the revision of the environmental footprint methods to address or improve several issues that have been identified in the last year, including the wool sector.

On rural areas, once again, knowing that rural area areas cover 80 % geographically of Europe – only 20 % are urban areas, but the number of population is vice-versa, so only one third of the European population live in rural areas and two thirds in urban areas. We have to somehow balance this.

Just to make you aware, the third demographic report will be issued on 14 July, next Tuesday. I already know some results. The problem is not the number of population in Europe, but it's about how the population is distributed. This is the key problem: what are we going to do with this. So, we have to work in order to improve the environment and life for the people who live in rural areas, in order to attract, not those who have right to stay, according to the Letta report, you know, but how to attract newcomers there, and this is our responsibility and your responsibility. We have to work together.

So, we are ready to explore support for innovation and the new or modernised European wool processing and, of course, including cooperative projects that keep value in rural areas where there is a clear market potential.

We are advancing with the development of eco-design requirements, which are expected in 2027, in order to improve the environmental sustainability of apparel textile products. Although most textile products are made of polyester and cotton, products composed of wool may also be included in the scope of this initiative. The impact assessment may consider wool in the overall assessment of possible recycled content requirements and requirements on the content of bio-based fibres. Other measures could also apply to apparel textile products containing wool fibres.

To Maria Walsh, you ask about the pellets and regarding the use of wool as fertiliser pellets. The competent authorities can already authorise this at national level, I have to tell you, under the animal by-product rules.

To conclude, the Commission will analyse the final results of the focus group which we already mentioned. The Commission will also continue to monitor new treatments, new technologies, new uses and innovations that mitigate risks, and we are ready to enact these outcomes into the corresponding implementing regulation. This is what you ask, if necessary, after a risk assessment by the European Food Safety Authority.

Thank you so much and have a nice summer vacation.

4-0270-5000.sourceText:
In cadrul sedintei plenare din iulie 2026 am lansat, printr-o întrebare scrisă adresată Comisiei Europene, dezbaterea privind viitorul lânii europene.

Este inacceptabil ca un material natural, regenerabil, biodegradabil și cu un potențial economic și ecologic uriaș să fie tratat, în practică, mai degrabă ca un deșeu decât ca o resursă. În prezent, din cauza cadrului legislativ european, mulți fermieri sunt obligați să plătească pentru colectarea, depozitarea sau eliminarea lânii, deși Uniunea Europeană promovează economia circulară și utilizarea eficientă a resurselor.

Prin această întrebare scrisă am solicitat Comisiei Europene să explice de ce lâna provenită de la animale sănătoase continuă să fie tratată, în practică, mai mult ca un deșeu decât ca o resursă agricolă valoroasă și dacă intenționează să revizuiască Regulamentul (CE) nr. 1069/2009 pentru a crea un cadru de reglementare specific și proporțional pentru lână.

Lâna trebuie să redevină o resursă cu valoare economică, utilizată în agricultură, construcții, industria textilă și bioeconomie, nu o povară financiară pentru crescătorii de animale.

Voi continua să susțin măsuri concrete care reduc birocrația, valorifică resursele locale și oferă fermierilor europeni șansa de a transforma ceea ce astăzi este considerat o problemă într-o oportunitate economică.
4-0270-5000.englishText:
During the July 2026 plenary session, through a written question addressed to the European Commission, I launched the debate regarding the future of European wool.

It is unacceptable that a natural, renewable, biodegradable material with huge economic and ecological potential is treated, in practice, more like waste than a resource. Currently, due to the European legislative framework, many farmers are forced to pay for the collection, storage, or disposal of wool, even though the European Union promotes the circular economy and the efficient use of resources.

Through this written question, I asked the European Commission to explain why wool from healthy animals continues to be treated, in practice, more as waste than as a valuable agricultural resource and whether it intends to revise Regulation (EC) No 1069/2009 to create a specific and proportional regulatory framework for wool.

Wool must become once again a resource with economic value, used in agriculture, construction, the textile industry, and the bioeconomy, rather than a financial burden for livestock breeders.

I will continue to support concrete measures that reduce bureaucracy, capitalize on local resources, and offer European farmers the chance to transform what is considered today a problem into an economic opportunity.

4-0272-0000.sourceText: The next item is the explanations of vote.

4-0274-0000.sourceText: Începem cu explicațiile privind Fezabilitatea celui de-al 28-lea regim de impozitare și potențialul său de sprijinire a competitivității UE.
4-0274-0000.englishText: We begin with the explanations regarding the feasibility of the 28th tax regime and its potential to support EU competitiveness.

4-0275-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, am votat împotriva raportului privind fezabilitatea celui de-al 28-lea regim de impozitare, deoarece nu cred că Uniunea Europeană are nevoie de încă un regim fiscal suprapus peste sistemele fiscale ale statelor membre. Sub pretextul simplificării pentru întreprinderi, acest raport deschide calea către o centralizare fiscală tot mai accentuată, care nu va face economia europeană mai competitivă. Realitatea este simplă: companiile europene nu cer noi reguli. Ele cel mai puțină birocrație, taxe mai mici și un cadru legislativ stabil și predictibil.

Nu lipsa unui nou regim fiscal împiedică investițiile, ci excesul de reglementare și povara administrativă, pe care UE continuă să le impună mediului de afaceri. Politica fiscală trebuie să rămână în competența statelor membre. Concurența fiscală loială stimulează investițiile, inovarea și dezvoltarea economică. Uniformizarea fiscală nu va face UE mai puternică, ci mai puțin flexibilă și mai puțin competitivă. Dacă vrem o Uniune capabilă să facă față competiției economice globale, trebuie să avem curajul să reducem birocrația, să diminuăm povara fiscală și să lăsăm statele membre să adopte politicile economice care răspund cel mai bine propriilor provocări.
4-0275-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, I voted against the report on the feasibility of the 28th tax regime because I do not believe the European Union needs yet another tax regime overlapping with the tax systems of the member states. Under the pretext of simplification for businesses, this report paves the way for increasingly accentuated fiscal centralization, which will not make the European economy more competitive. The reality is simple: European companies are not asking for new rules. They want less bureaucracy, lower taxes, and a stable and predictable legislative framework.

It is not the lack of a new tax regime that hinders investment, but the excess of regulation and the administrative burden that the EU continues to impose on the business environment. Fiscal policy must remain within the competence of member states. Fair tax competition stimulates investment, innovation, and economic development. Tax harmonization will not make the EU stronger, but less flexible and less competitive. If we want a Union capable of coping with global economic competition, we must have the courage to reduce bureaucracy, lessen the tax burden, and allow member states to adopt the economic policies that best respond to their own challenges.

4-0277-0000.sourceText: Următoarele explicații ale votului se referă la comunicarea comună privind ajutorul umanitar. Prima este domnul SIDL Günther.
4-0277-0000.englishText: The following explanations of vote refer to the joint communication on humanitarian aid. The first one is Mr. SIDL Günther.

4-0278-0000.sourceText:
Sehr geehrter Herr Präsident! Wir leben in einer Welt, in der das Völkerrecht immer weiter durch das Recht des Stärkeren ersetzt wird, in einer Welt, in der statt Politik und Diplomatie immer öfter die Waffen sprechen und in der inzwischen 239 Millionen Menschen auf humanitäre Hilfe angewiesen sind.

Da darf die Europäische Union nicht wegschauen, im Gegenteil: Die EU als größtes Friedensprojekt in der Geschichte hat hier eine besondere Aufgabe. Wir müssen helfen und daran arbeiten, die Welt wieder zu einem stabileren Ort zu machen, wo das Völkerrecht wieder mehr zählt als die Drohgebärden irgendwelcher Machthaber.

Deshalb unterstützte ich diese Entschließung, mit der sich unser gemeinsames Europa seiner globalen Verantwortung stellt.
4-0278-0000.englishText:
Mr President! We live in a world in which international law is increasingly being replaced by the law of the strongest, in which weapons speak more and more often instead of politics and diplomacy, and in which 239 million people are now dependent on humanitarian aid.

The European Union must not look away; on the contrary: the EU, as the greatest peace project in history, has a special task here. We must help and work to make the world a more stable place again, where international law counts for more than the posturing of any rulers.

That is why I support this resolution, with which our shared Europe faces up to its global responsibility.

4-0279-0000.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, maailma täytyy ottaa sellaisena kuin se on. On nimittäin niin, että me täällä Euroopassa emme ehkä aina muista aivan täysin, miten vaikeissa olosuhteissa monet maailman ihmisistä joutuvat elämäänsä rakentamaan ja selviytymään päivästä toiseen. Niinpä äänestin tarkistuksen kolmetoista puolesta, koska uskonnollisista ryhmistä kristityt, etenkin kristityksi kääntyvät, kokevat eniten vainoa maailmassa uskonnollisista ryhmistä ja unohdamme sen ehkä täällä aika helposti. Maailmassa on toki muitakin uskonnon takia vainottuja ryhmiä, kuten rohingyat Myanmarissa tai erilaiset vähemmistöuskonnot Pakistanissa ja osassa Intiaa.

Samoin äänestin tarkistuksen viisi puolesta, koska mielestäni EU:n on tehtävä voitavansa sen puolesta, että EU:n rahoittamat hankkeet ja humanitäärinen apu menevät todella perille sinne, minne niiden kuuluukin mennä, tapahtuivatpa nämä hirvittävät onnettomuudet, humanitäärinen hätä ja pula missä päin maailmaa tahansa.
4-0279-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the world must be taken as it is. The fact is that we here in Europe perhaps do not always fully remember in what difficult conditions many people around the world have to build their lives and survive from day to day. Therefore, I voted in favour of amendment 13, because of religious groups, Christians, especially converts to Christianity, experience the most persecution in the world among religious groups, and we perhaps forget that quite easily here. Of course, there are other groups in the world persecuted because of religion, such as the Rohingya in Myanmar or various minority religions in Pakistan and parts of India.

Similarly, I voted in favour of amendment 5, because in my view the EU must do its utmost to ensure that EU-funded projects and humanitarian aid really reach where they are supposed to go, no matter where in the world these horrific accidents, humanitarian emergencies and shortages take place.

4-0280-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, dear colleagues, especially after the recent USAID cuts, the European commitment to humanitarian aid has become crucial for millions of people across the world.

Conflicts, climate change and economic factors drive millions of people in various countries into utterly precarious situations. While we can go back to our safe homes at night, millions of people across the world do not have this privilege. Millions of people across the globe do not know if they will have a proper meal today, and many people across the globe have no access to basic necessities.

We must act now, and we must not leave the people in need alone. Even though I believe it is our human responsibility to help these people in need, I would like to say one thing to all the critics of humanitarian aid. We need to invest in humanitarian aid, not only because it's a human thing to do, but also for our own interests. If we do not invest properly where needed, we will face the consequences of our inaction in the form of mass migration, global health pandemics or detrimental economic impacts.

I thank all of my colleagues who have voted in favour, and I did too on this joint communication statement today.

And if I may ask one humanitarian favour from this Parliament before the summer: I would really love to also be able to get a coffee in the plenary after the summer break.

4-0281-0000.sourceText: Acest punct de pe ordinea de zi a fost închis.
4-0281-0000.englishText: This item on the agenda has been closed.

4-0285-0000.sourceText: Procesul verbal al acestei reuniuni va fi înaintat Parlamentului spre aprobare la începutul viitoarei sale reuniuni. Dacă nu există obiecții, voi transmite rezoluțiile adoptate în cadrul ședinței de azi persoanelor și organismelor menționate în rezoluții.
4-0285-0000.englishText: The minutes of this meeting will be submitted to Parliament for approval at the beginning of its next meeting. If there are no objections, I will forward the resolutions adopted during today's session to the persons and bodies mentioned in the resolutions.

4-0287-0000.sourceText: Următoarea perioadă de sesiune va avea loc între 14 și 17 septembrie 2026, la Strasbourg.
4-0287-0000.englishText: The next part-session will take place from 14 to 17 September 2026 in Strasbourg.

4-0289-0000.sourceText: I have the honour, even though the room is eerily empty, just to say thank you to the Members, to their assistants, to the staff of the European Parliament, to everyone involved – officials, interpreters, ushers, staff working in the restaurants and in the cafes, cleaning staff and everyone making the European Parliament what it is. Also, thank you to the public for watching us and holding us to account.

4-0292-0000.sourceText: Sesiunea Parlamentului European se suspendă. Ședința este închisă. O vară cât mai frumoasă!
4-0292-0000.englishText: The European Parliament session is suspended. The sitting is closed. Have a very nice summer!
